title: YOLOv11-based segmentation of vitiligo lesions using standardized clinical photography.
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework that automatically segments vitiligo lesions in standardized clinical photographs captured under controlled conditions, enabling reproducible lesion quantification across longitudinal visits. Methods Standardized photographs from 18 patients were acquired at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months under controlled imaging conditions, including fixed lighting, camera settings, and color calibration. Images underwent preprocessing involving resizing, color and illumination normalization, noise reduction, and geometric standardization. Expert dermatologists generated binary lesion masks that were used as ground truth for training a one-stage YOLOv11 segmentation model. Model performance was evaluated using patient-wise data splits and 5-fold cross-validation. Results The proposed model achieved 95 % accuracy, 92 % precision, 89 % recall, 90 % F1-score, with mAP@0.5 values of 0.878 (bounding box) and 0.892 (mask) from precision-recall analysis. Qualitative review indicated consistent segmentation quality across follow-up visits and moderate illumination variations, though formally stratified quantitative analysis by visit was not performed in this study. Visual assessment demonstrated close agreement between predicted and expert-annotated lesion boundaries, with minor under-segmentation observed mainly in low-contrast peripheral regions. Conclusions Standardized clinical photography combined with a YOLOv11-based segmentation framework enables reliable vitiligo lesion delineation and has potential for integration into quantitative disease monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.

Objectives

To develop and validate a YOLOv11-based deep learning framework that automatically segments vitiligo lesions in standardized clinical photographs captured under controlled conditions, enabling reproducible lesion quantification across longitudinal visits.

Methods

Standardized photographs from 18 patients were acquired at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months under controlled imaging conditions, including fixed lighting, camera settings, and color calibration. Images underwent preprocessing involving resizing, color and illumination normalization, noise reduction, and geometric standardization. Expert dermatologists generated binary lesion masks that were used as ground truth for training a one-stage YOLOv11 segmentation model. Model performance was evaluated using patient-wise data splits and 5-fold cross-validation.

Results

The proposed model achieved 95 % accuracy, 92 % precision, 89 % recall, 90 % F1-score, with mAP@0.5 values of 0.878 (bounding box) and 0.892 (mask) from precision-recall analysis. Qualitative review indicated consistent segmentation quality across follow-up visits and moderate illumination variations, though formally stratified quantitative analysis by visit was not performed in this study. Visual assessment demonstrated close agreement between predicted and expert-annotated lesion boundaries, with minor under-segmentation observed mainly in low-contrast peripheral regions.

Conclusions

Standardized clinical photography combined with a YOLOv11-based segmentation framework enables reliable vitiligo lesion delineation and has potential for integration into quantitative disease monitoring and clinical decision-support systems.

title: Cervical lymph node image analysis using YOLO11 segmentation model: an application and performance study.
abstract: Objectives Ultrasound assessment of superficial cervical lymph nodes is clinically valuable, yet current diagnostic methods are highly operator-dependent, with limited objectivity and consistency. This study investigates a more objective approach for analyzing lymph node ultrasound images, focusing on the stability and practical applicability of different model architectures on real-world clinical data. It aims to evaluate the utility of deep learning models for detection and segmentation of superficial lymph nodes and to provide a feasible methodology for objective lymph node ultrasound analysis. Methods Using real-world clinical data, a cervical lymph node ultrasound image dataset comprising 1,050 patients was constructed, with histopathological confirmation and standardized clinical-imaging follow-up (≥50 % diameter reduction over 6-9 months after treatment) serving as reference standards. Three different models - transformer-based RF-DETR, two-stage YOLO11+MedSAM, and end-to-end YOLO11-Seg - were systematically compared on detection and segmentation tasks within the same dataset. Results YOLO11-Seg demonstrated superior performance in both detection and segmentation. Under COCO evaluation metrics, it achieved an mean average precision (mAP) at 0.5 of 0.795 and an mAP at 0.5:0.95 of 0.558. Pixel-level segmentation evaluation yielded a Dice coefficient of 0.775 ± 0.15 and an IoU of 0.645 ± 0.15, with Precision and Recall values of 0.796 and 0.783, respectively. In contrast, the two-stage YOLO11+MedSAM and Transformer-based models exhibited lower accuracy and reduced consistency. Conclusions This study provides preliminary evidence for the application of deep learning-based methods in lymph node ultrasound analysis and suggests a potential technical framework for generating structured imaging data, which may support future computer-assisted assessment pending further validation.

title: Current findings, application, and diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder within the motor neuron disease (MND) spectrum, characterized by progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. The clinical phenotype ranges from pure motor syndromes to forms with cognitive and behavioral impairment, and the pathological burden extends beyond the motor system. Diagnosis remains primarily clinical, supported by electrophysiology and exclusion of mimics. Therefore, objective imaging biomarkers are urgently needed. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used as an auxiliary and differential diagnostic tool in ALS. T1- and T2-weighted imaging can assess cortical thickness, gray matter atrophy, and signal changes. Diffusion tensor imaging probes white matter microstructure. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy detects neurochemical alterations. Resting-state functional MRI assesses functional connectivity and network organization. Susceptibility-weighted imaging is sensitive to iron and calcium deposition. Ultra-high-field MRI provides higher resolution and improved metabolite quantification. This critical review summarizes current findings on MRI in ALS, but importantly organizes the evidence by the specific question being addressed: pathological/histological correlates, diagnostic or discriminatory performance, and clinical associations with phenotype, severity, progression, and prognosis. We also discuss major limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, limited standardization, small and clinically heterogeneous cohorts, frequent use of healthy rather than disease controls, and scarce multicenter validation. Although advanced MRI has revealed robust group-level alterations, none of these techniques has yet become established in routine clinical diagnosis of ALS. We, therefore, distinguish promising research findings from validated clinical biomarkers and outline priorities for future translation.

title: Revisiting the Role of Chemotherapy in Advanced Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Background Chemotherapy has been always considered scarcely or completely ineffective in the treatment of metastatic and progressive MTC. Case report We report the case of a 45-year-old man who underwent total thyroidectomy and lymphadenectomy in May 2023 for bilateral MTC with extrathyroidal extension and 2/23 metastatic lymph nodes. Germline and somatic RET genetic analysis were negative. From July 2023 to February 2024 tumour markers progressively increased and a 18F-DOPA PET/CT revealed metastases in the cervical region and mediastinal inlet. Therefore, cabozantinib was started, obtaining a partial response, but after 1 year of treatment disease progression at the cervicomediastinal level was documented, despite dosage increase. Thus, an off-label treatment with lenvatinib was started, achieving a transient stabilization. In October 2025, a further disease progression was diagnosed. The patient started off-label chemotherapy consisting of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 400 mg/m2 intravenous (IV) bolus, followed by 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 as a 48-hour infusion, combined with dacarbazine 800 mg/m2 IV in 30 minutes, every 14 days for the first month and then every 21 days for the following months. Chemotherapy was very well tolerated. At the last visit, after 17 cycles, tumour markers returned to the normal range (CA 19-9 22.9 kU/L, CEA 2.5 μg/L) and PET/CT scanning showed a complete response. Conclusion In conclusion, this case shows that, although treatment with multikinase inhibitors is actually the first choice for advanced RET-wild-type MTC, conventional chemotherapy can be effective at least in some patients and should always be considered, especially in case of failure of other approaches.

title: Association between medial meniscus extrusion and joint effusion persistence at 1 month in knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: [Purpose] Joint effusion is common in knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and contributes to functional limitations and disease progression. Persistence at 1 month is clinically relevant, as it may predispose patients to long-term effusion; however, the associated intra-articular lesions remain unclear. We aimed to identify intra-articular lesions associated with effusion persistence at 1 month using ultrasonography (US) for effusion quantification and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for lesion assessment. [Participants and Methods] This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients with medial compartment KOA and joint effusions. Joint effusion was quantified as the suprapatellar pouch distance (SPP-d) by US at baseline and 1 month. Baseline intra-articular lesions were graded using the MRI Osteoarthritis Knee Score. Participants were classified into persistent (SPP-d ≥4 mm) and non-persistent (SPP-d< 4 mm) effusion groups at 1 month. Binary logistic regression identified lesions independently associated with persistence. [Results] The persistent effusion group (n=40) showed a significantly higher medial meniscus extrusion (MME) score than the non-persistent effusion group (n=17) at baseline. In multivariable logistic regression, the MME score was independently associated with effusion persistence (odds ratio, 6.42; 95% confidence interval, 1.95-21.1). [Conclusions] MME is independently associated with joint effusion persistence at 1 month.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics for predicting pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.
abstract: Objective The aim of this study was to develop and validate machine learning models integrating clinical and pre-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging radiomic features for predicting pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 299 breast cancer patients from the publicly available Duke Breast Cancer magnetic resonance imaging dataset who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. From pre-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, 534 IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted. A five-method consensus feature selection pipeline retained 24 features. Notably, three prediction models were developed: clinical-only (Model A), radiomic-only (Model B), and combined clinical-radiomic (Model C). In total, seven machine learning algorithms were compared using 20 repeated five-fold stratified cross-validation with SMOTE applied within each training fold and assessed on a held-out test set (30%, n=90). Performance was evaluated using AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals, calibration (Brier score), and decision curve analysis. Results The pathologic complete response rate was 20.4% (61/299). The combined model (Gradient Boosting) achieved the highest test AUC of 0.723 (95%CI 0.595-0.835), with sensitivity of 0.333 and specificity of 0.833. DeLong tests revealed no statistically significant differences between model pairs (all p>0.05). Decision curve analysis demonstrated the highest net benefit for the combined model across 10-50% threshold probabilities. Conclusion The combined clinical-radiomic model demonstrated modest discriminative ability for pathologic complete response prediction. The limited sensitivity suggests potential utility as a rule-out test to identify patients unlikely to achieve pathologic complete response. These hypothesis-generating findings require external validation in independent multi-center cohorts.

title: Aptamer Interfaces for Serum-Based Gastric Cancer Detection: From Molecular Recognition to Clinical Decision
abstract: Gastric cancer is the fifth most commonly diagnosed malignancy and the fifth leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and it remains lethal chiefly because it is detected late. Endoscopic screening demonstrably works where it is deployed at scale, but endoscopy cannot be extended to the several hundred million people who would need it; a blood test that stratifies risk before endoscopy is therefore the only realistic route to population-level early detection. Aptamers-short, chemically synthesizable nucleic acid ligands-are attractive recognition elements for such a test, and more than a decade of work has produced hundreds of aptasensors that detect gastric cancer serum markers with impressive analytical sensitivity. Almost none has reached clinical use. Here we argue that this impasse is not a problem of affinity, nor of limit of detection, but of interface design. We resolve aptamer-based serum diagnostics into four coupled interfaces-molecular recognition, the serum matrix, signal transduction and clinical evidence-and show that each has been optimized locally while the constraints they impose jointly have been ignored. We then specify a reference architecture and a minimum evidence standard for a gastric cancer serum aptamer test, and identify the five measurements that would move the field from demonstration to deployment.

title: NeuroTürkNet: A Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Brain MRI Tumor Classification and Localization
abstract: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) presents challenges for computational tumor classification and localization because tumor appearance and surrounding anatomy vary across examinations. This work presents NeuroTürkNet, a two-stage prototype that combines a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) for four-category image classification with a YOLOv8n model for tumor-region localization. Input MRI images were resized to 640 × 640 pixels and processed using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) and bilateral filtering. The classification dataset comprised 3,264 publicly sourced images, and the localization dataset comprised 5,858 annotated images. The CNN was trained with Adam optimization, class weighting, and validation-based learning-rate scheduling; the YOLOv8n component was trained separately and applied to images classified as tumor-bearing. In the detailed test results reported for the classifier, accuracy was 90.84%, precision 90.87%, recall 90.84%, F1-score 90.80%, and ROC-AUC approximately 0.99. The localization component reported an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.81, a best mAP@50 of 0.88, and best precision of 0.85. A graphical prototype supports MRI upload, visualization of predicted regions, and PDF output. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed computational workflow on the datasets described, but they do not establish clinical diagnostic validity. Independent validation and a complete audit of dataset partitions are needed before medical deployment.

title: Beyond the Dedicated Suite: A Practical Review of Shared Imaging Platforms for Precision Interventional Pulmonology
abstract: Background: Advanced interventional pulmonology (IP) increasingly depends on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and hybrid imaging workflows for the diagnosis and management of intrapulmonary lesions. However, globally, many IP teams still lack a dedicated pulmonology procedure suite in their institution and instead perform cases in rooms originally designed for cardiovascular, neurovascular, interventional radiology, or surgical use. Methods: This review evaluates ceiling-mounted single-plane systems, floor-mounted systems, older and newer biplane angiography suites, robotic CBCT hybrid operating room systems and mobile CBCT systems and their suitability for IP procedures. Results: Based on available literature and institutional experience, ceiling-mounted single-plane systems may offer ergonomic advantages for bronchoscopic IP because they preserve head-side access and procedural ergonomics. Floor-mounted systems remained usable, particularly in older institutions, but could restrict airway-side positioning. Biplane-suite capabilities varied by system generation and configuration; some newer configurations provided CBCT and overlay functions that may facilitate pulmonary workflows. Robotic hybrid systems may provide broad procedural flexibility for complex and combined procedures but require greater institutional support. Mobile CBCT systems represented a practical entry strategy for centers without dedicated infrastructure, while conventional multidetector CT remained valuable for selected percutaneous interventions. Successful adaptation across all platforms depended on room layout, workstation capability, team familiarity, anesthesia support, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Conclusions: Advanced IP programs can be developed without a purpose-built pulmonology suite. Careful adaptation of existing imaging environments may allow centers to expand precision bronchoscopic and percutaneous capabilities according to local resources and workflow realities.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Longevity Research: From Molecular Clocks to Interventional Geroscience
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded the scale, resolution, and modalities through which biological aging can be estimated, but evidence that these estimates are valid intervention targets or surrogate endpoints remains limited. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed-indexed literature identified through documented PubMed and Consensus searches in October 2026, plus a separate search of primary US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) documents. No protocol was registered, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were not searched, and screening was by a single reviewer. We distinguish four biomarker properties: chronological-age estimation, prognostic association, responsiveness to intervention, and validated surrogacy. Deep-learning clocks across epigenomic, proteomic, retinal, electrocardiographic, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities report low chronological-age error, and several show prognostic associations with mortality, but calibration was rarely reported in the records reviewed and head-to-head comparisons with mortality-trained clocks in the same cohort were uncommon. Randomized trials show that responsiveness is clock-specific: in the CALERIE trial, caloric restriction slowed DunedinPACE but did not significantly change PhenoAge or GrimAge, and effect sizes were small. Machine learning has accelerated senolytic and mTOR-pathway candidate nomination, and a generative-AI-designed TNIK inhibitor reached phase 2a in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, an age-related disease indication rather than an aging indication. Coverage of the twelve hallmarks of aging by AI studies is uneven: epigenetic alteration and cellular senescence are best represented, whereas autophagy, proteostasis, genomic instability, and telomere attrition are thinly represented. Constraints include reliability, tissue specificity, confounding by ancestry and social factors, the gap between prediction and causation, and the absence, in the primary documents consulted, of a pathway that accepts a biological-age measure as a surrogate endpoint. We propose an evidence ladder and a translational chain for appraising AI-derived aging biomarkers and set out priorities for 2026-2030.

title: Uncertainty-Guided Dynamic Pseudo-Label Enhancement for Semi-Supervised Left Atrial Segmentation
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common atrial-origin arrhythmia. Left atrial image segmentation is critical for timely diagnosis and intervention. The traditional manual annotation is inefficient and inconsistent. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has thus become a practical way to alleviate the annotation bottleneck in medical imaging. Existing SSL segmentation methods still suffer from fixed confidence thresholds, accumulated pseudo-label noise, and insufficient local perturbations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a semi-supervised medical image segmentation method based on uncertainty-guided dynamic pseudo-label enhancement. This method dynamically adjusts the confidence threshold to better adapt to the dynamic characteristics of data distribution and feature changes. And it introduces an uncertainty-guided region mixing (UMIX) module, which uses prediction entropy to identify high uncertainty regions and achieves data enhancement through cross-sample feature replacement. UniMatch serves as the backbone, with strong and weak perturbations applied at both image and feature levels to enable more effective supervised learning and improve segmentation. The proposed method was compared against competing methods on two public datasets. Through comparative experiments with other methods on two public datasets, together with ablation studies, we validated the superior performance of the proposed method in image segmentation tasks and the effectiveness of its individual components.

title: Aptamer-Based Screening and Detection of Serum Biomarkers for Lung Cancer
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and most patients are still diagnosed after symptoms appear, when curative treatment is no longer possible. Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces mortality in high-risk smokers, yet uptake is low, eligibility criteria exclude the large never-smoker populations of East Asia, and false-positive findings generate downstream harm. A blood test that could triage who needs imaging, or rule out disease in indeterminate nodules, would therefore have substantial clinical value. Aptamers - short single-stranded oligonucleotides selected in vitro and produced by chemical synthesis - are attractive as the recognition layer of such a test because they can be generated against native membrane proteins and glycans, are thermostable and can be labelled site-specifically at low cost. Here we review the serum biomarker landscape in lung cancer, the chemistry that makes aptamers usable in serum, the selection strategies that now deliver picomolar binders within days, and the transduction architectures that convert binding into a clinical readout. We argue that analytical sensitivity is no longer the limiting factor: the field’s bottleneck has moved upstream to matrix-adapted affinity and downstream to prospective, blinded validation.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of CT Image Segmentation for Liver Cancer Screening Using Artificial Intelligence (1998--2026): A Review
abstract: Liver cancer is a global challenge, with increasing mortality rates. This article presents a detailed bibliometric analysis of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) methods to segment CT images and, subsequently, screen for liver cancer. We analyzed 2029 articles indexed in the recognized Scopus database, which covers the period between 1998 and 2026 (data collected on July 25, 2026), using a bibliometric analysis and visualization software called VOSviewer, in combination with complementary network analysis methods to explore co-occurrence networks, authors' scientific performance, and influence on citations. Major findings include the identification of researchers, research organizations, and countries contributing to the development of AI-based liver cancer screening techniques, with China, India, and the United States being the main contributors. Similarly, our study highlights the most influential publications and journals in this field, and also the accelerated increase in research output after 2019, mainly supported by deep learning algorithms. Five thematic clusters emerged from keyword co-occurrence analysis: clinical and radiomic evaluation, deep learning-based CT segmentation, quality imaging and contrast-enhanced imaging, neural networks, and AI applications in MRI-based oncology imaging. The analysis also highlights gaps in the existing and burgeoning literature for future investigations, most notably explainable AI, integration of multimodal imaging data, and testing in large-scale clinical settings.
authorString: Rebbane K, Senhaji S, Boukil N, El Ogri O, Khachchab MA, Berriche A.

title: Phase-Mixed Versus Phase-Specific Training for Pancreatic Lesion Segmentation on Contrast-Enhanced CT: A Non-Inferiority Study on PanTS
abstract: A model that segments pancreatic lesions from either arterial or portal venous CT could simplify deployment, provided that its performance is not inferior to that of phase-specific models. We evaluated nnU-Net ResEnc-M models trained on arterial scans (A), portal venous scans (P), or the combined dataset (M-full). Quality control, reconstruction of patient groups, and automatic phase assignment yielded 3,085 development scans and 438 held-out PanTS test scans. Five-fold cross-validation was repeated with three training seeds for A, P, and M-full; five reduced, phase-balanced training subsets were evaluated using seed 0. Non-inferiority required the lower confidence bound for the paired difference in lesion Dice to exceed −0.03. M-full met this criterion in both phases during cross-validation with all three seeds. On 85 lesion-positive portal test scans, its Dice advantage over P was 0.0387–0.0473, with all corresponding 95% confidence intervals above zero. M-full had fewer complete misses (17–19 versus 21–23 of 85), but more false-positive scans (34–39 versus 23–27 of 243 lesion-negative scans). Reducing the portal training subset lowered portal cross-validation performance in all five balanced variants. The arterial test contained only four positive scans and was therefore descriptive. Evaluation on 281 annotated Task07 scans was also descriptive because of known and unresolved dataset overlap. Mixed-phase training met the specified non-inferiority criterion while requiring only one CT volume at inference, but small-lesion misses and the false-positive trade-off remained.
authorString: Davydov R, Nefediev N, Staroverov N.

title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Medical Imaging, Radiotherapy, and Biophysical Modeling: Methods, Comparative Evidence, and Clinical Readiness
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) incorporates measurement operators, governing equations, simulated data, or mechanistic assumptions into learning. Despite encouraging biomedical demonstrations, performance against a numerical solver and physical plausibility alone do not establish trustworthy predictions or clinical benefit. This critical narrative review examines medical imaging, radiotherapy, and biophysical modeling through a unified assessment of prior fidelity, integration mechanism, fair comparators, quantitative endpoints, and evidence maturity. We distinguish physics-informed neural networks, learned surrogates, neural operators, and hybrid reconstruction pipelines; critically, we separate fundamental physical constraints from uncertain constitutive laws and phenomenological biological models. We summarize representative computational and patient-informed studies, including expanded evidence from radiation-dose modeling, and show why reported improvements in gamma agreement, segmentation, flow reconstruction, or speed cannot be pooled across distinct tasks. An original decision framework identifies when different physics-AI couplings are candidates for comparison. We introduce a proposed Physics Contribution Profile that separates predictive gain, physical validity, robustness, uncertainty calibration, and lifecycle cost; a diagnostic taxonomy of failure modes; and a reproducible, domain-specific benchmark and extraction protocol. A six-level evidence classification distinguishes numerical verification from patient outcomes. Principal limitations are model discrepancy, parameter non-identifiability, correlated simulation samples, and sparse prospective evaluation. The literature synthesis is non-exhaustive; the original database-screening records were unavailable, and the proposed benchmark has not been executed. The review proposes a testable agenda: compare matched data-only, mechanistic, and hybrid baselines; quantify conservation and uncertainty; and demonstrate transfer and clinical value independently of the simulator.
authorString: Ghaith M, Al Najjar A, Hussain M, Obaideen K, Taha Z, Al Anouti F.

title: Cost-Effectiveness, Budget Impact and Value of Information of Artificial-Intelligence-Supported Detection of Breast, Lung, Colorectal and Cervical Cancer in the Philippines: A Decision-Analytic Modelling Study
abstract: The economic value of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported cancer detection in the Philippines remains uncertain. This study evaluated opportunistic AI reading and AI-supported screening programmes for breast, lung, colorectal and cervical cancer from the public-payer perspective. A decision-analytic model integrated stage shift, precursor-lesion prevention, budget impact and value-of-information analyses using published inputs, 7% discounting and 10,000 probabilistic draws. At PHP 250 per read, opportunistic AI reading would avert approximately 270 deaths per annual cohort at a net cost of PHP 0.93 billion and PHP 628,000 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY). Only computer-aided colonoscopy approached the benchmark of one gross domestic product per capita (PHP 220,000 per QALY). Combined opportunistic reading met this benchmark at AI prices of PHP 50 or less. Increasing screening uptake from 1% to 20% would avert approximately 4750 deaths per annual cohort at PHP 14.0 billion annually, with a five-year budget impact of PHP 56 billion. Further research had greatest value for lung and breast screening programmes and opportunistic colonoscopy. Auto-contouring could expand annual radiotherapy capacity to 19,100–23,900 courses. Cost-effectiveness depends on software pricing, prevention benefits and affordable acquisition; conditional reimbursement should prioritise Philippine evidence on incremental detection and prevalence. AI-supported cancer detection offers substantial health gains but requires affordable implementation to achieve cost-effectiveness. This study identifies actionable pricing thresholds and research priorities to guide evidence-based reimbursement and equitable cancer screening in the Philippines.
authorString: Subong BJJ.

title: Magnetron-Sputtered TaCu and NbCu Coatings on 3D-Printed Titanium Implants: Implant Retention Following Staphylococcus aureus Challenge
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Periprosthetic infection remains a major challenge in orthopedic implantation, particularly for porous titanium implants that promote bone integration but may also facilitate bacterial colonization. This study evaluated magnetron-sputtered tantalum–copper (TaCu) and niobium–copper (NbCu) coatings on Ti6Al4V implants following Staphylococcus aureus challenge, with particular attention to implant geometry. Methods: TaCu-coated, NbCu-coated, and uncoated Ti6Al4V implants with dense (smooth) or porous (rough) geometries were evaluated. Cytocompatibility was assessed using rat mesenchymal stromal cells exposed to implant-conditioned media, and Cu release was measured by ICP-MS. Twenty-four rabbits received femoral implants followed by local S. aureus inoculation. Outcomes were assessed by clinical observation, macroscopic examination, radiography, and confocal microscopy. DAPI-positive structures were analyzed three-dimensionally using a 100 μm³ volume threshold and sensitivity analysis. Results: Neither TaCu- nor NbCu-conditioned media adversely affected MSC metabolic activity, and both coatings released measurable Cu. Despite infection across groups, TaCu-coated implants showed the greatest preservation of implant retention. Analysis of 6,248 segmented objects from 21 animals showed significant associations of coating and implant geometry with the proportion of small DAPI-positive objects (both p < 0.001). Uncoated Ti6Al4V showed higher proportions than NbCu and TaCu (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), whereas TaCu and NbCu did not differ (p = 0.731). Rough implants showed higher proportions than smooth implants, and the coating-related pattern persisted across thresholds of 25–200 μm³. An additional analysis using a 5 µm³ threshold confirmed differences in the relative proportions of very small DAPI-positive objects (p = 0.0156), whereas total volumetric object density did not differ significantly among coating groups (p = 0.769). Conclusions: Cu-containing coatings altered the distribution of implant-associated DAPI-positive structures without adversely affecting MSC metabolic activity. TaCu showed the greatest preservation of implant retention despite a confocal profile comparable to NbCu, supporting further investigation of TaCu for infection-resistant orthopedic implants.

title: Integrating Imaging and Clinical Information With Artificial Intelligence When Data Are Missing or Uncertain
abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence can integrate medical imaging with clinical information to support diagnosis and prognosis. However, inputs are frequently missing, acquired at different times, or inconsistent, reflecting clinical judgement, measurement limitations, or barriers to care. This Review critically examines approaches to using available inputs, reconstructing missing information, integrating sources according to reliability, and incorporating clinical knowledge. Particular attention is given to foundation and vision-language models, informative missingness, and the distinction between predictive confidence and demonstrated reliability. A proposed evidence-to-action framework connects information limitations and uncertainty to supporting a decision, obtaining further information, or deferring to expert assessment, illustrated through cardiovascular, ophthalmic, dental, and oncology applications. Evaluation must extend beyond predictive accuracy to calibration, equitable performance, deferral outcomes, workload, diagnostic delays, and patient benefit. The framework requires prospective validation across the complete care pathway. This includes assessing whether missing information disproportionately affects particular patient groups and their access to appropriate further assessment.
authorString: Pham TD.

title: Self-Supervised Pretraining Reduces Labeled Data Requirements for Whole-Brain Parcellation of Magnetic Resonance Images
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer disease are commonly studied with struc tural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in which whole-brain parcellation provides volu metric measures of brain structures. Atlas-based parcellation takes hours per subject, and deep learning models that accelerate it are limited by the cost of volumetric annotation. Self-supervised pretraining addresses this, but is usually demonstrated on large external unlabeled corpora that many laboratories do not have. We ask whether pretraining on the same modest cohort that supplies the labels helps, and at which annotation budgets. Using 148 T1-weighted volumes from OASIS-3 (one per participant, Clinical Dementia Rating 0–2) and 27 FreeSurfer-derived structures, a 3D U-Net was pretrained by masked-volume reconstruction on each cross-validation fold’s training split and fine-tuned with 10, 25, 50 and 104 labeled subjects. The gain from pretraining was largest when annotation was scarce: +0.0610 Dice at 25 labeled subjects against +0.0143 at 104. Under a corrected resampled t-test for dependent folds, it was significant at 25 (p = 0.005) and 10 (p = 0.039), but not at 50 or 104. With 25 labeled subjects, the pretrained model reached 95.7% of the Dice of a randomly initialized model trained on 104. Segmentation accuracy showed no detectable dependence on dementia severity once scanner model was accounted for, whereas scanner model had a large effect (Cohen’s d = 0.99 among cognitively normal participants), and the pretraining benefit did not vary detectably with severity. When annotation is the constraint, pretraining on the unlabeled cohort before annotating a fraction of it is the better use of effort.
authorString: Bagale A, Bakhati P, Kunwar B, Thapa A.

title: Prognostic Value of Imaging and Genomic Biomarkers in Systemic Therapy-Naïve Metastatic Androgen Pathway Modulator-Naïve Prostate Cancer Undergoing Radioligand Therapy
abstract: BACKGROUND: [177Lu]Lu-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radioligand therapy (RLT) has demonstrated clinical efficacy in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-naïve (mAPMN) and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), however treatment responses remain heterogeneous. PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic value of PSMA PET-derived imaging biomarkers and genomic alterations in relation to biochemical response and clinical outcomes in systemic therapy-naïve patients with mAPMN PCa receiving [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RLT as first-line systemic therapy. METHODS: Systemic therapy-naïve patients with mAPMN PCa treated exclusively with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-RLT were retrospectively analyzed. Standardized uptake value (SUV) parameters (SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVpeak) and PSMA total tumor volume (PSMA-TTV) were derived from baseline and post-treatment [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET scans, with imaging response defined as a ≥30% reduction. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, PSA-PFS and androgen deprivation therapy (ADT)-free survival were assessed. Available germline and somatic genomic alterations were analyzed for associations with outcomes. RESULTS: 26 patients were analyzed. Reductions ≥30% in SUVmax and PSMA-TTV were associated with prolonged PSA-PFS (27.1 vs. 9.4 months, p=0.01; 27.1 vs. 5.5 months, p< 0.001, respectively) and ADT-free survival (39.0 vs. 19.9 months, p=0.03; 23.9 vs. 13.8 months, p=0.028, respectively). In multivariable analysis, ΔPSMA-TTV ≥30% was independently associated with prolonged PSA-PFS (HR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.68; p=0.008). Of 17 genomically profiled patients, nine had somatic alterations, most frequently involving TP53, MYC, NF1. Patients with altered DNA damage repair (DDR) pathway had lower baseline PSA (0.78 vs. 12.3 ng/mL; p=0.03) and SUVpeak (7.9 vs. 16.7; p=0.03). No other associations with genetic alteration status were observed. CONCLUSIONS: In systemic therapy-naïve patients with mAPMN PCa, reductions of ≥30% in SUVmax and PSMA-TTV following PSMA-RLT were associated with favorable outcomes, with ΔPSMA-TTV independently associated with prolonged PSA-PFS. PSMA PET-derived parameters may support treatment response assessment, whereas no prognostic association with genomic alterations was identified in this cohort.

title: Diagnostic Performance of DWIBS for Lung Cancer Staging and Postoperative Recurrence Detection: An Exploratory Non-Inferiority Analysis Compared with PET-CT
abstract: Background: Diffusion-weighted whole-body imaging with background body signal suppression (DWIBS) is a radiation-free whole-body MRI technique that may provide an alternative to PET-CT for lung cancer evaluation. This study compared the diagnostic performance of DWIBS with that of PET-CT plus brain MRI for lung cancer staging and with PET-CT for postoperative recurrence detection. Methods: A total of 136 patients with lung cancer were evaluated. Clinical staging was assessed in 81 patients using DWIBS and PET-CT plus brain MRI. Postoperative recurrences were assessed in 55 patients, including 37 who underwent both DWIBS and PET-CT. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated. Paired differences in accuracy were evaluated using Newcombe's Method 10, and exploratory non-inferiority analyses were performed using margins of −5, −10, and −15 percentage points. Results: For clinical staging, DWIBS correctly classified 61 of 81 patients (75.3%), compared with 56 of 81 (69.1%) with PET-CT plus brain MRI. The observed difference in accuracy was +6.17 percentage points (95% CI, +0.30 to +12.27), supporting non-inferiority at all three margins. For postoperative recurrence detection, DWIBS demonstrated a sensitivity of 96.9%, specificity of 100.0%, and accuracy of 98.2%. Among the 37 patients who underwent both DWIBS and PET-CT, the accuracy was 100.0% for DWIBS and 91.9% for PET-CT. The observed difference was +8.11 percentage points (95% CI, −2.69 to +21.30), supporting non-inferiority at all three margins. Conclusions: DWIBS demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to PET-CT-based imaging for lung cancer staging and postoperative recurrence detection. DWIBS may represent a useful radiation-free alternative to PET-CT.

title: Treatment Exit in Aging Multiple Sclerosis: A Critical Review of Discontinuation, De-Escalation, and Dose Reduction, with Implications for GCC Practice
abstract: Background: Aging and prolonged disease stability prompt reassessment of multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapy. Discontinuation, switching, dose reduction and interval extension are distinct strategies. Stability during treatment may reflect reduced inflammatory activity, continuing drug effects, or both; chronological age alone cannot establish that withdrawal will preserve control. Objective: To critically assess treatment-exit evidence, reconcile apparently conflicting findings, distinguish treatment effects from prognostic associations, and examine implications for Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) practice. Approach: A targeted, web-assisted critical narrative review examined accessible primary studies, corrections, conference reports, trial registrations and regional documents through 1 November 2026. Comparisons considered population, mechanism, strategy, outcome, surveillance, residual exposure, restart and alignment of follow-up. No meta-analysis, independent duplicate screening or formal certainty grading was performed. Principal findings: In DISCOMS, new disease activity occurred in 12.2% of discontinuers versus 4.7% of continuers over two years: an absolute difference of 7.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 0.6–15.0); non-inferiority was not established. DOT-MS stopped early after significant inflammatory activity in 8/45 discontinuers versus 0/44 continuers. Differences in eligibility, MRI thresholds and follow-up prevent attribution of these findings to age alone. Selected older-adult cohorts report limited relapse activity, but disability and patient-reported outcomes remain less certain. Natalizumab and fingolimod cessation carry early reactivation concerns requiring explicit consideration of the subsequent treatment pathway. Anti-CD20 cessation studies show sustained suppression in some selected populations, although residual exposure, treatment selection and imprecision limit conclusions about durable treatment independence. The included evidence does not establish a reliable comparative reduction in serious infection following treatment exit. Lower-efficacy switching can increase recurrence, while findings for specified extended intervals cannot be generalized to arbitrary dose reductions. Kuwait supplies direct natalizumab interval-extension evidence in younger adults; other GCC cohorts mainly inform treatment context. Regional guidance offers practical criteria that require appraisal against primary evidence and local monitoring conditions. Conclusions: Treatment reassessment should compare specified alternatives with continuation, communicate relevant absolute outcomes and uncertainty, and distinguish estimated benefit–harm from regional applicability. An author-proposed framework organizes patient goals, reasons for change, inflammatory activity, disability trajectory, exposure, harms, observation and reassessment. Its accompanying minimum dataset supports prospective evaluation without assigning a risk score or universal stopping threshold. Neither the framework’s feasibility nor its clinical utility has been validated. Mechanism-specific comparative studies and coordinated GCC research should evaluate inflammatory recurrence, disability, serious infections, treatment burden and continuity of care. Such evaluation should distinguish elective reassessment from treatment interruptions caused by changing access arrangements.

title: Algorithm-based diagnosis and targeted epidural blood patch for spontaneous intracranial hypotension: a case report from a Vietnamese tertiary center
abstract: Abstract Background Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is an increasingly recognized disorder caused by spinal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. Although characteristic brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings may suggest the diagnosis, precise localization of the leak often requires advanced imaging techniques. Reports describing the application of contemporary SIH diagnostic algorithms in Southeast Asia remain limited. Case presentation A 40-year-old Japanese woman presented with severe orthostatic headache and vertigo after heavy lifting and excessive neck rotation. Brain MRI demonstrated diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement, venous sinus engorgement, and brain sagging, yielding a Bern SIH score of 7 and indicating a high probability of spinal CSF leakage. Whole-spine MRI revealed a spinal longitudinal epidural CSF collection extending from T1 to T12. Based on the positive SLEC pattern, prone dynamic CT myelography was performed and identified a thoracic ventral dural tear at the T2 level. Targeted epidural blood patching was subsequently performed using 4 mL of autologous blood. Follow-up MRI demonstrated marked reduction of the epidural fluid collection and re-expansion of the thecal sac. The patient experienced gradual clinical improvement and was discharged with significant symptom relief. Conclusions This case illustrates the clinical value of a structured multimodality imaging approach for SIH, integrating the Bern SIH score, whole-spine MRI, and dynamic CT myelography to guide targeted treatment. Accurate leak localization enabled successful targeted epidural blood patching and favorable clinical recovery. Furthermore, this report demonstrates the feasibility of implementing advanced SIH diagnostic and interventional techniques in a Vietnamese tertiary-care hospital.

title: Histopathological alterations of deep cervical lymph nodes in Alzheimer's disease and their association with cognitive decline
abstract: Abstract Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive and functional decline with amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathology. In addition to abnormal protein aggregation, impaired clearance of brain-derived solutes through glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic pathways may contribute to disease progression. Deep cervical lymph nodes (DCLNs), as major downstream lymphoid structures of central nervous system drainage, may provide a peripheral histological window into the brain-cervical lymphatic axis. However, whether human DCLNs undergo histopathological remodeling in AD and whether such changes are clinically relevant remain unclear. Methods DCLNs were obtained from 66 participants, including 59 patients with moderate-to-severe AD and 7 cognitively unimpaired controls. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was used to assess lymph node morphology and germinal center (GC) abundance. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to evaluate Aβ, tau, alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA), CD31, and LYVE-1. Reduced GC abundance is associated with greater clinical impairment, fibrosis-related remodeling, and poorer 6-month postoperative improvement, suggesting that DCLN histopathology may have potential clinical and prognostic relevance in AD.

title: Teleophthalmology for preventable blindness screening in semi-urban primary care: a cost-effectiveness study from Brazil
abstract: Abstract Background Visual impairment from preventable causes remains a critical public health challenge in Brazil, where over 34% of the population has never undergone ophthalmic examination and specialist access is severely maldistributed. Diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, and cataract are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet systematic screening in primary care remains rare in semi-urban municipalities. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a teleophthalmology-based active screening pathway versus the standard Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) passive referral pathway, assessed acceptability among professionals and patients, and estimated quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained through early detection. Methods A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted across eight Primary Health Care Units in a semi-urban municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil (October 2025–March 2026). A total of 1,290 patients aged 50 years or older and/or with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were screened using a portable non-mydriatic fundus camera with remote specialist reporting assisted by artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation. A two-arm decision tree compared intervention costs (bottom-up micro-costing) against standard pathway costs (SIGTAP 2024/SISREG 2024) from the public payer perspective. The primary effectiveness measure was time to diagnosis. A QALY scenario analysis was performed using Brazilian-validated utility coefficients. Acceptability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUScale; n = 13 professionals) and the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire – Brazil (TUQ-Brazil; n = 99 patients). Results Of 1,290 patients, 41.79% had abnormal findings and 2.32% had ungradable images. Mean time to diagnosis was 1.26 days versus 83 days via standard referral. Cost per detected case was R$50.64 versus R$70.82, a reduction of 28.5%. Teleophthalmology was absolutely dominant across all sensitivity scenarios. A QALY analysis (n = 376) yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of –R$4,330/QALY, well below the SUS threshold (~ R$132,000/QALY). Professionals rated the platform 90.96 ± 5.91 (SUScale; “Excellent”). Patients reported a mean TUQ-Brazil score of 6.61 ± 0.32 out of 7.00, with 93.9% willing to reuse the service. Conclusions Teleophthalmology demonstrated absolute dominance over standard SUS referral in both cost-effectiveness and QALY analyses, delivering earlier diagnosis at lower cost. High bilateral acceptability supports scalability within the SUS, and these findings offer actionable evidence for policymakers considering portable fundus camera integration into semi-urban primary care networks.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: 3D Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation in MRI with Attention U-Net and Voxel-Level Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke is a major cause of death and disability around the world, and accurate segmentation of stroke lesions from MRI diagnosis are critical for treatment planning and clinical decision making. Compared to traditional methods, while deep learning has advanced automated stroke segmentation, but existing approaches predict single binary masks with no estimate of prediction confidence, a crucial limitation since clinical usage would require knowledge on where the model can be trusted just as much as the prediction itself. We propose a reliability-aware 3D framework combining an Attention U-Net with Monte Carlo Dropout inference and an optimized decision threshold, tested on the ISLES 2022 benchmark (240 multi-center DWI + ADC cases; 168/36/36 split). At inference, T = 20 stochastic forward passes generate both a segmentation mask and a voxel-level uncertainty map. This work achieved a Dice of 0.6816 (IoU = 0.5526, Precision = 0.8764 and Recall = 0.6595) for single-model volumetric methods on this benchmark dataset, meanwhile boiling Monte Carlo Dropout increased Recall by + 2.65% at the zero-training cost. Uncertainty maps were semantically aligned but spatially localized to the edges of lesions, highly correlated with segmentation errors, and inversely associated with lesion size automatically marking small and difficult lesions as cases of high uncertainty.

title: Portable Spectrophotometric Olive Oil Quality Analysis System Integrated with Oxidative Stress-State Modeling
abstract: Abstract Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. Conventional reference techniques such as gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and standardized wet-chemistry assays remain essential for confirmatory analysis, yet their cost, infrastructure needs, and sample-processing demands limit continuous use at farms, mills, warehouses, and retail inspection points. Here we present a full research framework for a portable spectrophotometric olive oil quality analysis system that integrates ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, near-infrared spectroscopy, chemometric calibration, edge-machine-learning classification, and oxidative stress-state modeling. The system is designed to quantify quality indicators such as free acidity, peroxide value, conjugated diene/triene absorbance, phenolic depletion, pigment degradation, and adulteration-associated spectral deviation without relying on destructive laboratory workflows. The research develops the platform as an analytical chemistry and embedded diagnostic system rather than as a simple consumer sensor. The designed instrument combines controlled optical illumination, wavelength-resolved detection, temperature-compensated sample handling, onboard preprocessing, encrypted data storage, and cloud-supported model governance. The biochemical model links spectral behavior to triglyceride structure, oleic-linoleic acid balance, phenolic antioxidant buffering, radical propagation, hydroperoxide accumulation, aldehyde formation, and the degradation of chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments during light or heat exposure. The computational model couples standard normal variate correction, derivative spectroscopy, principal component analysis, partial least squares regression, support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting, and uncertainty-aware edge inference. A validation strategy is applied using authenticated extra virgin, virgin, refined, and pomace oils; controlled adulteration series with sunflower, soybean, canola, palm, and refined olive oils; and accelerated storage experiments under oxygen, heat, and light stress. Expected outputs include rapid screening of authenticity, estimation of regulatory quality parameters, early detection of oxidative instability, and generation of traceable reports for producers, inspectors, and supply-chain actors. The framework is aligned with international olive oil quality concepts while emphasizing that portable spectroscopy is best positioned as a high-throughput screening and decision-support layer rather than a replacement for legal confirmatory testing.

title: Hybrid U-Net Model with Transformer-Enhanced Skip Connections for Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Laparoscopic Images
abstract: Abstract The organ Segmentation in surgical images plays a crucial role in computer-assisted diagnosis and robotic surgeries, yet it faces challenges like class imbalance, occlusions, and computational constraints. In order to overcome these challenges, we propose an architecture which uses asymmetric multi-scale transformer along with the attention-gated skip connections in U-Net Model to efficiently segment abdominal organs. Our proposed architecture allows efficient extraction of local features and modelling of global contexts. We also propose a hybrid loss function by combining Lovasz-Softmax loss and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss, which helps in overcoming class imbalance in the training process and improving performance on the minor classes. Our proposed method attains a mean precision of 0.9667, mean recall of 0.9432, mean dice of 0.9522, mean IoU of 0.9150, and mean HD95 of 0.4704 on all 13 classes of the CholecSeg8k dataset, which makes it better than the state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Dynamic digital radiography–derived low signal area ratio for assessing emphysema and associated pulmonary vascular changes in COPD
abstract: Abstract Emphysema in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) destroys alveolar walls together with the alveolar capillary bed, yet unenhanced computed tomography (CT) quantifies parenchymal change rather than perfusion. Dynamic digital radiography (DDR) generates perfusion-related maps from cardiac-synchronised changes in radiographic lung density without contrast material. In 40 prospectively enrolled patients with clinically stable COPD who underwent breath-hold DDR, inspiratory high-resolution CT and pulmonary function testing, we quantified a low signal area (LSA) ratio by histogram-based segmentation of DDR perfusion maps. The LSA ratio correlated with the percentage low attenuation volume at CT ( r s = 0.692), forced expiratory volume in 1 s ( r s = − 0.553) and diffusing capacity ( r s = − 0.436). Absolute pulmonary vessel volume showed no association with the LSA ratio, whereas vessel volume normalised to lung volume did ( r s = − 0.556); this association persisted after adjustment for emphysema extent (partial r = − 0.324) and for lung volume (partial r = − 0.517), although its confidence interval approached zero. When both CT measures were considered simultaneously, the LSA ratio was more strongly related to emphysema extent than to vessel volume. The LSA ratio therefore reflects emphysematous destruction predominantly, with an additional pulmonary vascular component that requires confirmation.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Nomogram for Risk Stratification of Anxiety in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Objective Anxiety, a common and disabling non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), highlights the clinical importance of early identification of PD with anxiety (PDA). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an nomogram that integrates routine clinical indicators and structural MRI radiomic features for early PDA risk stratification. Methods 139 PD patients were retrospectively enrolled and split into training (n = 97) and internal test (n = 42) sets at a 7:3 ratio. 21 clinical variables were collected, and 584 quantitative morphological features were extracted. Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman collinearity elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used to select optimal imaging metrics to calculate a radiomics signature. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified independent clinical predictors. A clinical prediction model and an integrated clinical–radiomics nomogram were constructed, and assessed in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1-score, receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Elevated UPDRS-III score, cognitive impairment, higher levodopa-benserazide dosage, and 12 MRI features were independent PDA predictors. The combined nomogram outperformed the clinical-only model, achieving an AUC of 0.99, accuracy of 0.93, sensitivity of 1.00, specificity of 0.91 in the test set. Calibration curves confirmed favorable consistency between predicted and actual anxiety risk, while DCA demonstrated sustained net clinical benefit of the integrated nomogram across wide threshold ranges. Conclusion The visualizable clinical-radiomics nomogram enables accurate individualized PDA risk prediction. This non-invasive, bedside-accessible tool assists neurologists in early screening and stratified management of PDA.

title: Thermo-regulatory response of static and dynamic breast thermography as a biomarker of malignancy
abstract: Abstract This study assesses the diagnostic potential of static and dynamic infrared thermography by relating physiological vascular patterns to established indicators of breast malignancy. Mammography remains the principal global screening modality; however, its accuracy declines in women with dense breast tissue [1], and its high cost limits access in developing countries [2]. Although dynamic thermal imaging may improve lesion detection, its clinical implementation in developing settings is constrained by the opacity of artificial intelligence models and the limited availability of high-quality datasets [3]. This paper presents a physiology-based model intended to reduce reliance on extensive training data and thereby facilitate analysis in small patient cohorts. Earlier Virtual Wave Transformation approaches appear to capture dynamic thermal responses but struggle to differentiate metabolic heat from vascular signals. The present study combines dynamic thermal imaging with static infrared imaging. By exploiting the different temporal behaviors of these signals, the model may distinguish increased cancer-related metabolic activity from other thermal patterns. In contrast to black-box deep-learning systems and even explainable AI approaches, this algorithm provides a more interpretable mathematical alternative by decomposing thermal patterns and separating convective vascular heat transport from thermal conductive metabolic signals. Analysis of the temporal variation in each component's amplitude indicates a possible association with patient diagnosis. Whereas conventional AI methods generally require large databases and expensive clinical validation, such as MRI, this approach uses physiological parameters to obtain diagnostic information from smaller samples. This work is a limited pilot study focused on evaluating the mathematical methods; we did not perform detailed statistical analysis.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. title: Multiparametric CEST MRI–Guided Intranasal Theranostic Liposomes for Quantitative Biodistribution and Response Prediction in Glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) treatment is limited by the blood-brain-barrier(BBB) and lack of non-invasive methods to track drug delivery and therapeutic response simultaneously. We developed a theranostic strategy utilizing multiparametric chemical exchange saturation transfer(CEST) MRI to guide the nose-to-brain delivery of mucus-penetrating liposomes encapsulating gemcitabine and iohexol(1:1; Gem/Ioh-Lipo). These multiple CEST contrast indicated drug-specific signals (gemcitabine 2.4 ppm, iohexol 4.3 ppm and liposome − 3.5 ppm), demonstrating that > 70% intranasal dose reached the frontal cortex from the olfactory bulb.Importantly, CEST at 4.3 ppm strongly correlated with tumor response(R² > 0.9), indicating the prognostic value of image-guidance. Another CEST contrast (APTw at 3.5 ppm) indicated the tumor response, intranasal Gem/Ioh-Lipo produced an 8.6-fold tumor volume reduction versus drug-free liposomes (P < 0.0001). Controls showed a 55.9% increase in APTw signal in tumor (P < 0.005), indicating increased cellularity and proliferating cells, which were absent in treated animals. This CEST MRI-guided theranostic strategy enables non-invasive, real-time quantification of drug biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy for GBM, enabling precise treatment evaluation.

title: Machine learning implementation for host-based infectious disease diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Host-based diagnostics coupled with machine learning may support faster discrimination of infectious states and reduce unnecessary antimicrobial treatment. We reviewed recent studies that applied machine-learning methods to clinical patient data for pathogen detection, infection classification, or closely related host-response diagnosis. Eligible infection targets included bacterial and viral infections, bacterial-versus-viral classification, and syndrome-based presentations such as sepsis. Malaria was included when evaluated within a mixed febrile cohort. Searches were conducted of four literature databases spanning January 2020 through August 2025. Of 144 retrieved records, 51 passed an initial host-diagnostics screen and 21 articles met the final eligibility criteria. The included articles covered structured clinical variables, gene or molecular-expression measurements, medical imaging, physiological signals, and microscopy. For the quantitative model-class comparison, we extracted 54 evaluations belonging to four machine-learning classes: random forest (23), neural network (17), support vector machine (9), and logistic regression (5). Less frequently evaluated approaches, including gradient boosting, decision trees, naive Bayes, and k-nearest neighbors, were summarized descriptively. Model performance could not be compared directly because input modalities, cohort composition, preprocessing, validation strategies, hyperparameter selection, and reported endpoints varied substantially. Accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were the dominant performance measures. Among the 54 focal-class evaluations, 14 reported accuracy alone, 20 reported AUC alone, and 20 reported both. Only 16 evaluations reported additional measures such as sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, or Matthews correlation coefficient. Imaging studies generally favored neural-network approaches, whereas molecular-expression studies frequently used random forests. However, the evidence did not support a universally optimal model.

title: Screening of Bacillus bacterial strains with capability of degrading T-2 toxin
abstract: Abstract T-2 toxin (T-2) is a toxic fungal metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species that are known to contaminate food products worldwide, posing serious risks to public health and the economy. Effective control of this toxin is therefore a key objective in food safety. Recent efforts to manage T-2 contamination have focused on utilizing microbes, especially bacterial species from the Bacillus genus, as promising toxin degraders. This study evaluated the in vitro capacity of ten Bacillus strains (BC1–10) in degrading T-2. Three out of ten strains demonstrated T-2 degradation activity, with complete toxin removal achieved within 96 hours under standard culture condition. The major biotransformation product of T-2 was isolated by high-performance liquid chromatography and structurally characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy as HT-2 toxin. Toxicity assessment in kidney-derived HEK293T cells showed that HT-2 was less toxic than T-2, with EC 50 values of 12.8 and 1.8 nM, respectively. The findings supported the potential application of selected Bacillus strains as functional microbial additives to mitigate T-2 contamination and toxicity.

title: Characterizing the Spatiotemporal Boundaries of Functional Ultrasound for Brain Decoding
abstract: Abstract Functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) measures task-associated changes in cerebral blood volume (CBV) with fine spatial sampling and rapid acquisition, supporting functional mapping and brain-signal decoding. As an indirect measure of neural activity, fUS-CBV signals are shaped by neurovascular coupling and vascular dynamics, which influence the spatial and temporal stimulus information available for decoding. Consequently, the functional distinctions accessible in fUS-CBV signals require characterization under controlled experimental conditions. Here, controlled whisker stimulation in awake, head-fixed mice was used to characterize these decoding-relevant response properties. Whisker identity and number, stimulation duration, and inter-stimulus interval were systematically varied. All-whisker stimulation produced contralaterally dominant responses in the primary somatosensory barrel field and ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus. Different whisker inputs were associated with distinguishable cortical response distributions, while stimulation involving more whiskers produced broader representative activation patterns. Across durations of 0.5–10 s, brief stimulation generated measurable stimulus-associated signals, and response magnitude, persistence, and spatial distribution varied with stimulus duration. For paired 2-s stimuli, trial-level separability was already high at the shortest tested 1-s gap, corresponding to a 3-s onset-to-onset spacing, and reached 100% at gaps of 3 s or longer. Building on the experimentally characterized spatiotemporal response properties of fUS-CBV signals, a proof-of-concept modeling and decoding framework was developed, comprising cross-animal spatial prediction, classification of short versus long stimulation from S1BF ΔCBV time courses with known stimulus onset, and modeling of paired-event separability. Together, the results show that fUS-CBV signals retain structured spatial and temporal information about controlled sensory input after neurovascular transformation. These measured response properties characterize the spatiotemporal boundaries within which neural activity can be reliably distinguished using fUS-CBV signals, providing constraints for the development of fUS-based decoding models and the design of stimulation paradigms suitable for reliable fUS decoding.

title: Effects of a Ciprofol-Etomidate Mixture on Intraoperative Hypoxemia and Hypotension in Older Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Under Sedation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a 1:1 ciprofol-etomidate mixture for sedation during combined gastrointestinal endoscopy in older patients and to provide evidence for optimizing clinical sedation strategies. Methods This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 203 patients aged 60–80 years who were scheduled to undergo combined gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either ciprofol alone (Group C, n = 101) or a ciprofol-etomidate mixture (Group CE, n = 102). Patients in Group C received intravenous ciprofol at a dose of 0.3 mg/kg, whereas those in Group CE received a slow intravenous injection of a ciprofol-etomidate mixture comprising ciprofol 0.15 mg/kg and etomidate 0.12 mg/kg over 1 min. The primary outcome was the composite incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxemia. Secondary outcomes included adverse events, sedation onset time, first-dose sedation success rate, recovery time, and satisfaction scores reported by patients, anesthesiologists, and endoscopists. Results The incidence of the composite outcome of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxemia was significantly lower in Group CE than in Group C (P < 0.05). Group CE also had significantly lower incidences of hypotension (21.2% vs. 42.3%) and vasopressor use (15.4% vs. 34.6%) (both P = 0.001). Sedation onset was significantly faster in Group CE than in Group C (61.0 ± 6.1 s vs. 71.1 ± 14.4 s), the first-dose sedation success rate was higher (97.1% vs. 89.4%), and recovery time was shorter (18.3 ± 3.8 min vs. 19.6 ± 4.2 min) (all P < 0.05). The incidences of myoclonus and injection pain did not differ significantly between the groups ( P > 0.05). Anesthesiologist satisfaction was significantly higher in Group CE than in Group C (P < 0.001), whereas patient and endoscopist satisfaction scores were comparable between the groups. Conclusion A 1:1 ciprofol-etomidate mixture improves hemodynamic stability, accelerates sedation onset, and increases the first-dose sedation success rate in older patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation, without increasing adverse events. This regimen may enhance the efficiency of anesthesia management and represents a potentially useful clinical sedation strategy. Trial registration The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500103032, https//www.chictr.org.cn/)on 23/05/2025.

title: Development of a Deep Learning Model Integrating Computed Tomography Images and Blood Data for the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis
abstract: Abstract Background In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model for the diagnosis of acute cholecystitis (AC) using non-contrast CT images and clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 197 patients (100 AC, 97 non-AC) treated between January 2016 and December 2025 at a single center. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 139) and test (n = 58) datasets. Three models were constructed: an imaging-based deep learning model, a clinical data-based machine learning model, and a hybrid machine learning model integrating deep learning-derived imaging features with clinical data. CT images were preprocessed, and gallbladder regions were segmented. Clinical variables included white blood cell counts and levels of C-reactive protein and liver function markers. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Statistical comparisons were performed using Welch's t-test and Chi-square test. Results The imaging-based model achieved accuracy 0.741, precision 0.703, recall 0.867, specificity 0.607, F1 score 0.776, and AUC 0.863. The blood-based model achieved accuracy 0.914, precision 0.931, recall 0.900, specificity 0.929, F1 score 0.915, and AUC 0.946. The hybrid model showed the highest performance, with accuracy 0.931, precision 0.882, recall 1.000, specificity 0.857, F1 score 0.938, and AUC 0.996. Conclusions A hybrid model integrating CT imaging and clinical data improved diagnostic performance for AC compared with single-modality models.
