title: An Interpretable Multimodal Machine Learning Model for Predicting Early Hematoma Progression in Bifrontal Cerebral Contusion
abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a risk prediction model for early hematoma progression (HP) in patients with bifrontal cerebral contusions, systematically compare the performance of multiple machine learning algorithms, identify an optimal model with robustness, generalizability, and clinical interpretability, and determine the key factors driving HP. Methods This dual-center retrospective study included 1,100 adult patients with radiologically confirmed bifrontal cerebral contusions. The modeling cohort comprised 454 patients from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University and was randomly divided into a training set of 318 patients and an internal validation set of 136 patients. An independent cohort of 646 patients from the Second Affiliated Hospital of the University of South China was used for external validation. Demographic characteristics, vital signs, laboratory indicators, and cranial computed tomography features were collected, with HP defined as the outcome. To minimize information leakage, preprocessing, feature selection, model fitting, and hyperparameter optimization were conducted exclusively within the training set. A two-stage feature-selection strategy combining random forest importance ranking and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to identify the core predictors, which were subsequently applied unchanged to the internal and external validation cohorts. Thirteen machine learning models were developed, and their discrimination, classification performance, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated. Shapley Additive Explanations were used to characterize global and patient-level contributions of the predictors to the selected model. Results The intersection of features selected by RF and Lasso yielded 10 stable core predictors: time to baseline CT, ventricular compression, sulcal effacement, hematoma density coefficient of variation (Hematoma.DCV), heart rate, white blood cell count, eosinophil count, albumin, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI). Among the 13 models, LightGBM achieved the highest apparent training-set AUC of 0.872 but decreased to 0.652 in the internal validation set, a pattern consistent with limited generalizability and possible overfitting. In contrast, Lasso achieved the numerically highest AUC in the internal validation set, with an AUC of 0.764 (95% CI: 0.677–0.852). In the external cohort, its AUC decreased to 0.694 but remained numerically higher than those of the other models displayed in the external ROC analysis. Because formal pairwise statistical comparisons were not available, these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating the statistical superiority of Lasso over the other models. External decision curve analysis indicated potential net benefit mainly at low threshold probabilities, whereas calibration was suboptimal (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ²=33.87, P < 0.001; Brier score = 0.2405), with a tendency to underestimate observed HP risk. SHAP analysis indicated that Hematoma.DCV, time to baseline CT, MLR, sulcal effacement, PNI, heart rate, and ventricular compression were the main drivers of model prediction. Conclusion In patients with bifrontal cerebral contusions, the Lasso model showed comparatively stable discrimination and greater structural interpretability than the higher-capacity ensemble models. However, external discrimination was modest, calibration was inadequate, and clinical net benefit was mainly confined to low threshold probabilities. Hematoma density heterogeneity, the timing of baseline CT, systemic inflammatory–immune–nutritional status, and local intracranial compression signs contributed importantly to model predictions. The model should currently be regarded as a supplementary risk-ranking approach rather than a stand-alone screening tool or a source of directly actionable absolute-risk estimates. External recalibration and larger multicenter prospective validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: CBCT-based three-dimensional morphometric analysis of the upper airway and its influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients across different bone ages
abstract: Abstract Objective Previous studies have largely treated skeletal Class II patients as a homogeneous group for overall analysis, without fully accounting for subgroup differences in vertical facial patterns or variations in developmental timing. Consequently, a systematic understanding of the associations between upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacial morphology remains insufficient, which limits the formulation of precise clinical intervention strategies. This study aims to analyze the three-dimensional morphological changes of the upper airway and their associated influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients, stratified by cervical vertebral bone age staging, so as to provide evidence for the development of stage-specific orthodontic treatment strategies. Methods A total of 205 skeletal Class II average-angle patients were enrolled and divided into four groups (T1–T4) according to cervical vertebral bone age staging. Upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacialparameters were assessed using cone-beam CT (CBCT) three-dimensional reconstruction combined with Dolphin and WinCeph software. Inter-group comparisons were conducted using analysis of variance (ANOVA). Spearman correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were used to identify independent predictors of upper airway morphology. Results In females, total upper airway volume and nasopharyngeal volume increased significantly at stages T2 and T4, whereas palatopharyngeal and laryngopharyngeal volumes showed significant increased only at stage T4 ( P < 0.05). In males, significant volumetric increments across all airway segments were observed predominantly at stages T3 and T4 ( P < 0.05). Multiple regression analysis revealed that in females, the positive predictors of total upper airway volume included bone age stages T2 and T4, Mx'-Mx, H-RGn, and H-CVP. In males, the positive predictors comprised bone age stage T3, H-RGn, and H-CVP. Conclusion Upper airway volume in skeletal Class II average-angle patients exhibits a sex-dimorphic developmental pattern across bone age stages. Females display a biphasic growth pattern with leap-like increases at T2 and T4, whereas males demonstrate a steady and pronounced growth spurt from T3 to T4. title: Analysis of Influencing Factors and Development of a Clinical Prediction Model for Postoperative Visual Improvement Prognosis in Patients with Age-Related Cataract
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To identify independent factors associated with postoperative visual improvement after phacoemulsification combined with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in patients with age-related cataract (ARC) and to develop an interpretable individualized clinical prediction nomogram for preoperative risk stratification. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 1,847 eyes with ARC who underwent phacoemulsification combined with IOL implantation. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors associated with postoperative visual improvement. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling with 1,000 iterations. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) value analysis. Results: Age, severity of preoperative visual impairment, fundus lesions, axial length, and keratometric value (K-value) were identified as independent predictors of postoperative visual improvement. The prediction model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78–0.89) in the training cohort and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.70–0.86) in the validation cohort. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis revealed that age contributed most significantly to the model prediction. A visual nomogram was subsequently developed to provide individualized risk estimation. Conclusion: The nomogram incorporating five independent predictors demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability for predicting postoperative visual improvement in patients with ARC. This model may serve as a practical tool for preoperative risk assessment, individualized patient counseling, and doctor–patient communication.

title: Complex Müllerian Duct Anomaly Presenting as a Rare OHVIRA Variant: Clinical and Surgical Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Background Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, also referred to as Herlyn–Werner–Wunderlich syndrome, is an uncommon congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract characterized by uterine malformations, an obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal agenesis. Atypical variants add further complexity, often posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 14-year-old girl presenting with primary amenorrhea and cyclical abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a bicornuate unicollis uterus with hematometrocolpos, absent left kidney, and a grossly dilated ectopic right ureter. Intraoperatively, the cervix was rudimentary and hypoplastic, precluding fertility preservation. A complete hysterectomy with right ureteric reimplantation was performed using the Politano–Leadbetter technique. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient experienced complete resolution of symptoms at follow-up. Discussion This case demonstrates an atypical variant of Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, characterized by bicornuate uterus, rudimentary cervix, segmental vaginal atresia, unilateral renal agenesis, and ureteric malpositioning. Such complex anomalies underscore the limitations of current classification systems and emphasize the importance of detailed anatomical description. Magnetic resonance imaging remains the diagnostic gold standard, while multidisciplinary planning is crucial for tailoring management to individual patients. When reconstructive options are not feasible, definitive surgical intervention is often required to achieve symptom relief and prevent long-term morbidity. Conclusion Atypical variants of OHVIRA syndrome underscore the importance of integrating embryological understanding, systematic renal screening, and collaborative surgical planning. Early recognition and tailored intervention are critical to achieving symptom relief and preventing long-term morbidity.

title: Evaluating Boundary-Aware Losses for U-KAN on BraTS 2023 Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Background:: Boundary-aware loss functions are intended to improve segmentation by penalizing spatial errors that may be insufficiently represented by region-based objectives. Whether they provide meaningful and reproducible benefits when incorporated into U-KAN for brain tumor segmentation remains unclear. Methods: : We compared five loss configurations in separate 2D and 3D U-KAN pipelines using multimodal MRI from the BraTS 2023 adult glioma dataset: a region-based baseline, fixed Boundary Loss, Staged Boundary Loss, a Generalized Surface Loss composite, and standalone Boundary Difference-over-Union loss. Each configuration was trained with three seeds in each pipeline, producing 30 runs. Performance was assessed using regional and macro Dice, the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), run-level consistency, and patient-level paired comparisons against the corresponding baseline. Results: : In 2D, Staged Boundary Loss achieved the highest mean macro Dice (0.8139 versus 0.8001) and reduced mean HD95 (22.55 versus 34.81~mm). Patient-level comparisons favored this configuration, but its overlap improvement was concentrated in whole-tumor segmentation and it exceeded the baseline in only one of three matched seed comparisons. In 3D, Staged Boundary Loss produced only small descriptive improvements in macro Dice (0.89794 versus 0.89698) and HD95 (3.645 versus 3.736~mm), with no significant favorable patient-level difference after multiplicity correction. The other boundary-aware configurations did not consistently outperform the baselines, and standalone Boundary Difference-over-Union exhibited substantial instability in one 2D run. Conclusions: : Boundary-aware training did not provide a consistent advantage over region-based objectives. Staged Boundary Loss was the most promising configuration, but its benefits were pipeline-dependent and not reliably reproduced across training runs.

title: Benign Struma Ovarii Presenting as a Large Multicytic Ovarian Mass: Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Struma ovarii is a very rare form of ovarian teratoma with thyroid tissue present in the ovarian mass. A struma ovarii is categorised based on 50% or more of solid tissue being thyroid tissues. This particular entity can be an adult teratoma with distinct diagnostic challenges by virtue of its peculiar features, including thyroid hormone production. The tentative diagnosis is examined in a perimenopausal woman, with long-standing lower abdominal distention. Case Presentation: A 42-year-old woman, with a parity of 4 presented with a two-year history of intermittent episodes of dull lower abdominal pain associated with a feeling of a mass descending across her abdomen. This was associated with episodes of nausea, occasional vomiting, and dyspareunia for about five months. The patient also had irregular heavy menstrual periods for a similar duration. History did not reveal any signs of hyperthyroidism, Abnormal Uterine bleeding nor urinary tract symptoms. On physical examination, a firm, immobile, well-defined suprapubic mass was noted. Evaluation with abdominopelvic ultrasound showed a large, complex left adnexal cystic lesion with multiple septations. The patient was taken up for an exploratory laparotomy. Intraoperatively, a large, tortuous, multi cystic mass and highly vascularized, arising from the left ovary was found, and a left salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed a multicystic ovary with solid areas that contained seromucinous fluid and hemorrhage. Histological verification was made by the demonstration of ovarian tissue containing 80–90% benign thyroid follicles of varied sizes lined with cuboidal epithelium; with foci of calcification; and no evidence of malignancy. The patient made an uneventful postoperative recovery Conclusion Struma ovarii is tough to diagnose because it mimics so many other conditions and rarely causes thyroid symptoms. In women of reproductive age who have complex ovarian masses, it’s worth keeping in mind, even if their thyroid tests are normal. The only way to be sure is to look at the tissue under a microscope after surgery, which, for benign cases, also solves the problem.

title: Pretreatment Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Risk Marker for Brain Metastasis in Patients with Stage I–III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Definitive Thoracic Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Brain metastasis (BM) represents a major pattern of distant failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following definitive thoracic radiotherapy (RT). Systemic inflammation plays a critical role in tumor progression and the metastatic cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for predicting the occurrence, cumulative incidence, and temporal dynamics of brain metastasis in patients with Stage I–III NSCLC receiving definitive thoracic RT. Methods A total of 138 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I–III NSCLC who received definitive-intent thoracic RT (60–66 Gy) between 2014 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Pre-treatment hematological parameters were obtained within two weeks prior to any oncological intervention. Time-dependent Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the dynamic predictive performance of baseline NLR. Independent predictors of brain failure were identified using cause-specific Cox proportional hazards regression, accounting for death as a competing risk. A pre-specified sensitivity analysis was restricted to Stage III patients (n = 108) with mandatory baseline and routine follow-up brain MRI. Results Over a median follow-up of 28.0 months, 40 patients (29.0%) developed BM. Median baseline NLR was significantly higher in patients who developed BM compared to those who did not (3.21 vs. 2.22; p < 0.001). Time-dependent ROC analysis at 28 months yielded an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.79, with an optimal NLR threshold of 2.26 (sensitivity: 91.7%, specificity: 54.6%). Multivariable cause-specific Cox regression demonstrated that higher continuous baseline NLR was independently associated with an increased hazard of BM (HR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.48–2.12; p < 0.001), alongside adenocarcinoma histology (HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 1.41–6.24; p = 0.004). In the Stage III sub-cohort sensitivity analysis, continuous baseline NLR maintained its independent prognostic significance (HR: 1.74, 95% CI: 1.44–2.09; p < 0.001). High baseline NLR (> 2.26) was significantly associated with a higher cumulative incidence of BM (Gray’s test p < 0.001), inferior overall survival (median 34.0 vs. 65.0 months; p = 0.015), and worse progression-free survival (median 18.0 vs. 42.0 months; p = 0.006). Baseline PLR was not significantly associated with BM (p = 0.136). Conclusions Continuous baseline NLR serves as a readily accessible, independent biomarker for predicting the risk and accelerated onset of brain metastasis in patients with NSCLC undergoing definitive chemoradiotherapy. Baseline NLR may aid in risk-stratified neuro-radiological surveillance protocols.

title: Airway Fire During Left Pneumonectomy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Intraoperative airway fire is extremely rare yet potentially fatal, and an oxygen-filled tracheal tube is a major risk factor. Fire during pneumonectomy—in which the airway is simultaneously the operative field, the sole ventilatory route, and the conduit for combustion—is uniquely hazardous. We describe such a case and analyze its mechanism, management, and prevention. Case presentation. A 70-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a long history of smoking underwent thoracoscopic resection of a centrally located left-lower-lobe squamous cell carcinoma. During left pneumonectomy, while the left main bronchus was being divided with monopolar electrosurgery, sudden flame and smoke indicated combustion of the double-lumen tube, which was judged nonventilatable and urgently changed to a single-lumen tube. Before chest closure, bronchoscopy showed red, edematous mucosa with diffuse black carbonized deposits over the carina and both main bronchi; four intraoperative lavage passes were performed, and three further passes were carried out intermittently while the patient remained intubated in the intensive care unit. He was extubated on the first postoperative day, developed transient atrial fibrillation on the second, and was discharged on the seventh. Histopathology confirmed keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (pT4N2M0, stage IIIB). Conclusions. Recognition of the fuel–oxidizer–ignition triad, and preventive measures adopted before and during bronchial division, are essential. Once a fire occurs, immediate cessation of oxygen, rapid re-establishment of a ventilatable airway, aggressive bronchoscopic saline lavage, glucocorticoid pulse therapy, and supportive postoperative care together supported a favorable outcome; at follow-up the patient had completed five cycles of chemotherapy, with intermittent cough and sputum production and hoarseness attributed to unilateral vocal cord paralysis, but remained able to carry out the activities of daily living without clinically significant laryngotracheal stenosis.

title: Anatomical Interfaces as a Complementary Substrate for Structural MRI Representation in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Abstract Background Structural MRI analysis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) commonly relies on region-of-interest (ROI) summaries or voxel-level deep networks, neither of which explicitly quantifies the physical interfaces shared by adjacent brain regions. We investigated whether these anatomical interfaces provide structural information complementary to conventional regional measures. Methods T1-weighted MRI was segmented into 79 anatomical regions using a pretrained nnU-Net. Each region was represented as a graph node with six morpho-textural descriptors, while edges were defined only between regions sharing voxel-level face contact and characterized by Structural Contact and Boundary Appearance features. Results Correlation analyses showed generally limited redundancy between node- and interface-level descriptors, supporting partially distinct representational information. Node-controlled analyses further showed that selected interface features remained significantly associated with disease stage after adjustment for the morpho-textural characteristics of both connected regions, indicating that interface-level variation was not fully reducible to regional abnormalities. White matter hypointensity interfaces repeatedly emerged among the retained stage-associated effects. Selected Structural Contact features also showed convergent associations with clinical severity across CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog13, and MMSE. Representation ablation demonstrated that disrupting anatomical adjacency or removing interface attributes reduced classification performance, supporting the contribution of anatomically organized relational information. The full representation also improved multi-class classification relative to conventional ROI-vector and voxel-level baselines, with this advantage preserved on the independent NACC cohort without fine-tuning. Conclusions These findings indicate that anatomical interfaces provide measurable and complementary structural information beyond conventional region-wise morphometry, offering an interpretable framework for representing inter-regional structural relationships in neurodegenerative disease.

title: Preoperative Risk Stratification of Lymph Node Metastasis in cT1 Lung Adenocarcinoma Using CT Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is important for risk stratification and surgical planning in patients with cT1 lung adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a multi-regional computed tomography (CT) radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information for preoperative prediction of LNM. Methods A total of 172 patients with cT1 invasive lung adenocarcinoma from one institution were retrospectively included and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 120) and an internal validation cohort (n = 52). An independent cohort of 63 patients from a second institution was used for external validation. Radiomic features were extracted from the intratumoral region, a 3-mm peritumoral region, and two habitat subregions generated using K-means clustering. After feature selection, a multi-regional radiomic signature (Radscore) was constructed and combined with preoperative clinical variables using logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Nineteen radiomic features were retained in the final radiomic signature. In the internal validation cohort, the clinical, radiomic, and combined models achieved AUCs of 0.758, 0.844, and 0.852, respectively. Using a prespecified training-derived threshold of 0.4036, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 65.0%, specificity of 87.5%, and NPV of 80.0% in the internal validation cohort. In the independent external cohort, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.731–0.930), with an accuracy of 77.8%, sensitivity of 77.3%, specificity of 78.0%, PPV of 65.4%, and NPV of 86.5%. The Radscore was significantly associated with IASLC pathological grade and visceral pleural invasion (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The multi-regional CT radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information demonstrated good discrimination for preoperative LNM risk stratification in cT1 lung adenocarcinoma and maintained stable performance in an independent external cohort. The model may provide complementary quantitative information for preoperative risk assessment, although further prospective validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

An independent cohort of 63 patients from a second institution was used for external validation. Radiomic features were extracted from the intratumoral region, a 3-mm peritumoral region, and two habitat subregions generated using K-means clustering. After feature selection, a multi-regional radiomic signature (Radscore) was constructed and combined with preoperative clinical variables using logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Nineteen radiomic features were retained in the final radiomic signature. In the internal validation cohort, the clinical, radiomic, and combined models achieved AUCs of 0.758, 0.844, and 0.852, respectively. Using a prespecified training-derived threshold of 0.4036, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 65.0%, specificity of 87.5%, and NPV of 80.0% in the internal validation cohort. In the independent external cohort, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (95% CI: 0.731–0.930), with an accuracy of 77.8%, sensitivity of 77.3%, specificity of 78.0%, PPV of 65.4%, and NPV of 86.5%. The Radscore was significantly associated with IASLC pathological grade and visceral pleural invasion (both P < 0.001). Conclusions The multi-regional CT radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information demonstrated good discrimination for preoperative LNM risk stratification in cT1 lung adenocarcinoma and maintained stable performance in an independent external cohort. title: Hierarchical transfer learning and region of interest standardization for bone age assessment in Thai children
abstract: Abstract \normalfont\unboldmath Bone age assessment (BAA) from hand radiographs is routinely used to evaluate child growth and endocrine disorders, but manual atlas-based reading is slow and reader-dependent, while deep learning models trained on large international datasets may lose accuracy in other populations. We developed a population-specific AI framework for BAA in Thai children. It combines ROI standardization using contrast enhancement, automatic hand detection, and segmentation with an EfficientNetB7 regression model trained through hierarchical transfer learning. The model first learned skeletal-maturity representations from the public RSNA and DHA datasets and was then fine-tuned on Thai hospital data. On a held-out Thai test set excluded from BAA training and validation, hierarchical adaptation achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.64 months (RMSE, 5.85 months; \((R^2=0.98)\)), compared with 5.73 months for pooled training and 7.60 months for the public-only baseline. The full preprocessing pipeline also reduced downstream MAE relative to raw radiographs. It met the predefined detection-and-segmentation processing criterion for all evaluated RSNA and DHA images; however, this finding represents processing completeness rather than independent quantitative validation of segmentation accuracy. Among GP, TW, and a hybrid strategy using TW when applicable and GP outside the validated TW3-RUS range, the hybrid produced the lowest point-estimate MAE, although its advantage over TW was small. Grad-CAM provided exploratory evidence of attention to anatomically relevant regions but also identified localized or non-skeletal attention. Improved RSNA hand ROI annotations are released to support future research.

title: Development and internal validation of a multivariable logistic model for pulp disease in children from the central Peruvian Amazon: a secondary analysis of a case–control study
abstract: Abstract Background Pulp disease is a frequent and largely preventable consequence of untreated dental caries in children, yet its determinants are seldom modelled jointly in socioeconomically vulnerable settings, and probability models that could support screening in primary care are rarely developed or validated. We aimed to identify factors independently associated with pulp disease and to develop and internally validate a multivariable logistic model estimating its probability in children from the central Peruvian Amazon. Methods This was a secondary analysis of the individual-level dataset of a case–control study conducted in 2023 at the primary health care centre of Pichanaki (Chanchamayo, Junín, Peru), comprising 270 children aged 5 to 11 years: 90 cases with pulpal or periapical pathology diagnosed on clinical and radiographic grounds and 180 controls without pulpal involvement. Biological (anemia, hemoglobin concentration, nutritional status), behavioural (fluoride toothpaste, mouthwash and dental floss use, ferrous sulfate intake) and socioeconomic variables (maternal educational level and occupation, maternal age, household income) were retrieved from a previously collected and validated database. Variables with p < 0.20 in bivariable analysis, together with clinically relevant covariates, were entered into a multivariable binary logistic regression model; multicollinearity was assessed with the variance inflation factor. Discrimination was quantified with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration with the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and a calibration curve, and internal validity with a 70/30 training–test split and k-fold cross-validation. The optimal classification threshold was derived from the Youden index, and performance was re-estimated across alternative thresholds. Results Dental caries (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 12.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.85–44.62), ferrous sulfate intake (aOR 11.63, 95% CI 3.85–40.76), anemia (aOR 5.73, 95% CI 1.99–18.14) and non-professional maternal educational level (aOR 3.83, 95% CI 1.36–11.82) remained independently associated with higher odds of pulp disease, whereas fluoride toothpaste use (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.03–0.25), dental floss use (aOR 0.13, 95% CI 0.04–0.36) and mouthwash use (aOR 0.30, 95% CI 0.10–0.83) were inversely associated. Maternal age below 20 years was no longer significant after adjustment (aOR 2.34, 95% CI 0.73–7.81). The final model was adequately calibrated (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ² = 6.11; p = 0.635; Nagelkerke R² = 0.817) and discriminated well (AUC 0.974, 95% CI 0.958–0.990), with an accuracy of 93.3%, sensitivity of 90.0% and specificity of 95.0% at the 0.50 threshold. Internal validation yielded an AUC of 0.975 in the 70/30 split and 0.966 in cross-validation. At the Youden-derived threshold of 0.31, sensitivity reached 96.7% and specificity 92.2%. Conclusions In this vulnerable paediatric population, pulp disease was explained by a combination of caries experience, anemia-related indicators, maternal educational level and everyday preventive behaviours, and these routinely available variables separated affected from unaffected children with high accuracy. Because predictors were recorded concurrently with the outcome within a case–control sample, the model should be regarded as a screening and prioritisation aid rather than a causal or population-calibrated risk tool; external and prospective validation is required before clinical deployment.

title: Third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with processing speed in multiple sclerosis: a single-centre retrospective observational study
abstract: Abstract Background: Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), and slowed information processing is among its most frequent manifestations. Although brain volumetry can quantify atrophy, automated volumetric tools are not universally available in routine practice. We investigated whether third ventricle width (3VW), a simple linear measure obtainable on conventional MRI, is associated with standardised Symbol Digit Modalities Test performance. Methods: This single-centre retrospective observational study included 100 adults with MS assessed in routine care between 2021 and 2023. Current MRI was acquired within one month of cognitive testing. A neuroradiologist blinded to cognitive results measured 3VW three times at the foramen of Monro, and the mean value was analysed. The primary analysis examined the association between current 3VW and age-standardised SDMT performance (SDMT-SD) using Spearman correlation with false-discovery-rate correction. Post hoc multivariable linear-regression sensitivity analyses adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates. MRI measurements approximately 3, 5 and 10 years earlier and analyses of SDMT impairment were exploratory. Results: Twenty-five participants (25%) met the prespecified definition of SDMT impairment (SDMT-SD ≤ -1). Current 3VW was inversely associated with SDMT-SD (rho = -0.556, 95% CI -0.678 to -0.404; q = 2.28 × 10⁻⁸). The association persisted in a fully adjusted linear-regression sensitivity model including age, sex, education and EDSS (β = -0.232 SDMT-SD units per 1-mm greater 3VW, 95% CI -0.391 to -0.074; p = 0.0045). Excluding 14 records previously labelled as CIS produced similar results. Analyses of prior MRI showed associations in selected subgroups but were limited by non-random availability of earlier scans. Conclusions: Greater third ventricle width on routine MRI is associated with worse processing-speed performance in MS. Because it is rapid to obtain and widely accessible, 3VW may serve as a simple imaging marker that prompts cognitive assessment when volumetric tools are unavailable. It should not replace cognitive testing or volumetric MRI, and predictive thresholds require prospective external validation.

title: Selective Endometrial Screening versus Routine Curettage in Postmenopausal Women Undergoing Intrauterine Device Removal: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background The choice between selective and routine endometrial screening during postmenopausal intrauterine device (IUD) removal remains controversial. Universal blind curettage frequently yields insufficient endometrial tissue and results in overtreatment. This study aimed to evaluate a selective, risk-stratified endometrial screening strategy for postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal and develop an individualized endometrial screening strategy for this patient population. Methods A total of 512 naturally postmenopausal women (amenorrhea ≥ 12 months) who underwent IUD removal were retrospectively enrolled. According to the presence or absence of postmenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), patients were divided into a bleeding group (n = 128) and a non-bleeding group (n = 384). All patients with AUB underwent endometrial sampling; asymptomatic patients were sampled only when high-risk transvaginal ultrasound findings were present (endometrial thickness > 8 mm, heterogeneous echogenicity, or uterine cavity effusion; n = 218). The remaining 166 low-risk asymptomatic patients underwent IUD removal alone. Baseline clinical characteristics, preoperative transvaginal ultrasound findings, and postoperative pathological outcomes were analyzed. Results Patients with AUB had significantly higher body mass index (BMI), higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus, hormone replacement therapy (HRT) history, and tamoxifen exposure history (all P < 0.05). Endometrial thickening, heterogeneous echogenicity, and uterine cavity effusion were all significantly more common in the AUB group (all P < 0.001), whereas the rate of IUD incarceration did not differ (P = 0.121). Among the 346 sampled patients, the overall detection rate of significant endometrial lesions (hyperplasia with or without atypia and carcinoma) was 10.40%. The lesion detection rate in the bleeding group was 14.06%, which was significantly higher than 8.26% in the asymptomatic ultrasound high-risk group (P = 0.040). Low-risk asymptomatic patients with normal ultrasound presented an extremely low risk of severe endometrial lesions. Blind curettage yielded invalid tissue specimens in a proportion of cases. Conclusions Postmenopausal abnormal uterine bleeding, abnormal endometrial ultrasound features, diabetes, obesity, and hormone-related exposure are significant risk factors for endometrial lesions in postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal. Routine universal curettage is unnecessary for unselected postmenopausal women undergoing IUD removal. A selective endometrial screening strategy integrating clinical symptoms, transvaginal ultrasound and systemic risk factors is feasible, safe and effective. It avoids unnecessary curettage in around one-third of patients and reduces overtreatment.

title: Noncontrast Multiparametric MRI Adds Value to Preoperative Peritoneal Cancer Index Assessment in Pseudomyxoma Peritonei: Comparison with Contrast-enhanced CT
abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare noncontrast multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for agreement with intraoperative peritoneal cancer index (PCI) and detection of key imaging features in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP). Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 40 patients with pathologically confirmed PMP who underwent cytoreductive surgery and preoperative mpMRI and CECT in 2024. Intraoperative PCI across 13 abdominopelvic regions served as the reference standard. Total PCI agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland–Altman 95% limits of agreement (LoA), with analyses stratified by PCI (≤ 20 vs > 20). Regional agreement and sensitivities for key imaging features were also compared. Results Forty patients (median age, 60 years; 25 women) were included. mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative total PCI than CECT (ICC, 0.98 vs 0.90; difference, 0.08 [95% CI: 0.05, 0.15]), with narrower LoA (7.1 vs 19.1 points). Agreement remained greater with mpMRI for PCI ≤ 20 (ICC, 0.91 vs 0.58) and PCI > 20 (ICC, 0.95 vs 0.74). mpMRI showed higher regional agreement in 11 of 13 regions after multiple-comparison correction. mpMRI had higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites (100% vs 61%; P = 0.002) and intralesional septation (95% vs 37%; P = 0.002), whereas CECT had higher sensitivity for intralesional calcification (100% vs 0%; P = 0.021). Conclusion Noncontrast mpMRI showed greater agreement with intraoperative PCI than CECT and higher sensitivity for mucinous ascites and intralesional septation, whereas CECT better detected intralesional calcification.

title: Chemical Composition of Radiolucent Urinary Stones: A Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy Study
abstract: Abstract Background Radiolucent urinary stones are commonly presumed to represent uric acid calculi; however, the chemical composition of these stones may be heterogeneous. Accurate characterization of stone composition may provide clinically relevant information for understanding stone pathogenesis and optimizing individualized management. This study aimed to determine the FTIR-based chemical composition of radiolucent urinary stones and evaluate its association with demographic and clinical characteristics. Methods This cross-sectional study included 43 patients with radiolucent urinary stones who underwent percutaneous nephrolithotomy or endoscopic lithotripsy at Razi Hospital, Rasht, Iran. Retrieved stones were analyzed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Stone composition was classified based on comparison of overall spectral patterns with reference spectra. Associations between stone composition and demographic characteristics, body mass index, stone size, medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, and history of urinary tract infection were assessed. Results Mixed stone compositions were identified in 60.5% of specimens, while pure uric acid stones accounted for 14.0%. The most frequent FTIR-based classification was uric acid plus calcium phosphate (53.5%), followed by pure calcium oxalate (25.6%). Overall, uric acid-containing compositions were identified in 74.4% of specimens. Age was significantly associated with stone composition (p = 0.048), with uric acid plus calcium phosphate becoming more frequent among older patients. No significant associations were observed between stone composition and sex, BMI, stone size, previous medical history, dietary pattern, urine culture results, or history of urinary tract infection. Conclusion Radiolucent urinary stones in this cohort demonstrated substantial compositional heterogeneity and should not be assumed to represent pure uric acid stones based solely on radiographic appearance. FTIR analysis identified frequent uric acid-containing mixed compositions, particularly uric acid plus calcium phosphate. These findings highlight the value of direct stone composition assessment in radiolucent calculi and support further investigation using larger cohorts with detailed metabolic evaluation to clarify the mechanisms underlying mixed stone formation.

title: A MobileNetV2-Based Boundary-Aware Improved DeepLabv3+ Network for Gastrointestinal Endoscopic Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Objective: Gastrointestinal endoscopic lesion segmentation is challenging because lesions often exhibit substantial variations in morphology and size, blurred boundaries, small foreground regions, and complex mucosal background interference. This study proposed an improved DeepLabv3+ segmentation model that integrates a lightweight backbone, cascaded multi-scale contextual modeling, and boundary-aware auxiliary supervision to improve automatic lesion segmentation in endoscopic images. Methods: DeepLabv3+ was used as the baseline framework. The original feature extraction backbone was replaced with MobileNetV2 to reduce model complexity while extracting both low-level spatial details and high-level semantic features. The ASPP module was redesigned as a cascaded multi-scale atrous convolution module to enable feature reuse among branches with different dilation rates. In the low-level feature pathway, a boundary attention module was introduced to enhance contour-related responses according to a predicted boundary probability map. During training, boundary targets were automatically generated from ground-truth masks, and the model was optimized using a combination of cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and boundary BCE loss. The dataset included 1,445 gastrointestinal endoscopic images with pixel-level labels, of which 1,300 were used for training and 145 for testing. F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and IoU were used for evaluation. Results: The complete model achieved an F1-score of 0.878, sensitivity of 0.860, specificity of 0.995, accuracy of 0.990, and IoU of 0.784 on the test set. Compared with the original DeepLabv3+ baseline, IoU increased from 0.755 to 0.784. Compared with SegNet, the best-performing competing model, the proposed model improved IoU by 0.040. Ablation experiments demonstrated that both the cascaded ASPP module and the boundary attention branch contributed to performance improvement. Conclusion: The proposed improved DeepLabv3+ model effectively integrates multi-scale semantic information and low-level boundary details, achieving favorable segmentation performance for gastrointestinal endoscopic lesions. This method has potential value for lesion localization, contour delineation, and quantitative analysis in computer-assisted endoscopy.

title: The prognostic role of lateral pelvic lymph nodes in patients with low and mid rectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose Lateral pelvic lymph nodes (LPLNs) represent a potential route of locoregional dissemination in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). LPLN management remains controversial, with routine LPLN dissection advocated in some Eastern centres, whereas Western strategies rely primarily on neoadjuvant treatment followed by total mesorectal excision (TME) without systematic lateral pelvic lymph node dissection (LPLND). As a result, the prognostic significance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-suspected LPLNs in patients treated with contemporary neoadjuvant approaches remains uncertain, particularly in Western cohorts where pathological confirmation is rare. This study aimed to determine the incidence of MRI-suspected LPLN involvement and to evaluate its prognostic impact on overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Methods This was a retrospective study at the Institut Jules Bordet that included patients treated for LARC between January 1, 2007 and December 31, 2021. Pre-treatment MRI was used to identify suspected LPLN involvement. The prognostic impact of MRI-suspected LPLNs on OS and DFS was assessed. Results A total of 115 patients with LARC were included. Twenty-one patients (18.3%) had MRI-suspected LPLNs at diagnosis. Despite a higher risk of LPLN recurrence in the group with MRI-suspected LPLN (9.5% vs 1.1%), no statistically significant association was observed between pre-treatment LPLN status and OS or DFS (P = 0.88 and P = 0.73, respectively). Conclusion In this cohort, MRI-suspected LPLN involvement was not associated with impaired survival outcomes. Prospective studies using standardised radiological criteria and treatment strategies are warranted to better define the prognostic role of LPLNs in LARC.

title: Impact of Epicardial Adipose Tissue on Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Coronary computed tomography Angiography-Based Imaging Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to explore the association between epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume quantified by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and prognosis in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Patients and methods: In this retrospective study, 119 HFrEF patients undergoing CCTA between January 2022 and December 2023 were enrolled. EAT volume were semi-automatically quantified using CCTA sequences. The primary endpoint was the composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure rehospitalization during follow-up. Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier analyses assessed the association between EAT volume and events. Conventional and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to evaluate predictive performance, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated. Results Over a median 649-day follow-up, 50 patients (42.0%) experienced endpoint events. Compared with patients without endpoint events, those with endpoints had lower EAT volume (56.55 ± 21.33 cm³ vs. 74.64 ± 25.19 cm³, P < 0.001) and higher EAT density (-72.94 ± 6.80 Hounsfield Units vs. -76.61 ± 5.07 Hounsfield Units, P = 0.002). Multivariate regression analysis showed that EAT volume was an independent prognostic predictor in HFrEF patients; lower EAT volume was associated with poorer prognosis, with a determined cut-off value of 65.53 cm³. Subgroup analysis revealed that patients with lower EAT volume combined with lower body mass index had the poorest prognosis compared with other subgroups. Conclusion In patients with HFrEF, EAT volume is an independent prognostic predictor with moderate predictive value, and its cut-off value may provide additional information for clinical management.

title: Three-dimensional visualisation combined with intraoperative ultrasound in laparoscopic hepatectomy for complex hepatolithiasis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objective Complex hepatolithiasis remains challenging for laparoscopic hepatectomy. Three-dimensional visualisation technology (3DVT) alone is limited by its static, preoperative nature, whereas intraoperative ultrasound (IOUS) lacks a global anatomical overview, and quantitative evidence for their synergistic benefit remains insufficient. This propensity score-matched (PSM) retrospective cohort study evaluated whether combined 3DVT and IOUS navigation improves perioperative safety and long-term outcomes compared with conventional two-dimensional imaging in patients with complex hepatolithiasis. Results Among 180 patients who underwent laparoscopic hepatectomy between January 2020 and December 2025, 66 matched pairs were analysed. The combined-navigation group had significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss and lower conversion and transfusion rates than the control group (all P < 0.05). The one-stage stone clearance rate was 100.0% versus 90.9% (P = 0.028), and the overall postoperative complication rate was 3.0% versus 18.2% (P = 0.009). Over a mean follow-up of approximately 37 months, the stone recurrence rate was 1.5% versus 10.6% (P = 0.039), with significantly better recurrence-free survival (log-rank P = 0.039). Combined navigation was an independent protective factor for postoperative complications (OR = 0.313, 95% CI 0.107–0.915; P = 0.034).

title: Influence of body composition on survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis: a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram development and validation
abstract: Abstract Background Bone metastasis (BM) reduces survival in breast cancer (BC) patients. Altered body composition is prognostic but poorly captured by conventional models; radiomics enables precise CT-based quantification. This study aimed to determine the influence of body composition on survival in BC patients with BM and to develop and validate a comprehensive web-based nomogram. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 197 breast cancer patients with bone metastasis at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute & Hospital, Tianjin, China, between January 2010 and December 2017. Another 38 patients from January 2012 to December 2016 in P.A. Hertsen Moscow Oncology Research Center, Moscow, Russia, as the external validation cohort to test the nomogram. The radiomics score for predicting survival was established by using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression. The Kaplan-Meier method was used for survival analysis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to construct a clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram based on clinicopathologic and radiomics features of body composition. A clinicopathologic web-based nomogram was also established. Receiver operating characteristic curves and internal validation cohort were used to evaluate aforementioned nomograms. We verified the clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram model using the external validation cohort. Results The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed the 1-year survival in breast cancer patients with bone metastasis in construction cohort was 81.9%, the 3-year was 48.6%, the 5-year was 19.6%. Body composition was proved to be significantly correlated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Eight variables were selected into the clinicopathologic-radiomic model: radscore, bone CT-value, bone metastasis location, pathology subtype, brain metastasis, ALP, Ca and TMI. The clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram was satisfactory with the C-index of 0.82, which was higher than the clinicopathologic model (C-index was 0.71). The AUCs of clinicopathologic-radiomic web-based nomogram in 1-, 3-, 5-years were internally validated (82.3%, 91.1% and 82.9%, respectively) and externally validated (85.1%, 84.3% and 67.7%, respectively). Conclusions Body composition was significantly associated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients with bone metastasis. Individualized rehabilitation training and nutritional support intervention should be encouraged for the patients. The established clinicopathologic-radiomic nomogram was an effective tool for prognostic prediction, and could help clinicians make personalized clinical decisions.

title: Individualized Structural Brain Deviations in Bipolar I Disorder: a Normative Modeling Study of 4 660 ENIGMA Participants
abstract: Abstract Bipolar disorder (BD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition characterized by marked clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity. Prior neuroimaging studies have used case-control comparisons yielding small to moderate effect sizes for group differences. Large and diverse samples are needed to map heterogeneity within BD. Here, we used individualized brain morphometry deviations derived from normative modeling for three MRI-based measures (regional cortical thickness, regional surface area, and subcortical volumes). We applied this approach to a large international sample of 4 660 individuals (1 145 with bipolar I disorder and 3 515 healthy controls) from the ENIGMA Bipolar Disorder Working Group consortium (age range = 8–80, female = 53.15%) and examined the distribution of deviations within the bipolar disorder group, differences between healthy controls and individuals with bipolar disorder, and associations between neuroanatomical deviations and clinical variables. We found that individuals with bipolar disorder showed a higher proportion of localized extreme deviations, notably negative cortical thickness deviations in regions consistently reported as thinner in prior studies (the left superior frontal gyrus, bilateral inferior frontal gyrus (pars opercularis), left precuneus) and subcortical volume negative deviations in the left hippocampus. In addition, ROI-level deviations in the left middle temporal gyrus and the left inferior temporal gyrus were associated with longer illness duration. This is the largest study to date exploring individualized deviations as neuroanatomical features associated with bipolar disorder. Our findings suggest that neuroanatomical heterogeneity is a core feature of bipolar disorder, with preferential left-lateralized cortical-hippocampal involvement pointing to spatially structured heterogeneity.

title: DSPAN: Dual-domain structure-aware adversarial learning with physics-inspired consistency for low-dose CT denoising
abstract: Abstract Background Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but increases noise and artifacts that can obscure low-contrast anatomy. We developed the Dual-domain Structure-Preserving Adversarial Network (DSPAN) to improve LDCT image fidelity. Methods DSPAN combines a ResNet-based generator with dual-domain structure-aware attention and coupled gradient- and frequency-consistency learning. We used five-fold patient-level cross-validation on all 10 patients in the 2016 NIH-AAPM-Mayo Clinic Low Dose CT Grand Challenge dataset. Each fold included seven training patients, one validation patient for checkpoint selection, and two test patients. Every patient was tested once. Slice-level measurements were averaged within each patient, and performance was summarized descriptively across the 10 patients. No null-hypothesis tests were performed. Results DSPAN achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio of 40.2105 ± 1.6183 dB, structural similarity of 0.9424 ± 0.0220, and root mean squared error of 2.5359 ± 0.5303 in 8-bit-equivalent units. It had the best mean value for all six evaluated image-quality metrics. Compared with DU-GAN, mean peak signal-to-noise ratio increased by 0.1505 dB and root mean squared error decreased by 0.0410. Module ablation showed a 1.0662 dB mean peak signal-to-noise ratio gain over ResNetGAN alone. Conclusions Combining structure-aware attention with gradient and frequency consistency improved internal image-quality performance in this 10-patient dataset. External validation and diagnostic reader studies are needed to establish generalizability and clinical relevance.

title: Optimization of Post-processing Reconstruction for Orthopedic Metal Implants on Photon-Counting Detector CT: A Within-Patient Comparison
abstract: Abstract Objectives To determine how iterative metal artifact reduction (iMAR), virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), and reconstruction kernel selection affect metal artifacts and image quality around orthopedic implants on photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT), and to identify task-specific reconstructions for bone and soft-tissue evaluation. Materials and methods This retrospective within-patient study included 10 patients with 11 orthopedic implant sites. All reconstructions were generated from the same PCD-CT raw data. Three predefined comparisons were performed: iMAR off versus on at 70 keV/Br40/1.0 mm; four bone reconstructions combining T3D or 145-keV VMI with Qr64 or Br64 at 0.4 mm; and four soft-tissue reconstructions combining T3D or 65-keV VMI with Br40 or Qr40 at 1.0 mm. CT attenuation, image noise, artifact index (AI), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), 5-point Likert scores, and interreader agreement were evaluated. Results With matched parameters, iMAR increased median bone scores from 2 to 4 and soft-tissue scores from 1 to 2–3. For bone, 145-keV VMI reduced image noise and AI compared with T3D; 145-keV Br64 had the highest subjective scores, whereas 145-keV Qr64 showed the most favorable quantitative metrics. For soft tissue, T3D had lower noise and AI and higher SNR than 65-keV VMI, and T3D Br40 received the highest subjective scores. Weighted κ ranged from 0.635 to 0.717. Conclusion Post-processing optimization on PCD-CT was task specific. iMAR improved image evaluability, 145-keV VMI favored bone and bone-implant interface assessment, and T3D Br40 favored adjacent soft-tissue evaluation.

title: Comprehensive Treatment of a Patient with Osteogenesis Imperfecta and Congenital Hemivertebra: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder characterized by extreme bone fragility, making the surgical management of associated severe scoliosis exceptionally challenging due to the high risk of instrumentation failure. The coexistence of OI and a congenital hemivertebra in a single patient is exceedingly rare and further complicates spinal deformity correction. We report the case of a 17-year-old boy with OI who presented with progressive, severe thoracolumbar scoliosis and worsening lumbar pain. Imaging revealed major Cobb angles of 85° and 95°, a fully segmented L3 hemivertebra, and markedly reduced bone mineral density with a total lumbar Z-score of –5.8. To optimize surgical safety and outcomes, a comprehensive, multidisciplinary treatment strategy was implemented. This included preoperative halo-gravity traction to improve spinal flexibility and alignment, alongside bisphosphonate therapy to enhance bone mass. The patient underwent a posterior L3 vertebrectomy and spinal fusion from T4 to S1. Postoperative radiographs demonstrated satisfactory deformity correction. Although asymptomatic pedicle screw breakage was observed at the 6-month follow-up—highlighting the immense biomechanical stress posed by the inherent bone fragility in OI—the patient maintained stable spinal alignment without significant loss of correction at 12 months. This case underscores that while meticulous perioperative optimization (including traction and pharmacological therapies) combined with advanced surgical planning can achieve successful deformity correction in patients with OI and congenital scoliosis, continuous long-term monitoring remains vital due to the persistent risk of hardware fatigue. Trial registration Not applicable. This study is a case report and not a clinical trial.

title: Development and internal validation of a CSF-free machine-learning model to distinguish immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis from HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 encephalitis
abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced encephalitis (ICI-iE) is difficult to distinguish from herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and its work-up includes invasive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing. We evaluated whether a model excluding CSF features could achieve discrimination similar to a CSF-inclusive model and support triage before lumbar puncture. Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

Methods We reanalysed 51 complete cases (ICI-iE, 19; HSV-1, 20; anti-LGI1, 12) from a publicly available retrospective dataset combining registry-based ICI-iE cases with single-centre HSV-1 and anti-LGI1 comparators. Random-forest models with 29 features (including CSF) or 25 features (excluding CSF) were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation (5 outer folds × 20 repeats). We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, out-of-fold TreeSHAP values, and a hypothetical high-specificity rule-in strategy across assumed prevalences. Results Mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) across repeats were 0.894 with CSF and 0.902 without CSF. On the repeat-averaged out-of-fold predictions, AUCs were 0.911 with CSF and 0.908 without CSF, and an approximate DeLong comparison showed no significant difference (ΔAUC [with CSF minus without CSF], + 0.003; 95% CI, − 0.033 to + 0.040; p = 0.86). Encephalitis-typical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings and C-reactive protein were the leading contributors. In an exploratory sensitivity analysis, additionally excluding MRI features from the CSF-free model yielded a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.769. At specificity of 0.967–0.973, sensitivity was 0.574–0.597. Under the hypothetical rule-in strategy, the true-positive classification proportion was 21%–22% at the cohort prevalence (37.3%) but 3%–6% at 5%–10% prevalence. False-positive classification remained 2–3% of patients across the evaluated prevalence scenarios. Calibration was poor. Conclusions In this small internally validated dataset, excluding CSF features did not materially lower the point estimate of discrimination, whereas discrimination depended substantially, but not exclusively, on MRI findings. The CSF-free model may support triage while confirmatory testing is pending but should not replace CSF testing to exclude HSV-1 encephalitis. External validation in standardised, representative cohorts is required, particularly given potential confounding by data source.

title: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich Syndrome Complicated by Right Ectopic Atrophic Kidney: A Case Report from a Primary Hospital
abstract: Abstract Background Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS), also termed obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA), is a rare congenital Müllerian duct anomaly frequently accompanied by structural abnormalities of the ipsilateral kidney and ureter. Owing to its nonspecific clinical features, which often overlap with common acute abdominal conditions such as pelvic inflammatory disease and appendicitis-HWWS is frequently misdiagnosed or missed in primary healthcare settings, particularly among post-menarchal adolescents with atypical symptoms. This case report presents a 9-year-old girl with HWWS and ipsilateral ectopic atrophic kidney associated with an ectopic ureteral orifice, and discusses the diagnostic reasoning, stepwise imaging strategy, and multidisciplinary management experience gained at a primary hospital. Case presentation: A 9-year-old girl presented with intermittent lower abdominal distending pain for 15 days. Menarche had occurred four months earlier; menses were irregular, without cyclic dysmenorrhea or vaginal purulent discharge. Initial pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a mixed echogenic pelvic mass and absent right kidney. Subsequent contrast-enhanced pelvic MRI and CT urography (CTU) confirmed the diagnosis of type I HWWS, characterized by uterus didelphys with double cervix, right vaginal atresia with hematometra and hematocolpos, and a right ectopic atrophic kidney with an ectopic ureteral orifice. After multidisciplinary consultation involving gynecology, urology, and general surgery, the patient underwent combined hysteroscopic resection of the right vaginal oblique septum, laparoscopic resection of the ectopic right kidney and ureter, and cystoscopy. The intraoperative course was uneventful. Postoperative anti-infective therapy and vaginal care were provided; the patient recovered satisfactorily and was discharged on postoperative day 10 without abnormal vaginal discharge. Conclusion HWWS exhibits heterogeneous and often atypical manifestations in adolescent girls. Primary-care physicians should maintain a high index of suspicion and adopt an integrated genitourinary diagnostic mindset. A stepwise imaging strategy combining ultrasonography, MRI, and CTU can significantly improve early recognition. Combined minimally invasive surgery under multidisciplinary collaboration is safe and feasible, and may serve as a useful reference for the management of complex congenital genitourinary malformations in primary hospitals.

title: CINet: Communication-aware Inter-modality Network for Distributed Multi-Modal MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Abstract AI-enabled medical imaging is increasingly moving toward distributed acquisition, computing, and inference, where information required by a downstream task may reside at different nodes. In multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction, this situation arises when a fully sampled auxiliary contrast is not locally available but can provide complementary information for reconstructing an undersampled target contrast. Existing methods generally assume direct access to the auxiliary modality and therefore do not consider the communication constraints involved in transferring such information between distributed nodes. To address this problem, we propose the Communication-aware Inter-modality Network (CINet) for distributed multi-modal MRI reconstruction, which jointly considers auxiliary representation transmission and cross-modal reconstruction under communication constraints. Specifically, a Task-Oriented Communication Encoder reweights multi-scale auxiliary features and generates compact representations under a prescribed communication budget. The resulting representations are transmitted through a noisy channel, and a Target-Conditioned Selective Fusion module selectively incorporates the received auxiliary information according to the current target representation. CINet thus coordinates compact auxiliary information transmission with its downstream utilization for target reconstruction. Experiments on multi-modal prostate MRI demonstrate that CINet achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance under different undersampling patterns and acceleration factors while preserving local structural details. Further evaluations under varying communication budgets and channel signal-to-noise ratios characterize the communication--reconstruction trade-off under different transmission conditions.

title: CTA-Based 3D Thrombus Radiomics and Machine Learning for Differentiating Stroke Etiology in Acute Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and evaluate machine learning models integrating three-dimensional (3D) thrombus radiomic features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) with clinical variables to differentiate large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA) from cardioembolism (CE) in patients with acute middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Materials and Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 453 patients with acute MCAO who underwent endovascular treatment (EVT). The 3D thrombus region was segmented on preoperative CTA, and radiomic features reflecting intensity, texture, and morphology were extracted. Multiple machine learning models integrating radiomic and clinical variables were developed using the training cohort and evaluated in a held-out test cohort. Discrimination, calibration, SHAP-based interpretability, feature importance, and decision curve analysis were assessed. Results: Among the evaluated models, the random forest (RF) model showed competitive performance in the held-out test cohort, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.822, sensitivity of 0.867, and the lowest Brier score (0.171) among the evaluated models. Both clinical and 3D thrombus radiomic features contributed to model predictions. Intraprocedural tirofiban use, admission LDL-C level, sex, admission NIHSS score, and selected thrombus texture and morphological features were important predictors. Decision curve analysis indicated positive net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05–0.60. Conclusion: Three-dimensional thrombus radiomics from routine preoperative CTA combined with clinical variables may help differentiate LAA from CE in acute MCAO. The interpretable RF model may serve as a complementary tool for acute-phase stroke etiological assessment.

title: Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty With Dual Mobility Cup for Neglected Non- Traumatic Dislocation Following Conversion Long Stem THA After Failed Intertrochanteric Fracture Fixation: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conversion total hip arthroplasty (THA) following failed internal fixation of proximal femoral fractures is technically challenging and is associated with an increased risk of complications, including postoperative instability.¹˒² Dual mobility constructs have been increasingly used in revision THA to improve stability and reduce the risk of recurrent dislocation.⁴˒⁵ Case presentation We report the case of a 62-year-old South Asian female who presented with chronic pain and inability to walk following neglected non-traumatic dislocation of a previously operated left long-stem total hip replacement. She had initially sustained a left intertrochanteric femur fracture following a slip and fall at home, which was treated with open reduction and internal fixation using an angle blade plate. Following implant failure, she underwent conversion to an uncemented long-stem THA. Within two weeks, she developed spontaneous anterior dislocation of the prosthetic hip without trauma. Closed reduction under anaesthesia was attempted but failed, and she subsequently had persistent pain, functional limitation, and inability to bear weight. Imaging demonstrated a dislocated prosthesis with extensive fibrosis and pseudo-acetabulum formation. Revision THA was performed using an extended trochanteric osteotomy for removal of the existing femoral stem, an uncemented long diaphyseal-fitting revision femoral stem, and a cemented dual mobility acetabular cup. Cerclage wiring was used to provide additional support. The hip was stable intraoperatively, and postoperative rehabilitation was initiated. The patient achieved full weight-bearing mobilisation with a walker from postoperative day 2, with satisfactory postoperative radiographs and significant relief of pain. Conclusion Neglected prosthetic hip dislocation following conversion THA after failed fracture fixation presents a complex reconstructive challenge because of altered anatomy, fibrosis, pseudo-acetabulum formation, and compromised soft tissues.¹˒² Revision THA using an uncemented long revision stem combined with a cemented dual mobility acetabular component can provide a stable reconstruction in such high-risk cases.⁴˒⁶ Dual mobility articulation should be considered in revision THA when there are significant risk factors for instability.⁴˒⁵˒⁷

title: Base deficit and triage, not blood ethanol, predict poor outcome after acute alcohol ingestion: a 10-year cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Clinicians often anchor on the blood ethanol concentration when judging the severity of acute alcohol ingestion, yet its prognostic value is uncertain. We compared the blood ethanol concentration with routinely available markers of physiological derangement for predicting a poor outcome in emergency department (ED) patients with acute alcohol ingestion. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults (≥ 18 years) presenting to a tertiary ED between September 2014 and September 2024 with a blood ethanol concentration > 10.1 mg/dL; co-ingestions and toxic-alcohol exposures were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of intensive care unit (ICU) admission and/or all-cause mortality at 30 days or 6 months. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC); independent predictors were identified by multivariable logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation. Analyses were repeated after stratification by presentation type (trauma versus non-trauma). Results Of 2,460 patients (85.4% male; median age 35 years), 90 (3.7%) had a poor outcome. Blood ethanol did not discriminate poor outcome overall (AUC 0.527), whereas base deficit (0.783), bicarbonate (0.768), lactate (0.730) and admission glucose (0.690) discriminated moderately to well. Base deficit performed similarly in non-trauma (0.790) and trauma (0.770) strata. Among non-trauma presentations, patients with a poor outcome had a lower median ethanol concentration (129.9 versus 185.2 mg/dL; p = 0.021). A model combining red triage, base deficit and pathological computed tomography achieved an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.874. Conclusions In ED patients with detectable ethanol, the ethanol concentration is a poor predictor of poor outcome, whereas base deficit, lactate, admission glucose and red triage are stronger, readily available markers. Risk stratification should rest on physiological and structural assessment rather than the toxicological level.

title: Deep Feature Selection and Multi-Sparsity Functional Connectivity Networks for Autism Classification
abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with heterogeneous alterations in functional brain organization, making reliable neuroimaging-based characterization difficult. We developed a framework combining deep feature selection with multi-sparsity functional connectivity networks to identify discriminative connectivity patterns and classify ASD. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 871 participants in the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I dataset (403 ASD and 468 typically developing controls) were analyzed. Pearson correlation networks were constructed across 111 regions and thresholded at multiple sparsity levels. Deep feature selection identified stable connections across training folds, while nested cross-validation selected the optimal sparsity level and evaluated a linear support vector machine. The framework achieved 86.2\% accuracy, 88.8\% sensitivity, 84.0\% specificity, and an area under the curve of 91.6\%. Discriminative connections were concentrated in frontal, occipital, and parietal regions, including the superior frontal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex. These findings show that combining feature selection with multi-sparsity connectome analysis can improve the identification of reproducible autism-associated connectivity patterns. The results should be interpreted as research-level classification rather than a clinical diagnostic test and require independent external validation.
