title: PG-HSAM: Prototype-Guided Hierarchical Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation with Limited Annotations
abstract: Abstract Adapting segmentation foundation models to medical images with limited annotations requires effective use of semantic information without substantially increasing model complexity. We propose PG-HSAM, an extension of H-SAM that introduces prototype prior fusion (PPF) and balanced pixel-to-prototype contrastive regularization (BPC). PPF maintains exponential-moving-average class prototypes, converts pixel-to-prototype similarities into a semantic probability prior, and fuses this prior with the first-stage prediction before hierarchical refinement. BPC regularizes the same feature space with class-balanced pixel sampling. For binary segmentation, foreground and background prototypes are jointly normalized to construct the semantic prior. The prototype memory is non-trainable, and BPC is used only during training. Under the limited-label protocols of H-SAM, PG-HSAM achieves mean Dice scores of 80.49%, 85.20%, and 83.51% on Synapse, LA, and PROMISE12, respectively. Compared with H-SAM, the gains are 0.81, 1.26, and 6.56 percentage points, while Synapse HD95 decreases from 18.35 to 13.70. Ablation and hyperparameter studies further verify the contributions of PPF and BPC and show that the improvement is obtained without increasing the model parameter count.

title: Incremental Value of Pretreatment 18F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI for Predicting Early Treatment Response and Long-Term Prognosis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Undergoing Chemoradiotherapy​
abstract: Abstract Objectives Effective noninvasive tools for predicting treatment response and prognosis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remain lacking. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of integrating pretreatment 18 F-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FAPI PET/CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for short-term complete response (CR) and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with NPC undergoing chemoradiotherapy. Materials and Methods This retrospective study analyzed pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI) parameters in 46 patients with NPC who underwent chemoradiotherapy. Logistic regression identified predictors of CR and developed predictive models, which were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, DeLong test, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Cox regression identified independent predictors of PFS, while Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank test evaluated survival outcomes. Results Nineteen patients (41.3%) achieved CR, whereas 27 (58.7%) did not. Total lesion fibroblast activation protein expression (TLF), signal intensity ratio (SIR), and radiologic extranodal extension (rENE) independently predicted CR. A multimodal model incorporating these variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88, outperforming PET/CT-only (AUC = 0.76) and MRI-only (AUC = 0.79) models numerically. A maximum standardized uptake value of the primary lesion (SUVmax-T) ≥ 17.0 and the presence of rENE independently predicted shorter PFS. The Sankey diagram illustrated that high-risk parameter combinations were associated with non-CR and shorter PFS, while short-term CR was strongly concordant with longer PFS. Conclusion Pretreatment 18 F-FAPI PET/CT and MRI provide complementary information that may improve short-term response assessment and prognostic stratification in NPC.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Treated with Therapeutic Hypothermia: Prognostic Values of Selected Real-World Markers from a Single- Centre Study
abstract: Abstract Background To verify the accuracy and reliability of clinically applicable prognostic markers assessed by neonatologists—specifically, background amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG) at 24 and 36 hours and the presence of abnormal posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) signaling on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)—for predicting mortality and long-term morbidity in newborns undergoing therapeutic hypothermia. Methods This retrospective cohort study included newborns admitted to a tertiary perinatal center (2009–2020) for therapeutic hypothermia. Background aEEG recordings at 24 and 36 hours of life and the presence of abnormal PLIC imaging were evaluated. The ability of these markers to predict mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes was statistically tested. Results Of the 80 infants with complete follow-up data, 15 (18.75%) died, and 17 (21.25%) had an abnormal long-term neurodevelopmental outcome. The predictive ability was as follows: aEEG at 24 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.81 and specificity of 0.90; aEEG at 36 hours yielded a sensitivity of 0.78 and specificity of 0.83; abnormal PLIC signaling yielded a sensitivity of 0.72 and specificity of 0.77. Conclusions The tested markers demonstrate good prognostic value and are readily applicable in routine clinical practice for multimodal prognostication without requiring highly specialized radiological or neurophysiological expertise.

title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Contrast-Enhanced CT-Based Radiomics Model for Predicting Extrahepatic Metastasis after TACE in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a prediction model integrating pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) radiomics with clinical features, and to evaluate its value in predicting extrahepatic metastasis (EHM) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Clinical data of 152 patients with unresectable HCC who underwent TACE at the participating centers between January 2015 and December 2024 were retrospectively collected, and the patients were randomly assigned to a training set and an internal test set at a ratio of 7:3. Seventy additional HCC patients treated at other participating centers served as the external test set.Lesions were delineated on multiphase CECT images for radiomic feature extraction; after LASSO-based feature selection, the selected features were combined with independent clinical risk factors to construct prediction models and a nomogram. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration curves. The predictive performance of the models was validated using data from the external cohort. Results Multivariate analysis showed that age, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and maximum tumor diameter were independent predictors of EHM after TACE. Among the multiphase CT radiomics models, the venous-phase random forest (RF) model performed best (AUC = 0.899, 95% CI: 0.799–0.998), outperforming the logistic regression (LR) and support vector machine (SVM) models. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.923 in the internal test set, outperforming the clinical model alone. In the multicenter external validation cohort, the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.878 (95% CI: 0.801–0.957), indicating good generalizability. Conclusion The clinical-radiomics combined model, constructed from selected CT radiomic features and clinical features, demonstrated robust performance in predicting EHM in both the single-center development cohort and the multicenter external validation cohort. It holds promise for estimating the probability of EHM in patients with HCC after TACE and provides a noninvasive tool for preoperative risk stratification.

title: Quantifying Prematurity-Related Lung Disease in Adulthood using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) in adolescent sheep born premature: A pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is known to offer the best structural and functional pulmonary assessment and is a promising tool for monitoring and tracking disease progression in prematurity-related lung disease (PRLD). Objective We aimed to test the feasibility of capturing anatomical correlates of PRLD with MRI using the bronchopulMonary rottErdam mRi morpholoGy scorE (MERGE-BPD score), and correlating imaging with histological, and functional, lung analysis. Materials and methods In this pilot study, 8 sheep from a larger cohort underwent pulmonary MRI at 1 year of age: 4 term-born lambs and 4 preterm-born lambs, of which two were exposed to intra-amniotic lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Besides MRI, lung function was measured using respiratory oscillometry, and histological analysis was performed on post-mortem lung tissue. Statistics were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test and the Mann-Whitney test, and Z-scores were calculated. Results Areas of hyperintensity of lung parenchyma could be identified in all preterm-born animals and in one of the four term-born sheep. MRI changes are associated with histological changes driven by inflammation (− 0.97, 1.24, and 0.48 (overall p 0.04)) and mucus plugging (− 0.87, 0.86, and 0.82 (overall p 0.07)). Bronchial hyperreactivity was significantly different between the three groups (p 0.05). Conclusion We demonstrate that pulmonary MRI complements conventional lung function and histological analysis by detecting subtle abnormalities in prematurity-related lung diseases. It has the potential to become a valuable, safe, and radiation-free tool for predicting lung function trajectories in children and gaining a deeper understanding of pathophysiological mechanisms following preterm birth.

title: Molecular Findings, Clinical Severity, and Transplant-Free Survival in Pediatric Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Indian Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background The relationship between molecular findings, clinical disease severity, and heart failure (HF) outcomes in pediatric cardiomyopathy remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate genetic diagnostic yield and the relative associations of clinical severity, biomarkers, and multimodality imaging with death or heart transplantation in children with cardiomyopathy. Methods This prospective single-center study included 235 children younger than 18 years at a South Indian referral center. Genetic testing, HF functional class, biomarkers, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and longitudinal outcomes were evaluated. Transplant-free survival was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression. Hierarchical models evaluated incremental prognostic discrimination using Harrell's C-index. Results Genetic testing was performed in 112 children (47.7%), of whom 54 (48.2%) had reported pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants. During a median follow-up of 15 months, 63 children (26.8%) died or underwent heart transplantation. Transplant-free survival did not differ significantly between P/LP-positive and genetic-negative groups (log-rank P = 0.058). Reduced ventricular function and late gadolinium enhancement were associated with adverse outcomes in univariable analyses. Among complete cases, the apparent C-index increased from 0.527 for demographics and cardiomyopathy phenotype to 0.813 after adding HF functional class and 0.842 after biomarkers, with limited additional discrimination from imaging measures. Conclusions Genetic testing demonstrated substantial laboratory-reported P/LP yield, although its effects on clinical management, family screening, and costs were not evaluated. HF functional severity and biomarkers provided the greatest apparent prognostic discrimination for death or transplantation, supporting an integrated clinical approach to pediatric cardiomyopathy assessment.

title: Integrating Deep Learning Radiomics and Node-RADS for Interpretable Prediction of Colorectal Cancer Lymph Node Metastasis
abstract: Abstract Background and purpose: To develop and validate an interpretable multimodal fusion model integrating deep learning radiomics (DLR) and Node-RADS score for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer (CRC). Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 892 CRC patients (training: Center 1, n=684; external validation: Centers 2/3, n=208). Venous-phase CT tumor regions were segmented. 1394 radiomic and 320 ResNet-50 deep learning features were extracted; LASSO was used for feature selection. An XGBoost DLR model was integrated with Node-RADS score and clinical variables to construct a multimodal nomogram. Performance was assessed by AUC, calibration, decision curve analysis, and the DeLong test. SHAP analysis provided model interpretability. Results: LASSO regression identified 24 deep learning features and 9 radiomic features with non-zero coefficients, wherein deep learning features demonstrated higher predictive weights. The XGBoost-based DLR model achieved AUCs of 0.876 and 0.798 in training and external validation cohorts, respectively. The multimodal fusion model, incorporating Node-RADS score and selected imaging features, yielded significantly improved AUCs of 0.900 (95%CI:0.874–0.926) and 0.870 (95%CI:0.821–0.919), outperforming both the DLR model and the clinical model (AUC 0.751/0.641) (all DeLong P< 0.05). Calibration curves demonstrated excellent agreement (Hosmer–Lemeshow P > 0.05), and decision curve analysis confirmed superior net clinical benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified DL_27 and lbp_3D_m2_glszm_ZoneEntropy as the dominant predictive features. Conclusion: This externally validated, interpretable CT-based multimodal model integrating DLR signatures and Node-RADS score enables accurate preoperative prediction of LNM in CRC, offering a noninvasive decision-support tool to guide personalized treatment.

title: Diagnostic yield of Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) guided Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) in peripheral pulmonary infections: a prospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a key diagnostic tool in evaluating pulmonary infections and infiltrative lung diseases. However, conventional BAL relies on operator-dependent segment selection, potentially limiting diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions. Virtual Bronchoscopic Navigation (VBN) has been shown to improve localization in biopsy procedures but its role in guiding BAL remains unexplored. Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic yield of VBN-guided BAL in patients with clinical features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. Methods: This prospective observational pilot study included 50 adult patients with features of pulmonary infection having peripheral pulmonary lesions on radiology. All patients underwent VBN-guided BAL. Samples were analyzed using microbiological, molecular, and cytological techniques. Diagnostic yield and impact on clinical diagnosis were assessed. Results: A definitive diagnosis was achieved in 42/50 patients (84%). Diagnostic yield was higher in immunocompromised patients (92.9%) compared to non-immunocompromised patients (80.6%), though not statistically significant (p=0.414). The final diagnosis differed from the initial clinical diagnosis in 62% of cases. Common diagnoses included bacterial pneumonia (36%), tuberculosis (28%), and fungal infections (16%). Conclusion: VBN-guided BAL demonstrates high diagnostic yield in peripheral pulmonary lesions and may significantly alter clinical management. Larger comparative studies are required to validate these findings.

title: Analysis of Risk Factors and Establishment of a Predictive Model for Endplate Collapse After Posterior Short-Segment Fixation Combined with Screw Placement at the Injured Vertebra in Thoracolumbar Fractures
abstract: Abstract Purpose To identify the risk factors for endplate collapse in patients with thoracolumbar fractures undergoing posterior short-segment fixation combined with intermediate screw placement, and to develop and validate a clinical prediction model to aid in early risk stratification and prognosis optimization. Materials and methods Clinical data from 135 patients with thoracolumbar fractures treated with posterior short-segment fixation and screw placement at the injured vertebra were retrospectively analyzed. Based on postoperative imaging findings, patients were stratified into an endplate collapse group (n = 57) and a non-collapse control group (n = 78). Variables collected included demographic and fracture characteristics (age, gender, BMI, fracture location, fracture pattern, mechanism of injury, osteoporotic status), radiographic parameters (screw length at the injured vertebra, severity of endplate and intervertebral disc injury, extent of anterior and posterior complex injury, postoperative mean vertebral body height [MVBH] and Cobb angle [CA]), and postoperative outcomes (fixation duration, postoperative Pfirrmann grade). Univariate analysis identified variables with significant between-group differences. Independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse were determined by multivariable logistic regression analysis. A predictive model was constructed incorporating these factors, and its performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with calculation of area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in BMI, osteoporotic status, screw depth, endplate injury grade, intervertebral disc injury severity (Sander classification), load-sharing classification (LSC) score, postoperative Pfirrmann grade, and postoperative Cobb angle between groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade as independent risk factors for postoperative endplate collapse (all P < 0.05), with screw depth demonstrating the largest odds ratio and thus the strongest association. A predictive model incorporating these three factors was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888 (95% CI: 0.826–0.943), with sensitivity of 78.9% and specificity of 89.7%, indicating favorable predictive performance. Conclusion Postoperative endplate collapse following posterior short-segment fixation with injured vertebra screw placement for thoracolumbar fractures is multifactorial, with osteoporosis, screw depth, and endplate injury grade serving as major independent risk factors. The predictive model developed in this study effectively stratifies the risk of postoperative endplate collapse and may provide a valuable tool for preoperative risk assessment, intraoperative technical optimization, and postoperative individualized rehabilitation planning, thereby potentially reducing the incidence of endplate collapse and improving functional outcomes.

title: Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy and Metabolic MRI in Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Synthesis of Neurochemical Biomarkers and Clinical Applications
abstract: Abstract Background: Since the introduction of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹H-MRS) in epilepsy research in the 1980s, metabolic MRI has provided unique insights into the neurochemical alterations underlying epilepsy. However, evidence has remained fragmented across imaging modalities, epilepsy syndromes, and clinical applications. We systematically reviewed the literature to define the metabolic phenotype of epilepsy and evaluate the evolving role of metabolic MRI in epilepsy research and clinical practice. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched through April 2026 for original human studies investigating metabolic MRI in epilepsy. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Findings were synthesized through structured qualitative evidence, supported by integrated methodological, scientometric, tabular, and visual analyses. Results: A total of 298 studies were included. Focal epilepsy demonstrated widespread alterations involving N-acetyl aspartate, glutamate, Gamma-aminobutyric acid, choline-containing compounds, myo-inositol, lactate, and other metabolites across epileptogenic and brain networks. Generalized epilepsy was characterized by predominantly bilateral and thalamo-cortical metabolic abnormalities, whereas tumor-associated epilepsy showed distinct metabolic alterations within tumors and the peritumoral zone. Treatment and prognostic studies demonstrated metabolite-specific changes following pharmacological and surgical interventions, and emerging metabolic MRI techniques provided complementary information on bioenergetics, ionic homeostasis, glutamatergic cycling, and metabolic flux. Conclusions: The available evidence supports epilepsy as a disorder of distributed metabolic networks that share a common signature of neuronal dysfunction while exhibiting syndrome-specific alterations in neurotransmission, gliosis, and energy metabolism. Complementary metabolic MRI techniques provide distinct biological information, but their clinical translation will require methodological harmonization and multimodal integration.

title: CardioJEPA: A Framework for Holistic Cardiac Representations Through Predictive Multimodal Alignment with ECG-Preservation
abstract: Abstract The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used cardiac diagnostic tool, but it reflects cardiac structure and function only indirectly. Aligning ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) representations offers a way to transfer imaging-derived structural knowledge into the ECG encoder without compromising the electrophysiological information it already carries. Contrastive learning has become the predominant approach for ECG--CMR alignment, yet the quality of the learned representation is jointly determined by the CMR target representation, the alignment objective, and the preservation of electrophysiological information unique to the ECG. We propose CardioJEPA, a predictive alignment framework built on frozen cardiac foundation models that addresses all three: a target that separates static anatomy from cardiac motion, a predictive objective that maps ECG representations onto a fixed CMR target without instance discrimination, and a preservation term that retains nearly all pre-alignment electrophysiological information. On 63,193 paired ECG--CMR recordings from the UK Biobank, CardioJEPA outperforms previous ECG--CMR alignment methods across structural, electrical, and diagnostic tasks, retains 98.6% of the ECG-unique information present before alignment, substantially reduces the modality gap relative to matched contrastive alignment, and transfers to external cohorts for structural heart disease and Chagas cardiomyopathy without task-specific training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Anatomically-Guided Attention for False Positive Reduction in Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation can produce false positives in anatomically implausible locations, which inflate tumor volume estimates and reduce clinical trust. We investigate whether injecting an anatomical location prior into the network's attention can reduce these errors. We propose a prior informed attention gate that conditions U-Net features on empirical tumor-location prior maps computed from the training annotations, applied as a residual spatial gate at the bottleneck and at every decoder stage. Using the BRISC dataset of 2D contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI slices (glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor), we compare the proposed model with a vanilla U-Net and a learned-gate ablation under identical training, using 3-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set of 860 images. We evaluate Dice, IoU, precision, recall, Hausdorff distance, HD95 and a dedicated far false-positive measure. The proposed model matched the baseline in Dice (0.709 versus 0.708) and showed a slightly lower but non-significant HD95 (36.5 versus 37.9 px, p = 0.26); it did not significantly reduce far false positives (49.7 versus 48.0 px, p = 0.82). A simple location prior injected through a spatial gate is therefore insufficient on BRISC, and stronger prior integration, longer training and additional datasets are needed to establish any benefit.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D Local Fibre Orientation Estimation in Composite Computed Tomography: From Volumetric Convolutions to Real-Time Direct Projection Inversion
abstract: Abstract The mechanical integrity, load-bearing efficiency, and damage tolerance of short- and continuous-fiber-reinforced polymer (SFRP/CFRP) composites depend intrinsically on their local 3D fiber-orientation distribution. While X-ray micro-computed tomography (μCT) non-destructively reveals microstructural morphology, standard volumetric extraction relies on classical 3D structure-tensor eigen-analysis. These classical approaches require dense angular projection sets (180+ views), computationally demanding Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions, manual filter tuning, and exhibit severe degradation under Poisson photon noise. This paper introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework for local fiber orientation estimation that operates across two practical regimes: high-precision offline volumetric inspection and real-time inline scan-to-orientation inspection. To overcome the scarcity of physical CT ground truth, we develop a physics-grounded synthetic pipeline coupling directional sampling via the von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution (κ∈[0.5,25]) with collision-free Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) packing (V_f∈[10%,35%]) and GPU-accelerated forward projection with realistic Poisson noise. Ground truth is formulated analytically through second-order orientation tensors, mathematically resolving the unoriented fiber director ±180^∘ sign ambiguity. We benchmark three paradigms across N=7,889 held-out sub-volume patches drawn from 150 independent composite phantoms (70/15/15 parent split): (1) classical 3D structure tensor eigen-analysis, (2) a 3D volumetric convolutional neural network (Model B), and (3) a novel Direct Projection Network (Model C) that infers 3D orientation directly from only 8 raw 2D sinogram projection views, completely bypassing 3D volumetric reconstruction. Model B achieves an overall mean angular error of 9.35 ∘ (4.78 ∘ on aligned tape; a 67% error reduction relative to the 28.27 ∘ classical baseline) at an inference throughput of 140.9 patches/s on GPU. Model C demonstrates that 3D orientation can be recovered directly from sparse 2D projection shadows with 22.57 ∘ overall error (11.35 ∘ on aligned composites), achieving 174.0 patches/s with zero reconstruction computational overhead. Furthermore, industrial tolerance evaluation demonstrates an 84.57% in-spec acceptance rate at automotive tolerance (τ≤15^∘) for Model B. This work demonstrates that deep learning provides both a superior offline alternative to classical image filtering and a viable pathway for inline, reconstruction-free composite manufacturing quality assurance.

title: AI-Based Particle Size Distribution Prediction from 3D Packed-Particle Tomographic Volumes: A Comparative Study with classical Watershed Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Abstract Determining the Particle Size Distribution (PSD) of granular media and powder compacts is vital across condensed matter physics, geological sciences, and materials engineering. While X-ray computed tomography (µCT) captures granular microstructure non-destructively, traditional quantitative PSD estimation relies on classical morphological segmentation (binarization, distance transform, and watershed flooding), which is computationally intensive and sensitive to contact-neck ambiguities. In this work, we investigate whether a compact 3D Convolutional Neural Network (Compact3DCNN, 300,900 parameters) can predict normalized 20-bin PSD histograms directly from unsegmented 3D grayscale volumes without intermediate particle instance extraction. Using a synthetic dataset of 60 independent non-overlapping polydisperse packed-sphere volumes (48 3 voxels) with exact analytic PSD ground truth, we benchmark the CNN against a classical 3D Euclidean distance-transform watershed baseline on an untouched, held-out test split (N = 10, 40 train / 10 validation / 10 test). On this low-to-moderate packing regime (15%–25%), the classical watershed baseline achieved superior accuracy, attaining a mean Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) of 0.0974 ± 0.0261 voxels compared to 0.3428 ± 0.0949 voxels for the CNN (paired 95% bootstrap CI: [+0.1837, +0.3156] voxels). Measured runtime was 1.19 ± 0.27 ms per volume for the CNN on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU versus 33.71 ± 7.50 ms for the watershed pipeline on an Intel CPU; however, we emphasize that this reflects disparate computing architectures rather than a controlled hardware comparison. Furthermore, comparison against an empirical training-set-mean baseline (0.6206 ± 0.2440 vx EMD on validation) confirms that the CNN learns volume-specific morphological features (0.3970 ± 0.1335 vx, a 36.0% error reduction). A controlled validation experiment evaluating direct 1D Wasserstein-1 loss training yielded substantially higher error (1.1382 ± 0.4907 vx EMD) than the primary Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence configuration, illustrating optimization challenges in cumulative L1 histogram penalties. Our findings characterize the accuracy-throughput profile in direct volumetric PSD regression and delineate key open challenges for dense granular systems.

title: A Comparative Study of Lightweight Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian CNNs and Ensemble Models for MRI-Based ASD Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Background: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is essential for improving clinical outcomes. Although deep learning (DL) has demonstrated strong potential in analyzing structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (sMRI), most existing frameworks rely on deterministic models that lack uncertainty quantification—an essential component for clinical decision-making—and often involve high computational complexity, limiting real-world applicability. Objective: This study aims to conduct a comprehensive comparative evaluation of three deep learning paradigms to develop a robust and uncertainty-aware framework for ASD diagnosis using multi-orientational MRI data (axial, coronal, and sagittal views). Methods: We systematically evaluated three categories of models: (1) fine-tuned deterministic architectures, including EfficientNetV2B0, EfficientNetB3, and MobileNetV2; (2) ensemble learning strategies, including averaging, majority voting, weighted averaging, and stacked generalization; and (3) lightweight Bayesian convolutional neural networks (CNNs) incorporating Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout and Variational Inference (VI) to estimate predictive uncertainty. This hierarchical framework enables a balanced assessment of diagnostic accuracy and model reliability. Results: Experimental results demonstrate that ensemble models achieved the highest classification performance, with a peak accuracy of 99.51% in the coronal view. Notably, the proposed lightweight Bayesian CNNs delivered competitive performance while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, enabling the identification of ambiguous and out-of-distribution cases. Additionally, Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that model attention is concentrated in clinically relevant regions, particularly the frontal and temporal lobes, supporting the neurobiological plausibility of the predictions. Conclusion: This study highlights that integrating uncertainty quantification into lightweight deep learning architectures enhances both transparency and reliability compared to conventional deterministic approaches.

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Accurate and anatomically plausible medical image segmentation remains challenging due to low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, interpatient variability, and modality-specific artifacts. Interactive segmentation using spatial prompts has emerged as a promising strategyto guide attention and improve localization, particularly in low-contrast or structurally ambiguous regions. However, existing methodstypically restrict prompt integration to late-stage fusion and lack explicit mechanisms for channel-wise feature modulation, limiting theirability to capture deeper contextual and modality-specific variations across hierarchical representations. To address these limitations, weintroduce Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a novel modulation mechanism that enables deep, hierarchical integration ofsemantic prompts within encoder-decoder segmentation networks. PCCA extracts compact channel descriptors from both image and promptfeatures via pooling, projects them into a shared latent space, and fuses them through a gated excitation unit to compute prompt-awarechannel attention weights. These weights perform hierarchical channel-wise attention by adaptively reweighting feature responses atevery network stage, enabling spatially selective and semantically enriched representations. Building on this mechanism, we proposePROMISE-Net (PROmpt Modulated Integration for SEgmentation), instantiated in two architectural variants: a convolutional model(PROMISE-CNN) and a transformer-based model (PROMISE-Txformer). Across ISIC-Lesion, Kvasir-Polyp, CAMUS-Cardiac, andKvasir-Instrument benchmarks, integrating PCCA into PROMISE-CNN yielded relative IoU improvements of 10.4%, 8.7%, 0.8%, and3.4% over baseline U-Net, while PROMISE-Txformer achieved corresponding gains of 7.6%, 23%, 2.1%, and 1.1% over baseline UNETR.These results demonstrate consistent cross-architectural, cross-modal, and cross-anatomical improvements, establishing PCCA coupledPROMISE-Net as a scalable and generalizable framework for prompt-aware feature modulation in medical image segmentation. The codeis available at https://github.com/kamruleee51/PROMISENet.

title: An Update on Blood-Brain Barrier Penetrating Nanoparticles for the Treatment of Glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive and lethal primary brain malignancy, with patient survival largely unchanged over recent decades despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. A major therapeutic challenge is the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which restricts the delivery of many systemically administered drugs, including emerging biologic and gene-based therapies. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems have therefore attracted intense interest to overcome BBB-associated transport limitations, enhance tumor specificity and enable delivery of potent therapeutic cargos to infiltrative GBM cells. This review provides an overview of some recent advances in BBB-penetrating NP platforms for GBM treatment, spanning lipid-based, polymeric, dendrimer, inorganic, peptide-based and biomimetic systems. We discuss several extracellular and intracellular biological barriers to effective delivery, while outlining how these challenges may inform rational NP design. Targeting strategies exploiting a range of receptors are reviewed alongside stimuli-responsive systems and combination approaches that integrate BBB modulation techniques, including focused ultrasound and intranasal nose-to-brain delivery. While many NP platforms demonstrate compelling preclinical efficacy, translation to the clinic remains limited. We therefore discuss recent clinical developments and highlight select translational opportunities such as preclinical model selection, manufacturing scalability factors and regulatory considerations. As such there may be a need for integrated design strategies, clinically relevant model systems and robust biodistribution and toxicity assessment. Aligning advances in nanotechnology with GBM biology and clinical constraints may be essential in realizing the therapeutic promise of BBB-penetrating nanomedicines to improve outcomes for patients with this devastating disease. Collectively, BBB-penetrating NPs may represent a promising strategy for GBM treatment, and bridging the gap between preclinical success and clinical benefit may remain an opportunity for the field.

title: A Longitudinal Comparison of Baseline Predictors of Five-Year OAG Development.
abstract: To compare sensitivities for prediction of development of open angle glaucoma (OAG) in 5 years in eyes initially assessed as clinically suspect open angle glaucoma in a prospective longitudinal study. Data were collected prospectively every fourth month for five years from both eyes of 88 subjects with at least one clinically glaucoma suspect eye. Presently, observations at occasions 1, 2, 15 and 16 were analyzed. An eye was considered clinically glaucoma suspect eye if it met at least one of the criteria: suspicious ophthalmoscopic optic nerve head appearance, ocular hypertension, pigment dispersion syndrome, exfoliation syndrome, or visual field asymmetry. Measurements of mean deviation (MD) with standardized automatic perimetry (SAP) were used for classification of OAG at 5 years follow-up. The OAG conversion criterion was defined as a mean SAP MD below the critical limit for normality (-3.7 dB) across occasions 15 and 16. At specificity of 95% for measurement at baseline, 95% confidence intervals for sensitivity were estimated for intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disc ratio (C/D-vertical) and neuro-retinal rim area (NRA), both measured with confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (CSLO) and nerve fiber layer thickness measured with laser scanning polarimetry (GDx TSNIT-global) and optical coherence tomography (OCT cpRNFLT-global), respectively. Confidence intervals were estimated using Hilgers, Delta-Wald with logit transformation, and Bootstrap strategies. During the 5-year follow-up, 20 clinically suspect eyes met the OAG conversion criterion. The different strategies resulted in confidence intervals of the same order. The 95% confidence intervals estimated with Bootstrap strategy were 0.57 [0.30;0.84] for OCT cpRNFLT, 0.32 [0.08;0.61] for GDx TSNIT, 0.30 [0.08;0.59] for HRT NRA, 0.26 [0.05;0.58] for HRT vertical C/D, and 0.11 [0.02;0.27] for IOP. For the currently used MD-based OAG conversion definition, OCT-cpRNFLT has the highest sensitivity for prediction of OAG development at the initial visit among the morphometric variables. The low sensitivity for IOP questions the value of IOP slightly above 21 mmHg for prediction of OAG at baseline.

title: ERBB2 Exon 20 Mutation-Guided Trastuzumab Deruxtecan Therapy in Metastatic Lung Adenocarcinoma with Low HER2 Expression: A Case Report.
abstract: HER2 mutations are uncommon in lung adenocarcinoma, and treatment options become limited after failure of standard systemic therapies. We report a 69-year-old woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma involving multiple lymph nodes, bone, and the left adrenal gland. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examinations strongly supported a diagnosis of primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) performed at initial diagnosis in January 2024 identified an ERBB2 exon 20 in-frame insertion mutation (p.Y772_A775dup). The patient received six sequential treatment regimens, including platinum-based chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitor therapy, antiangiogenic therapy, and palliative radiotherapy. Initial tumor regression was observed, but sustained disease control was not achieved. Following further disease progression, the previously identified ERBB2 mutation was reassessed by the multidisciplinary team in 2025. HER2 immunohistochemistry showed an IHC score of 1+. Based on the activating ERBB2 mutation, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) was initiated in June 2025 at a fixed dose of 200 mg per administration (approximately 3.2 mg/kg), lower than the standard starting dose for HER2-mutant NSCLC. Five doses were administered between June and November 2025. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels decreased markedly after treatment. Serial chest computed tomography indicated radiological disease stabilization for approximately 5 months, with no clinically significant treatment-related adverse events documented. This case highlights the value of molecular profiling in identifying actionable ERBB2 mutations despite low HER2 protein expression. It also provides a real-world observation of disease stabilization with a lower-than-standard initial dose of T-DXd, although conclusions regarding reduced-dose efficacy cannot be drawn from a single case.

title: Effect of Ultrasound-Guided versus Conventional Lung Recruitment on End-of-Surgery Atelectasis in Adults Aged 45-74 Years Undergoing Prone-Position Spinal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to compare the effects of ultrasound-guided stepwise lung recruitment maneuver (LRM) versus conventional manual LRM on the incidence of end-of-surgery atelectasis in patients undergoing prone-position spinal surgery. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, 120 patients aged 45-74 years undergoing prone-position spine surgery under general anesthesia were randomized to ultrasound-guided group (n = 60) or conventional manual group (n = 60). Both groups received a fixed PEEP of 5 cmH 2 O intraoperatively. The primary outcome was the incidence of ultrasound-defined atelectasis at the end of surgery (T3). Results The final analysis included 60 patients in the intervention group and 59 in the control group. The incidence of atelectasis at the end of surgery (T3) did not differ significantly between groups [73.3% (44/60) vs 71.2% (42/59); RD = 2.1%, 95% CI: -13.9% to 18.2%; RR = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.82 to 1.29; P = 0.794]. Tidal volume at T3 was lower in the intervention group (385 ± 52 mL vs 437 ± 55 mL, P < 0.001), whereas dynamic compliance was comparable (37 ± 9 vs 36 ± 9 mL·cmH 2 O -1 , P = 0.517). No severe postoperative pulmonary complications occurred. Exploratory analyses suggested that higher T1 PaCO 2 was associated with an increased risk of newly emerged atelectasis at T3, whereas higher T1 heart rate and higher T2 PaO 2 were associated with a reduced risk of newly emerged atelectasis at T3. In the full cohort, T2 atelectasis was associated with T3 atelectasis, but the confidence interval was wide. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation. Conclusion Under a fixed PEEP of 5 cmH 2 O, stepwise ultrasound-guided LRM did not demonstrate superiority over conventional manual LRM. Exploratory analyses suggested that T2 atelectasis and higher preoperative PaCO 2 may be associated with atelectasis at the end of surgery, requiring validation in an independent cohort. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400086097; https://www.chictr.org.cn/). Registered on June 25, 2024.

title: Primary Male Appendiceal Choriocarcinoma With Background of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm: Diagnostic Challenges and Poor Prognosis.
abstract: Background/aim Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive trophoblastic malignancy that is most commonly gestational in origin. Non-gestational choriocarcinoma in the male gastrointestinal tract is extremely rare, and primary appendiceal involvement is exceptional. Case report We report such a case of a 75-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain. Physical examination indicated possible acute appendicitis suspicious for perforation, and computed tomography (CT) scans revealed a 7.5 cm mass in the lower right quadrant as well as numerous liver hypoechoic nodules. No lesions/nodules were identified in his testicles or mediastinum. Emergency surgery with right hemicolectomy and concurrent liver biopsy was performed. Pathology gross exam revealed a 7.5 cm appendiceal mass with associated appendiceal perforation. Histologically, the tumor showed a poorly differentiated carcinoma morphologically composed of syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts and intermediate trophoblasts with adjacent low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN). The carcinoma cells were positive for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), GATA-binding protein 3 (GATA 3) and Sal-like protein 4 (SALL4). These features supported a primary appendiceal choriocarcinoma and the liver biopsy demonstrated metastasis of choriocarcinoma with extensive tumor necrosis. Post-surgery lab tests also revealed an exceptionally high serum β-hCG titer of 289,308 mIU/ml. The patient underwent hospice care after surgery and expired one month later. Conclusion This is the first documented case of male primary choriocarcinoma with background of LAMN and poor prognosis. Recognition of the three carcinoma components in combination with the corresponding tumor immunohistochemical markers is the key for the precise diagnosis.

title: Topical Esomeprazole for the Prevention and Treatment of Radiation Dermatitis in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background Radiation dermatitis (RD) is a common and clinically significant toxicity affecting the majority of patients undergoing external beam radiation therapy, particularly those treated for head and neck cancer (HNC). RD can impair quality of life, limit treatment intensity, and compromise oncologic outcomes; yet, there is no established standard-of-care for its prevention or management. Preclinical studies suggest that a topically reformulated proton pump inhibitor (PPI), esomeprazole (Dermaprazole), has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic properties that may mitigate radiation-induced skin injury. Objective This phase 2 randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the potential safety, feasibility, and efficacy of prophylactic topical Dermaprazole compared with standard supportive care (Aquaphor) in reducing the incidence and severity of clinically significant RD in patients with HNC receiving definitive chemoradiation. Methods This is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial with a 2:1 allocation ratio. A total of 45 adults (≥18 y) with biopsy-confirmed head and neck malignancy planned to receive definitive chemoradiation of at least 66 Gy will be enrolled. Participants will be randomized to receive twice-daily topical Dermaprazole or Aquaphor beginning at computed tomography (CT) simulation and continuing through 2 weeks after completion of radiation therapy. The primary outcome is the rate and severity of RD, assessed weekly during treatment using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5 by the treating radiation oncologist, with blinded dermatologic assessment based on standardized medical photography. Feasibility outcomes include accrual rate, treatment compliance, and questionnaire completion rates. Secondary outcomes include time to onset and healing of grade ≥2 RD, quality of life assessed using the Skindex-16 instrument, radiation dose thresholds associated with dermatitis, and changes in inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin [IL]-1β, and IL-6). More specifically, secondary outcomes will be assessed through serial CTCAE version 5 evaluations for onset and healing, Skindex16 questionnaires for quality of life, radiation dose-volume parameters for dermatitis thresholds, and serum inflammatory marker concentration measurements before, during, and after treatment. Results The study began in June 2022 and has completed enrollment. Data analysis will commence following completion of data collection, with results expected to be published by 2027. Conclusions Should Dermaprazole demonstrate efficacy in reducing RD in patients undergoing radiation therapy, it may offer an alternative or adjunctive treatment option for the prevention and management of RD, potentially reducing treatment-related morbidity and improving patients' quality of life during radiotherapy. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04865731; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04865731. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/91035.

title: The Digital Twin Paradigm in Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Opportunities and Challenges.
abstract: Unlabelled Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. These digital twins include the anatomical twin, using virtual surgical planning and augmented reality for geometric precision; the dosimetric twin, using daily imaging and synthetic computed tomography generation for automated adaptive radiotherapy; and the biological twin, integrating deep phenotyping, radiomics, and mechanistic omics to simulate individualized therapeutic trajectories. Beyond acute care, we explore the clinical utility of digital twins in navigating the "de-escalation dilemma" for human papillomavirus-associated disease and improving survivorship through digital phenotyping. With the advent of longitudinal data from medical-grade Internet-of-Things sensors and circulating tumor DNA kinetics, digital twins can serve as active sentinels, detecting functional decline or subclinical events months before clinical manifestation. Furthermore, the implementation of synthetic control arms via virtual populations offers an avenue to accelerate clinical trials and address ethical issues in rare molecular subtypes. Despite this potential, substantial barriers to implementation remain, including profound anatomical instability during treatment, the "black box" nature of deep learning algorithms, and the challenges of multiscale data integration. We provide a technical roadmap for the development of "morphing" digital twins-dynamic systems capable of continuous geometric and biological auditing. By bridging the gap between the macroscopic world of radiation physics and the microscopic world of cellular evolution, digital twins may help shift the management of HNSCC from population-based statistical probability toward more individualized, biologically informed decision-making, with the goal of optimizing HNSCC management while preserving essential patient functions.

title: Expert Perspectives on Transparency and Trust in AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Chest X-Ray Diagnosis: Qualitative Study.
abstract: Background The integration of AI-based Clinical Decision Support Systems (AI-CDSS) into clinical practice has expanded rapidly, particularly in medical imaging. Beyond algorithmic performance, growing evidence suggests that clinicians' engagement with AI-CDSS is shaped by how transparently systems communicate their outputs, and how trust is formed through human-AI interaction. However, a limited understanding of how these concepts are perceived by end users and developers continues to hinder real-world implementation. Objective This study aims to explore expert perspectives on transparency and trust in AI-CDSS for chest X-ray diagnosis, with a focus on the two-dimensional lens: user interface and users' mental models. Methods A qualitative study was conducted using semistructured interviews with a total of 21 experts, including 11 radiologists and 10 AI experts experienced in AI-CDSS. Data were analyzed thematically to explore factors perceived to influence transparent communication and trust. Results Three themes emerged: (1) perspective of transparency and trust, (2) user interface, and (3) users' mental models. Findings reveal that trust is a dynamic calibration process developed through repeated use, feedback loops, and alignment with clinicians' mental models, rather than algorithmic accuracy alone. Significant discrepancies were identified between how developers design system transparency and how clinicians interpret AI outputs. Conclusions This study demonstrates that transparency and trust are achieved through interpretable outputs, clear communication of system limitations, and alignment with clinical workflows. Designing trustworthy AI-CDSS requires integrating transparent interface design with consideration of users' knowledge, experience, and attitudes to support effective human-AI interaction.

title: Prevalence and morphological types of middle mesial canals in mandibular molars according to the Barros-Costa classification: a CBCT study in a Turkish subpopulation.
abstract: Objective The purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence and configurations of middle mesial canals (MMCs) in a Turkish subpopulation using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) according to the Barros-Costa classification. Materials and methods Two experienced endodontists assessed the prevalence of MMCs in mandibular molars of 213 Turkish patients aged 18-65 years (111 females, 102 males). MMCs were categorized using the Barros-Costa classification based on their association with the mesiobuccal and mesiolingual canals using CBCT scans in all three planes. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons (p < 0.05). A multivariable generalized estimating equations (GEE) model with patient ID as the clustering variable was used to assess the associations between MMC presence and tooth type, age, and sex. Results Of 589 mandibular molars evaluated, 12.4% had an MMC. Distribution was: mesiolingual confluent (43.8%), mesiobuccal confluent (24.7%), independent (23.3%), and confluent (8.2%). MMCs were significantly more frequent in mandibular first molars (20.6%) than in second molars (6.6%) (p < 0.001). The most frequently observed MMC type was the mesiolingual confluent. In the multivariable GEE analysis, mandibular first molars had significantly higher odds of presenting an MMC than second molars (adjusted odds ratio = 3.54, 95% confidence interval: 2.16-5.80, p < 0.001), whereas age and sex were not significantly associated with MMC presence. Conclusions Within the examined single-center Turkish subpopulation and under the specific CBCT acquisition protocol used, MMCs were detected more frequently in mandibular first molars than in second molars. The mesiolingual confluent configuration was the most frequently observed morphological type. These findings highlight the anatomical variability of MMCs and support careful assessment of the mesial root canal system during endodontic treatment.

title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
abstract: Background Athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) remain a persistent challenge because recurrence is common and clinical decisions often depend on incomplete evidence. This consensus statement is intended to give clinicians a practical, unified framework for classification, rehabilitation, and return to sport after athletic hamstring injury. The purpose of this study was to achieve expert consensus on the management of athletic hamstring injuries through a structured, scientific survey approach. Study design Delphi Survey. Methods A modified Delphi process, aligned with CREDES guidelines, was conducted with an expert panel of sports physical therapists identified as having specific expertise in AHSI from the ICCUS Society. Seventeen experienced clinicians completed the final round. Overall, 54 statements reached consensus, with a mean Likert score of 4.56 ± 0.37 out of 5 (strongly agree), and mean agreement of 89.88% ± 12.1%. Clinicians should combine injury classification, functional presentation, symptom response, objective testing, sport demands, and athlete confidence when advancing rehabilitation and making RTS decisions. title: Diagnostic Musculoskeletal Ultrasound in the Evaluation of the Extensor Digitorum Longus.
abstract: The extensor digitorum longus muscle and tendons are among the longer muscle-tendon units in the lower leg and foot. This feather-like, unipennate muscle is part of the anterior ankle group, attaching proximally along the lateral side of the lateral condyle of the tibia and the upper three-quarters of the fibula's inner surface. Near the ankle, the tendon narrows as it passes beneath the extensor retinacula and divides into four smaller tendons that connect to the toes. Since it crosses the ankle joint and attaches to the second through fifth toes, it facilitates dorsiflexion of the foot and extension of the toe joints. An accurate diagnosis of extensor digitorum longus tendonitis or rupture is crucial for appropriate treatment planning and optimal patient outcomes. Diagnostic musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSKUS) has become a widely used imaging modality for assessing many ankle and foot pathologies. It offers a portable, real-time, and cost-effective alternative that is gaining traction in rehabilitation and sports medicine settings. MSKUS has emerged as a valuable, non-invasive imaging modality for evaluating ankle and foot injuries. This manuscript reviews the utility of MSKUS in evaluating the quality, size, sonographic techniques, and clinical implications for rehabilitation professionals who need to visualize the extensor digitorum longus. By integrating MSKUS into clinical practice, providers can improve diagnostic accuracy, increase diagnostic confidence, monitor healing progression, and guide rehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes for patients with ankle and foot injuries.

title: Development of machine learning models for fetal birth weight prediction: A single-center study in a Turkish population.
abstract: Fetal birth weight (BW) is a critical indicator of the prognosis of perinatal health. Accurate estimation of BW is essential in determining the appropriate delivery method. This single-center study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in estimating BW. The study population consisted of 456 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies evaluated at a single tertiary center in the Karaman region of Turkiye between 38 and 41 weeks based on their last menstrual period, who gave birth to a phenotypically normal live newborn within 7 days after the ultrasound examination. Seven out of the nine models developed using ML algorithms had the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) values ranging from 184.30 to 190.00 grams. The formula closest to these values was Hadlock III, with an MAE value of 223.33 grams. In our study, the model demonstrating the highest predictive accuracy was provided by Linear Regression algorithm with an MAE value of 184.30 grams. title: PDGFRβ-Targeting VHH Tracer Enables Noninvasive PET Imaging of Kidney Fibrosis.
abstract: With a prevalence above 10% worldwide, chronic kidney disease is one of the leading medical burdens. Independent of the underlying cause, kidney fibrosis emerges as the common final endpoint and serves as the most robust predictor of disease progression and long-term prognosis. Fibrosis is driven by extracellular matrix-producing mesenchymal cells, which are characterized by platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) expression. PDGFRβ also mediates fibrogenesis in these cells and represents a potential therapeutic target for direct intervention or a potential anchor for selective delivery of antifibrotic drugs. Diagnostic approaches assessing PDGFRβ expression in kidneys are missing. Here, we developed and evaluated a novel tracer using a PDGFRβ-targeting biparatopic variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, designated SP02SP26-ABD, for in vivo, noninvasive, molecular imaging of kidney fibrosis. Methods: PDGFRβ expression was assessed in human kidney biopsies and publicly available transcriptomic datasets. In vivo imaging studies were performed in 2 distinct murine models of kidney fibrosis using fluorescence imaging and 89 Zr-labeled PET. Specificity and dose dependency were evaluated using a nonspecific control variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, R2R2-ABD, and coinjection of increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD. Ex vivo biodistribution and correlation with histologic and molecular markers of fibrosis were performed. Results: PDGFRβ was increased in fibrotic human kidneys across multiple disease entities, predominantly localized to pericytes and fibroblasts, supporting its relevance as a translational imaging target. In vivo imaging demonstrated significantly higher tracer accumulation in fibrotic compared with nonfibrotic kidneys across both models, whereas tracer accumulation in nonrenal organs was low, with minimal uptake in the spleen. We found no difference between fibrotic and nonfibrotic kidneys when using a nonspecific R2R2-ABD control construct, whereas increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD led to a dose-dependent decrease in tracer accumulation, consistent with a saturation effect. Tracer signal correlated with PDGFRβ expression, confirming the specificity of the approach. Conclusion: We provide the first proof of concept for noninvasive PET imaging of PDGFRβ-expressing fibrogenic cells in kidney disease, supporting further development of this approach for specific, noninvasive assessment of kidney fibrosis.

title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor as a Radiotheranostic Target in Orthotopic Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a 5-y survival rate of approximately 20%. Although glypican-3-targeted radiotheranostics are under development, a plurality of patients with HCC lack glypican-3 expression, underscoring the need for alternative targetable antigens. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed in 50%-70% of HCC tumors and represents a clinically validated therapeutic target. Here, we developed and evaluated a panitumumab-based EGFR-targeted radiotheranostic pair, [ 89 Zr]Zr-desferrioxamine-panitumumab ([ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani) for immuno-PET and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Macropa-panitumumab ([ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani) for targeted α-particle therapy, in clinically relevant orthotopic HCC models. Methods: Panitumumab was conjugated with desferrioxamine or Macropa chelators and radiolabeled with 89 Zr or 225 Ac, respectively. EGFR expression was characterized across a panel of HCC cell lines. Binding affinity, biodistribution, and tumor specificity were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic Huh-7 models, with EGFR-mediated targeting confirmed by blocking (200-fold molar excess of unlabeled panitumumab). Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in mice bearing orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors ( n = 6 per group) after a single 9.3 kBq dose of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging, [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani immuno-PET, and blood chemistry. Results: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani exhibited high-affinity binding to EGFR (dissociation constant, 0.35 nM) and demonstrated robust tumor accumulation in both subcutaneous Huh-7 (20.6 ± 2.6 %IA/g) and orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors (19.3 ± 2.0 %IA/g) at 120-192 h postinjection. Biodistribution of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani closely mirrored that of [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani across organs and tumors, with tumor uptake reduced approximately 5-fold by blocking (21.7 ± 1.1 vs. 4.5 ± 0.6 %IA/g; P < 0.0001), confirming EGFR-specific targeting. A single 9.3 kBq administration of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani induced substantial early tumor regression and significantly prolonged median survival (70 d) compared with vehicle (28 d) and blocking (35 d) groups (log-rank P < 0.0001), with no clinically meaningful hepatotoxicity or renal toxicity. However, tumor regrowth eventually occurred in all treated mice. Conclusion: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani represent a radiotheranostic pair that enables EGFR-specific imaging and targeted α-particle therapy in orthotopic HCC models. These findings establish EGFR as a promising radiotheranostic target in HCC, broadening the patient population eligible for image-guided radiopharmaceutical interventions for liver cancer.

title: Intraoperative artificial intelligence for brain tumor surgery: from tissue diagnosis to real-time surgical guidance.
abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. Yet, in clinical practice the molecular information that matters most to a surgeon-IDH status, 1p/19q codeletion, and methylation class-typically arrives days to weeks after the operation it was meant to inform. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to close that gap. Over the past several years, a growing body of work has demonstrated that AI models can extract diagnostically relevant molecular and histological information from data sources available in the operating room, in real time, at the point of surgical decision-making. In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art intraoperative AI models available to neurosurgeons during brain tumor resections. They examine AI-augmented approaches to established intraoperative techniques, such as cryosection and fluorescence-guided surgery, before turning to novel technologies including nanopore sequencing and stimulated Raman histology (SRH). The authors conclude by discussing barriers to widespread clinical adoption and what lies ahead for this field. For cryosection, models such as LGNet and the Cryosection Histopathology Assessment and Review Machine (CHARM) have demonstrated strong performance on intraoperative discrimination of primary CNS lymphoma and molecular subtyping of glioma, respectively, with CHARM achieving areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88-0.93 across glioma subtypes. In fluorescence-guided surgery, hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning has enabled classification of tumor type, grade, and IDH mutation based on the 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) signal with up to 93% accuracy, extracting molecular information from a modality already present in the operating room. For nanopore-based methylation classification, ensemble models such as Rapid Nanopore Brain Intraoperative Classification (ROBIN) have achieved 90% concordance with the final diagnosis prospectively in under 2 hours. In SRH, foundation models for infiltration detection now outperform FLAIR, contrast enhancement, and 5-ALA fluorescence in identifying tumor margins, while molecular classification models have achieved over 90% glioma subtype accuracy in multi-institutional cohorts. At the single-cell level, morphometric profiling of SRH images has revealed nuclear features distinguishing IDH-mutant from IDH-wildtype tumors, opening new avenues for interpretability. Despite this progress, widespread adoption remains limited by the absence of randomized clinical trials demonstrating patient-level benefit. Addressing this gap and realizing the potential of multimodal AI systems that integrate imaging, pathology, and molecular data represent critical next steps for the field.

title: Sequential arterial feeder targeting with microscope-based augmented reality and multimodal navigation for brain arteriovenous malformation resection: an integrated operative workflow in 158 cases.
abstract: Objective Early proximal arterial control is an established principle of brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM) microsurgery but remains difficult to execute when feeding arteries are deep, obscured, or not apparent at the cortical surface. Herein, the authors describe the longitudinal clinical implementation of a workflow using multimodal navigation and microscope-based augmented reality (AR) to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection in bAVM resections. Methods Case-specific multimodal datasets were assembled according to clinical relevance and availability from CTA, high-resolution structural MRI with thin-slice T2-weighted imaging, MRA, and 3D rotational DSA studies and were fused within standard clinical neuronavigation platforms. All angiographically identifiable arterial feeders were segmented along their surgically relevant courses, prioritized as operative targets, and incorporated into exposure and corridor planning. Targets were displayed intraoperatively using the available navigation configuration, including microscope-based AR as the technology evolved. Functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were coregistered selectively to provide cortical and tractographic context. Consecutive navigation-assisted bAVM resections performed by a single neurosurgeon from 2013 to 2025 were analyzed. Outcomes included angiographic obliteration, perioperative morbidity, mortality, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score change relative to baseline. Results Of 192 bAVM resections performed during the study period, 158 consecutive navigation-assisted resections comprised the analytical cohort and included Spetzler-Martin (SM) grades I-V. Complete obliteration on initial angiography after microsurgery was observed in 97.5% of cases (154/158). At a median follow-up of 15 months, 93.0% of patients were functionally independent (mRS score 0-2). An increase in the mRS score relative to baseline occurred in 18.4% of patients, most commonly reflecting minor, nondisabling deficits with preserved independence. Loss of independence attributable to surgery occurred in 3.1% of patients, and the mortality rate was 1.3%. Conclusions Multimodal navigation with microscope-based AR was implemented longitudinally to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection, with selective integration of fMRI and DTI providing cortical and tractographic context for lesions near eloquent anatomy. Across SM grade I-V bAVMs, the workflow was feasible and was associated with high rates of angiographic obliteration and functional independence. By translating preoperative angioarchitecture into a planned sequence of discrete intraoperative arterial targets within their structural and functional context, the featured workflow provides a structured framework for operative planning, execution, and teaching in feeder-directed bAVM microsurgery.

title: First reported case of intradural extramedullary epithelioid hemangioma of the cauda equina: resection of an extremely rare vascular neoplasm. Illustrative case.
abstract: Background Intradural extramedullary (IDEM) tumors of the cauda equina are most often meningiomas, nerve sheath tumors, and myxopapillary ependymomas; purely vascular IDEM lesions are exceptionally rare. Fewer than 30 IDEM hemangiomas have been reported, mostly cavernous or capillary. Epithelioid hemangioma (EH), a benign vascular neoplasm arising in soft tissue and bone, has not previously been reported at the cauda equina. Observations A 63-year-old male with prior cutaneous melanoma presented with 3 months of progressive left L5-distribution radicular pain. MRI showed a 1.0 × 2.0-cm well-circumscribed IDEM mass at L4-5 with left L5-S1 foraminal stenosis. Under intraoperative ultrasound localization and continuous multimodal neurophysiological monitoring, en bloc gross-total resection was achieved through L4-5 laminectomy. Background

Intradural extramedullary (IDEM) tumors of the cauda equina are most often meningiomas, nerve sheath tumors, and myxopapillary ependymomas; purely vascular IDEM lesions are exceptionally rare. Fewer than 30 IDEM hemangiomas have been reported, mostly cavernous or capillary. Epithelioid hemangioma (EH), a benign vascular neoplasm arising in soft tissue and bone, has not previously been reported at the cauda equina.

Observations

A 63-year-old male with prior cutaneous melanoma presented with 3 months of progressive left L5-distribution radicular pain. MRI showed a 1.0 × 2.0-cm well-circumscribed IDEM mass at L4-5 with left L5-S1 foraminal stenosis. Under intraoperative ultrasound localization and continuous multimodal neurophysiological monitoring, en bloc gross-total resection was achieved through L4-5 laminectomy. Histopathological analysis revealed a well-circumscribed vascular neoplasm with lobular endothelial architecture and no cytological atypia; immunohistochemical analysis (ERG, CD31, and CD34 positivity; HHV8, inhibin, and melanocytic marker negativity) established the diagnosis of EH. At the 7-week follow-up, gross-total resection was confirmed on postoperative MRI.

Lessons

To the authors' knowledge, this is the first reported intradural EH at any spinal level. Recognition of epithelioid endothelial morphology combined with a comprehensive vascular and melanocytic immunohistochemistry panel is essential for diagnosis and separates EH from more common intradural vascular differentials. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26857.

title: Quantifying "Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus"-like Brain Morphometry patterns in an Alzheimer's Disease Cohort.
abstract: Background and purpose Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is largely underdiagnosed. It is a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive decline, and cognitive improvement may occur even with comorbid Alzheimer's disease. However, iNPH-related imaging features can overlap with age-related and neurodegenerative atrophy, making differentiation difficult. Automated morphometric profiling of NPH-like patterns in biomarker-defined Alzheimer's disease cohorts has not been systematically explored. This pilot study aimed to quantify iNPH-like brain morphometry in an Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort using deep-learning-based morphometry and automated callosal angle measurement. Materials and methods We included N=30 amyloid-negative reference iNPH patients and N=1003 ADNI participants with structural T1-weighted MRI and CSF biomarkers. Age- and sex-adjusted volumetric z-scores were obtained using a deep-learning-based morphometry algorithm. We derived an iNPH morphometric profile using principal component analysis and Gaussian modeling of the reference iNPH cohort and applied it to the ADNI participants to compute individual iNPH similarity scores. We also automated callosal angle measurement for further clinical representation. We compared scores across cognitive stages and biological Alzheimer's disease groups and evaluated against expert Radscale review. Results iNPH-like morphometry increased with cognitive impairment, with mean differences of 0.03 between cognitively normal and mild cognitive impairment (p=0.06), 0.06 between mild cognitive impairment and dementia (p<0.001), and 0.09 between cognitively normal and dementia groups (p<0.001). Among cognitively impaired participants, scores were higher in biologically-defined Alzheimer's disease patients than biologically-defined non-Alzheimer's disease patients (mean difference=0.08, p<0.001). The iNPH similarity score correlated most strongly with ventricular enlargement features. Automated callosal angle measurements showed high agreement with expert ratings (Gwet's AC1 = 0.939) and angles below 90° occurred in 1.5% of ADNI participants. Conclusions Automated normative morphometric profiling and callosal angle quantification identified heterogeneous iNPH-like structural patterns in the ADNI cohort. These tools provide a scalable approach for characterizing iNPH-like imaging features in dementia cohorts where identifying a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive impairment remains relevant. Further clinical validation remains necessary.

title: Venous Outflow Imaging in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An ASFNR State of Practice.
abstract: Background Venous outflow (VO) imaging describes the egress limb of the cerebral collateral circulation and has been associated with outcome in acute ischemic stroke; its added value beyond arterial collaterals and perfusion measures remains uncertain. More than a dozen VO measures have been proposed on CT and MR techniques used in acute stroke, spanning three physical signals: venous opacification, venous transit and venous oxygenation. They differ in what they measure, in evidence maturity and in readiness for reporting. Methods A writing group reviewed the peer-reviewed studies of cerebral venous drainage measures in acute ischemic stroke. The scope is CT and MRI obtained during routine acute stroke evaluation, excluding measures that require catheter angiography or ultrasound. We describe each measure's acquisition, definition, evidence and technical limitations, and propose a reporting framework based on these features. Key message VO markers are descriptive prognostic measures, not treatment-selection criteria. The cortical vein opacification score (COVES) has the most mature CTA evidence and may be considered when venous timing is adequate, though meta-analyses support an association rather than a threshold; comprehensive venous outflow (CVO) adds the internal cerebral vein. Prolonged venous transit (PVT) adds a temporal dimension read from perfusion, but remains investigational, as do the composite arterial-venous scores, quantitative venous timing and oxygen extraction fraction mapping. Susceptibility signs index deoxygenation and venous blood volume, not drainage. Reporting should name the technique and describe opacification, transit or oxygenation findings in their own terms. The evidence base is predominantly anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion imaged before thrombectomy.
