title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
abstract: Objective This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR. Materials and methods A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR. Results Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia. Conclusion Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

title: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n =46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n =46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO 2 ) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO 2 )<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T 0 ), upon endoscope insertion (T 1 ), 5 minutes post-insertion (T 2 ), at the end of surgery (T 3 ), and 5 minutes after waking up (T 4 ). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T 2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P >0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46), χ 2 =14.829, P <0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO 2 levels at T 1 , T 2 , and T 3 (all P <0.05). At T 2 , Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO 2 and lower PaCO 2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower ( P <0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval ( P >0.05). Intraoperative PetCO 2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P <0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

title: A Repeatable CT-Based Protocol for Nasal Cavity Volumetry and Choanal Airway Classification in Pediatric Syndromic Craniosynostosis.
abstract: Syndromic craniosynostosis (SC), such as Apert and Crouzon syndromes, causes midface hypoplasia that severely limits nasal cavity development. A computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric protocol for nasal cavity volumetry and choanal airway classification in pediatric SC patients, using landmark-based image segmentation software, is described and tested for intra-rater reproducibility. The protocol was applied to 10 SC patients (5 Apert, 5 Crouzon; 2-48 months; paired pre-/postoperative CT) and 10 reference children (60-168 months), not age-matched because CT is rarely indicated in healthy children. Intra-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.987 and 0.909; 95% CI 0.934-0.997 and 0.689-0.976). Preoperative nasal cavity volume was significantly lower in SC patients (median 2,063.77 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 1,275.53-3,457.18) than in the reference group (median 35,502.13 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 28,811.21-39,167.15) (Mann-Whitney U = 0.000, Z = -3.780, p < 0.001). Nasal cavity volume increased between the paired CT scans in nine of ten patients (Wilcoxon Z = -2.701, p = 0.007; difference in medians +1,584.25 mm 3 ; +76.8%), remaining at only 10.3% of the reference group median postoperatively. A weighted regression sensitivity analysis (log[Volume] vs log[Age], w = 1/Age; n = 10), accounting for the age disparity between cohorts, yielded an exploratory, model-based, non-normative estimate of 7,580 mm 3 at the SC median age (8.5 months), extrapolated below the reference group age range; the SC median represented 27.2% of this estimate. Preoperative volume varied descriptively by choanal category (normal, stenosis, atresia) without tracking narrowing severity, possibly reflecting global hypoplasia; small subgroups precluded inferential testing. Nasal cavity volume is an anatomical measure and does not by itself indicate functional airway obstruction. The protocol offers a standardized workflow for larger, age-matched multicenter studies.

title: The Effect of Alzheimer's Disease and Diabetes on the Volume of Brain Structures.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are increasingly prevalent chronic disorders with overlapping effects on brain structure. However, direct volumetric comparisons among patients with AD alone, DM alone, both conditions, and healthy controls remain limited. This retrospective study compared regional brain volumes in 160 adults (18-90 years) assigned equally to four groups (n = 40 each): AD+type 1 DM, AD-only, type 1 DM-only, and healthy controls. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were analyzed using VolBrain, an automated, multiatlas, patch-based segmentation platform, on 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) images acquired at 1.5 T. Regions evaluated included white and gray matter, subcortical structures, selected cortical gyri, and the ventricular system. Analyses were stratified by sex. No significant volumetric differences were observed between the AD+DM and AD-only groups. Compared with DM-only, differences were limited to the right amygdala (p = 0.004) and left thalamus (p = 0.001) in females. Relative to controls, both AD groups showed reductions in the bilateral amygdala, bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and middle temporal gyrus, together with third-ventricle enlargement (all p ≤ 0.005). The DM-only group showed fewer abnormalities. Reduced left caudate volume was the only finding consistently observed across all patient groups and both sexes (p ≤ 0.007). Overall, AD and DM showed partially overlapping regional differences in brain volume. The consistent left caudate reduction may represent a shared structural marker and warrants further prospective and longitudinal investigation in AD-DM comorbidity.

title: Percutaneous Transhepatic Cholangioscopy: Technical Evolution and Expanding Clinical Roles.
abstract: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangioscopy (PTCS) has evolved from a niche diagnostic technique into an increasingly versatile platform for managing complex biliary diseases, particularly in patients with surgically altered anatomy or failed conventional endoscopic access. Early applications were limited by suboptimal visualization, rigid instrumentation, and procedural complexity. Refinements in endoscopic design and percutaneous techniques now support direct intraductal visualization and targeted intervention through a transhepatic tract. Recent developments include digital single-operator systems, scope miniaturization, and dedicated therapeutic accessories. These advances facilitate targeted biopsy and lithotripsy, although comparative evidence for improved diagnostic accuracy, safety, or patient-centered outcomes remains limited. Relevant literature was identified through a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE search through October 17, 2026, and reference-list screening, with bibliographic verification in Crossref. This narrative review distinguishes PTCS-specific evidence from peroral and mixed-access cholangioscopy studies and summarizes representative clinical outcomes. Technical success, diagnostic yield, malignancy-discrimination accuracy, and therapeutic success are considered separately. The review also addresses collaboration with interventional radiology, access selection, staged versus single-session procedures, drainage management, and alternative treatment pathways. Existing evidence remains heterogeneous in procedural indications, outcome definitions, adverse-event reporting, and device generations. Three-dimensional reconstruction has limited comparative clinical data, whereas the cited artificial intelligence application is a peroral feasibility report without established PTCS benefit. This synthesis aims to clarify the current role of PTCS in hepatobiliary practice and identify priorities for technique standardization, safety reporting, and prospective comparative validation.

title: Host Fitness in Gastrointestinal Oncology: Beyond Tumor Biology.
abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancers face site-specific threats to nutritional intake, muscle function, organ reserve, and recovery. This critical narrative review examines host fitness as an organizing concept for these vulnerabilities rather than as a validated composite score. A targeted PubMed update identified publications from 2022 through September 14, 2026, using gastrointestinal cancer terms combined with prehabilitation, microbiome-immunotherapy, geriatric assessment, exercise, and digital assessment terms, while retaining relevant foundational studies. The review distinguishes guideline-supported care from prognostic associations and research-stage applications. Geriatric and nutritional assessments can guide established supportive care, whereas computed tomography-derived body composition and inflammatory indices primarily provide prognostic information. Microbiome signatures, epigenetic clocks, and integrated digital models require further validation before they can guide treatment decisions. Intervention effects vary by tumor site and treatment phase: selected prehabilitation trials demonstrate short-term benefits, although findings remain inconsistent, while long-term exercise after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer represents a distinct evidence base. An operational assessment protocol and multidisciplinary workflow are presented to link documented impairments with existing care pathways and repeated assessment. No host-fitness threshold is proposed for treatment escalation, de-escalation, or sequencing. Prospective studies should establish incremental predictive value and patient benefit beyond existing assessments before this integrated framework is used to support precision treatment decisions.

title: Application of Explainable Machine Learning for Individualized Risk Stratification and Surgical Optimization in Geriatric Intertrochanteric Fractures.
abstract: Mechanical failure remains a critical complication in the fixation of intertrochanteric fractures. While the Tip-Apex Distance (TAD) is a well-established prognostic metric, the independent biomechanical impact of the nail entry point remains controversial due to confounding surgical variables. This study aimed to evaluate the stability offered by a medialized entry point using interpretable machine learning. A retrospective cohort of 628 patients treated with cephalomedullary nailing was analyzed. A Random Forest model was developed using 12 clinical and radiographic variables to predict implant failure. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to disentangle confounding factors and visualize non-linear interactions between the entry-point strategy and TAD. The medialized entry point group exhibited a significantly lower failure rate compared to the standard group (25.3% vs. 44.2%; p < 0.001). The predictive model demonstrated robust performance (AUC: 0.877) on an independent testing set. Crucially, SHAP interaction analysis revealed a "buffering" effect: while risk profiles were comparable at optimal TAD levels, the medialized trajectory significantly attenuated the probability of failure when the TAD exceeded 25 mm, potentially mitigating the increased risk associated with suboptimal screw placement. The findings identify the medialized entry point as a significant independent predictor of success, increasing the biomechanical tolerance of the fixation construct. This surgical modification offers a valuable safety margin, particularly in cases where anatomical reduction or ideal screw positioning is challenging.

title: A Digital Clinician-Technician Collaborative Workflow for Complete-Arch Implant Rehabilitation in Edentulous Patients.
abstract: This case report describes a digital clinician-technician collaborative workflow for complete-arch implant rehabilitation in a 70-year-old woman with severe periodontitis and compromised dentition. The workflow integrated clinical examination, cone-beam computed tomography, intraoral and facial scanning, mandibular movement records, virtual treatment planning, guided implant placement, and computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing. Digital data sharing facilitated communication between the clinician and dental technician throughout surgical and prosthetic procedures. Following the extraction of compromised teeth, implants were placed using digitally designed surgical guides, and implant positions were recorded with scan bodies to fabricate an immediate provisional restoration. After six months, a definitive one-piece all-ceramic implant-supported prosthesis was digitally designed and fabricated. Clinical assessment demonstrated a stable prosthetic fit, acceptable occlusion, and no major complications during follow-up. This case illustrates a reproducible, digitally coordinated approach to integrating clinical and laboratory procedures in complete-arch implant rehabilitation, while acknowledging the limitations inherent in a single-patient case report and the need for further clinical validation.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Automated Measurement of the Anterior Segment by Ultrasound Biomicroscopy in ICL Calculation.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the agreement between an artificial intelligence-based automated system and manual ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) measurements of anterior segment parameters relevant to Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL; STAAR Surgical) planning. Methods This cross-sectional, observational, and analytical study was conducted at a tertiary referral ophthalmology center in Mexico City, Mexico. A total of 400 ultrasound biomicroscopy images of the anterior segment corresponding to one image per patient were used to generate segmentation masks and train a U-Net-based automated measurement model. An independent test dataset consisting of 40 UBM images from 40 different patients, not included in the training dataset, was used for model evaluation. Dataset splitting was performed at the patient level to avoid data leakage. Automated measurements of anterior chamber depth (ACD), angle-to-angle distance (ATA), sulcus-to-sulcus distance (STS), ciliary body inner diameter (CBID), and sulcus-to-sulcus lens rise (SSLR) were compared with manual measurements performed by an experienced ocular ultrasonographer. Results Automated measurements showed good to excellent agreement with manual measurements for ACD, ATA, STS, and CBID (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]: 0.891 to 0.994). In contrast, SSLR demonstrated moderate agreement (ICC: 0.680 to 0.810). Bland-Altman analysis showed minimal bias and no evidence of proportional error across parameters. Conclusions The artificial intelligence model demonstrated good agreement with manual measurements for most anterior segment parameters, with variable performance across parameters. These findings support the potential role of automated UBM-based measurements as an adjunctive tool for anatomical assessment in ICL planning. Further studies are warranted to determine its impact on ICL sizing decisions and postoperative outcomes.

title: Ultrasound Biomicroscopic Features of Ciliary Epithelial Detachment in Bilateral Hypotony: A Novel Diagnosis.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical and ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) features of a previously unreported entity, ciliary epithelial detachment, in a patient with metastatic melanoma treated with nivolumab and presenting with bilateral hypotony. Visual acuity was 0.6 logMAR in the right eye and 1.3 logMAR in the left, with intraocular pressures of 7 mmHg in the right eye and 5 mmHg in the left. UBM revealed abnormal ciliary body morphology with truncation of ciliary processes and a distinct separation at the level of the ciliary epithelium in both eyes, most prominent inferotemporally. No evidence of fibrovascular proliferation or tractional distortion suggestive of cyclitic membrane was identified. These findings suggest a novel imaging phenotype: a ciliary epithelial detachment. Recognition of this entity may improve interpretation of anterior segment imaging in hypotony and refine diagnostic classification of ciliary body pathology.

title: Correlation of Spectral Doppler Indices of Superior Thyroid Artery and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Values in Benign and Malignant Thyroid Nodules in a Tertiary Level Hospital.
abstract: Background Thyroid nodules are common in clinical practice, with a small but significant proportion harboring malignancy. Conventional ultrasonography has limitations in differentiating benign from malignant nodules. Advanced imaging techniques such as spectral Doppler ultrasonography and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements may improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim The study aimed to assess the role of spectral Doppler ultrasound values of the superior thyroid artery in thyroid nodules and correlating with ADC values using diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) to differentiate benign and malignant thyroid nodules. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Radiology, ACS Medical College and Hospital, Chennai, from November 2023 to November 2024. Forty-two patients aged 18-70 years with suspected thyroid nodules were included using purposive sampling. Spectral Doppler ultrasonography was performed to assess pulsatility index (PI) and resistive index (RI), followed by DW-MRI using a 1.5 Tesla Siemens Magnetom Essenza scanner for ADC value measurement. Histopathology served as the reference standard. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26.0, with independent t-test and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis; P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The majority of participants were females (71.4%) and belonged to the 41-50 years of age group (31.0%). Malignant nodules demonstrated significantly higher PI (1.30 vs. 0.87; P = 0.04) and RI (0.80 vs. 0.60; P = 0.02), along with significantly lower ADC values at b = 0 and b = 1000 s/mm2 (P < 0.05). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance with area under the curve values of 0.974 for ADC (b0), 0.984 for ADC (b1000), 0.993 for PI, and 0.978 for RI. Conclusion Spectral Doppler indices and ADC values are reliable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for differentiating benign from malignant thyroid nodules, with high diagnostic accuracy. Their combined use can enhance early diagnosis and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Clinical Spectrum of Young-onset Hypertension: Diverse Etiologies, Target-organ Damage, and Diagnostic Challenges - A Seven-case Series.
abstract: Young-onset hypertension - defined as sustained blood pressure elevation presenting before the age of 40 years - is increasingly encountered in tertiary care settings in India. Unlike hypertension in older adults, it frequently harbors secondary etiologies, presents with severe target-organ damage, and poses considerable diagnostic challenges. This case series illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of the condition and highlights the importance of systematic evaluation in this population. We report seven cases (age range 19-38 years; six males, one female) presenting to a tertiary care teaching hospital. Secondary etiologies included biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with nephrotic-range proteinuria (Case 1), bilateral ostial renal artery stenosis complicated by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (Case 2), and hypertension associated with erythrocytosis under evaluation (Case 6). Hypertensive emergency with acute ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic transformation, complicated by hypertensive dilated cardiomyopathy, occurred in Case 7. Essential hypertension was established in Cases 3-5, with end-organ manifestations including hypomagnesemia-induced ventricular premature complexes (Case 4) and hypertensive retinopathy (Case 5). Diagnostic investigations included renal biopsy, renal Doppler ultrasonography, renal angiography, 24-h Holter monitoring, serum erythropoietin assay, and brain magnetic resonance imaging. Individualized antihypertensive regimens were supplemented by disease-specific interventions. Outcomes ranged from clinical stabilization to partial neurological recovery, reflecting the variable prognosis associated with delayed diagnosis and inadequate treatment. Young-onset hypertension is not a uniformly benign or essential condition. Systematic evaluation for secondary causes and comprehensive assessment of target-organ damage are critical, particularly in resource-limited settings where these steps are frequently deferred.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using Clinical and Computed Tomography Markers: A Prospective Study.
abstract: Background Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represents a disproportionately high stroke burden (20%-30%) in low- and middle-income countries like India, necessitating accurate, early risk stratification using readily available clinical and radiographic features. Materials and methods This prospective observational study included 185 patients with spontaneous ICH at a tertiary care center. Baseline clinical severity was assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and the ICH score. Radiographic markers included hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and radiographic signs (swirl, blend, black hole, satellite, and spot signs). The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status (modified Rankin scale: 4-6, including mortality) at 90 days. Univariate analyses focused on identifying predictors associated with a poor outcome, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results The mean age was 56.0 ± 12.4 years, with 72.4% prevalence of hypertension. The unfavorable outcome rate was 37.3% (N = 69), with 22.2% mortality. Univariate analysis (P < 0.05) revealed strong associations between poor outcome and greater hematoma volume, lower GCS score, higher ICH score, IVH, swirl sign, blend sign, satellite sign, hydrocephalus, herniation, and ≥2 multiple noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) signs. Multivariable analysis identified hematoma volume, GCS score, ICH score, herniation, satellite sign, and male gender as independent predictors. Conclusion Clinical severity indicators and multiple NCCT signs in univariate analysis serve as robust markers of poor functional outcome. The independent prognostic value of the satellite sign and herniation highlights the utility of readily available radiographic features for immediate risk stratification.

title: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging in locally advanced prostate cancer: the radiologist's perspective on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment.
abstract: Clinically locally advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is usually defined as cT3-T4 disease with or without regional nodal involvement. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is still the reference examination for local T staging because it combines high-resolution anatomic evaluation with functional information from diffusion-weighted imaging and, when performed, dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. Its main strengths are the depiction of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, apical or bladder-neck involvement, and the delivery of side-specific information that surgeons and radiation oncologists need for planning. Its main limitation is reduced sensitivity for focal microscopic extension and for nodal metastases, for which prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) is more sensitive. In current practice, mpMRI and PSMA PET/CT therefore play complementary rather than competing roles: mpMRI defines the local extent of disease, whereas PSMA PET/CT refines nodal and distant staging. Beyond initial staging, mpMRI also contributes to surgical evaluation, radiotherapy target delineation, adaptive replanning after androgen deprivation therapy, and the detection of recurrence after treatment. Interpretation after hormonal therapy, surgery, or radiotherapy, however, requires awareness of treatment-related signal changes and of the risk of both under- and overcalling recurrence. This narrative review summarizes the radiologist's perspective on how mpMRI should be performed, interpreted, and reported in clinically locally advanced PCa. Particular emphasis is placed on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment within a multimodality imaging pathway.

title: Outcome of Children Treated with Rituximab for Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome: Renal Histopathology as a Response Marker.
abstract: Background Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) in children remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) are commonly used as first-line therapy, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission, and prolonged use may result in nephrotoxicity. Rituximab has emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory SRNS; however, treatment responses appear variable, and the influence of underlying renal histopathology remains incompletely understood. Objectives To evaluate the association between renal histopathological findings and clinical response to rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS). Methods Study Design and Setting:This prospective observational study was conducted between 2011 and 2020 at a university-affiliated tertiary pediatric nephrology center. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) and to examine the association between renal histopathological findings and treatment response. Twenty-four children aged 2-12 years were enrolled.Follow-up:Patients were followed prospectively after completion of rituximab therapy through regular clinical and laboratory assessments. The mean follow-up duration after the last rituximab infusion was 5.1 years (range: 6 months-8 years).Treatment Response Definitions:Complete remission was defined according to International Pediatric Nephrology Association (IPNA) recommendations as a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) ≤20 mg/mmol (≤0.2 mg/mg) or negative/trace proteinuria on dipstick testing on at least three consecutive occasions.Partial remission was defined as a UPCR >20 mg/mmol but <200 mg/mmol together with serum albumin ≥30 g/L.No response was defined as failure to achieve either complete or partial remission.Genetic Evaluation:Genetic testing was performed in all patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), classic minimal change disease (MCD), and MCD with IgM deposition. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome were identified in the tested patients. Genetic testing was not performed in patients with IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, C1q nephropathy, or dense deposit disease. Results Twenty-four children with SRNS were included (13 males and 11 females; age range 2-12 years). Histopathological diagnoses included focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) in 9 patients (37.5%), minimal change disease (MCD) in 4 (16.7%), MCD with IgM deposition in 6 (25.0%), dense deposit disease in 2 (8.3%), membranous nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), IgA nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), and C1q nephropathy in 1 (4.2%). Overall, 10 patients (41.7%) achieved complete remission and 3 (12.5%) achieved partial remission, predominantly among patients with MCD and MCD with IgM deposition. Responses were uncommon among patients with FSGS. Eleven patients (45.8%), all of whom were non-responders, progressed to end-stage kidney disease. No major adverse effects of rituximab were observed; mild infusion reactions occurred in three patients and mild cellulitis in one patient. Conclusion In this cohort of children with refractory SRNS, favorable responses to rituximab were observed predominantly among patients with CNI- resistant MCD and MCD with IgM deposition, whereas responses among patients with FSGS were uncommon. These findings suggest that renal histopathology may help identify patients more likely to benefit from rituximab therapy; however, the small sample size, heterogeneous histopathological distribution, and observational study design preclude definitive conclusions. Larger prospective multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive genetic evaluation are required to determine whether histopathology can serve as a reliable predictor of rituximab responsiveness.

title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
abstract: Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). Aims We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. Methods Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index. Results Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). Conclusions Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. title: Magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction and selected quantitative ultrasound methods for hepatic steatosis: histology-referenced diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To synthesize histology-referenced diagnostic performance at study-selected thresholds and the longitudinal responsiveness of magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and selected quantitative ultrasound methods in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Methods Four databases were searched from database inception through July 1, 2026. Sensitivity, specificity, and odds ratios were pooled with 95% confidence intervals using heterogeneity-selected fixed- or random-effects models. Small-study effects were assessed using funnel plots and Begg tests; longitudinal changes were pooled when change-score standard deviations were reported. Results In total, 44 articles were included: 34 contributed histology-referenced diagnostic data, and 11 were assessed for longitudinal responsiveness, with 1 article contributing to both. At steatosis grade (S) ≥ 1/S ≥ 2/S ≥3, MRI-PDFF sensitivity and specificity was 93.6%/81.5%/83.1% and 87.1%/86.7%/83.2%, respectively; the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) was 86.8%/81.2%/86.4% and 98.9%/71.0%/64.6%, respectively. The attenuation coefficient/attenuation imaging sensitivity/specificity was 83.2%/98.1%, 86.4%/79.9%, and 99.3%/76.4%, respectively. Ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter and ultrasound-derived fat fraction evidence was limited. Three head-to-head longitudinal studies included 298 participants, of whom only 158 had analyzable change-score data; in these, pooled changes were -4.53 percentage points for MRI-PDFF and -12.71 dB/m for the CAP. Thirty-two of the 34 diagnostic studies were at high-risk of bias from cohort-selected thresholds. Begg tests did not detect significant small-study effects, although their power was very limited in analyses that included only 2 or 3 studies. Conclusion At study-selected thresholds, MRI-PDFF showed balanced sensitivity and specificity across steatosis grades, whereas quantitative ultrasound varied by method, platform, and threshold. These findings support comparative synthesis but do not establish validated cut-offs or superiority of either modality. Clinical significance Study-selected thresholds limit clinical translation. MRI-PDFF proton density fat fraction and quantitative ultrasound are complementary, with use depending on clinical purpose, platform, and precision needs.

title: Comparative reasoning in radiology artificial intelligence: longitudinal and reference-case approaches.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology remains predominantly examination-centric, whereas clinical interpretation frequently depends on comparison across time or with relevant prior cases. This narrative review examines comparative reasoning in radiology AI through two related but clinically distinct forms: longitudinal reasoning, which compares examinations from the same patient over time, and reference-case reasoning, which uses clinically analogous cases from other patients to support interpretation. We propose a capability hierarchy that distinguishes simple access to comparative information from higher-level capabilities, including selection of relevant historical context, anatomical and lesion-level correspondence, characterization of interval change, temporal-state interpretation, multi-interval trajectory reasoning, and entity-specific assessment of clinical similarity. This distinction matters because providing prior examinations or retrieving visually similar cases does not itself demonstrate meaningful comparative reasoning. We review developments in prior-examination selection, registration, lesion tracking, temporal vision-language modeling, treatment-response assessment, analogous-case retrieval, and longitudinal report generation. Particular emphasis is placed on evaluation strategies that determine whether model performance depends appropriately on clinically relevant comparative information rather than on additional input volume, global image similarity, acquisition characteristics, or other shortcuts. Key challenges include incorrect prior selection, lesion mismatching, temporal inconsistency, clinically irrelevant reference-case retrieval, data leakage, misleading comparative language, and propagation of historical errors. Future progress will require models that preserve entity identity, reason coherently across multi-visit imaging histories, identify clinically informative reference cases, and demonstrate benefit under realistic clinical conditions. Comparative reasoning is therefore a necessary step in the transition from examination-level toward patient-level radiology AI.

title: Treatment-Response Evidence, Care-Pathway Gaps, and Guideline Discordance in Gastric MALT Lymphoma: An Umbrella Review.
abstract: Background/aims Reviews of gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma have quantified treatment response, but their coverage of the care pathway and relationship to guideline differences remain unclear. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 31, 2026. Eligible reviews were mapped to 13 clinical questions as direct, partial, or absent coverage. Question-specific anchors were selected without pooling overlapping reviews. All 16 items of A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews, version 2 were examined; overall confidence was assigned to intervention reviews. European Gastro-Intestinal Lymphoma Study, European Society for Medical Oncology, National Comprehensive Cancer Network, and British Society for Haematology recommendations were compared descriptively. Results Fifteen reviews were eligible; nine reviews answered seven questions. Complete remission was 75.2% after successful Helicobacter pylori eradication in H. pylori -positive disease. In H. pylori -negative disease, source-defined complete remission was 29.3%, including probable minimal residual disease. Remission was 22.2% in patients with t(11;18)/ BIRC3::MALT1 -positive disease versus 78.0% in patients with translocation-negative disease. The radiotherapy remission estimates were 97.3% after eradication failure and 96.0% in the limited-stage cohort. Gastric positron emission tomography (PET) detection was 62.0%, without evidence of management benefit. All eight intervention reviews had critically low confidence; seven nonintervention reviews received descriptive profiles. The guidelines differed for H. pylori -negative management, endoscopic ultrasonography, bone marrow biopsy, and PET/computed tomography. No eligible review compared the relevant treatment sequences or staging strategies. Conclusions Review-level evidence is concentrated on treatment response. It cannot establish superiority between treatment sequences or determine staging, escalation timing, surveillance, or relapse strategies. Guideline differences concern decisions for which the relevant comparisons remain unsynthesized.

title: Non-nutritional rickets: Approach, precision medicine, and outcomes.
abstract: Rickets are chronic bone disorders marked by impaired mineralization of the growing skeleton. While most cases arise from nutritional deficiencies, non-nutritional forms are frequently underrecognized. Subtle signs such as alopecia in vitamin D dependent rickets type 2A, cataract in Lowe syndrome, dental abscesses or sensorineural hearing loss in X-linked hypophosphatemia can prompt timely diagnosis and referral. A structured approach combining growth and skeletal assessment, targeted biochemistry (calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, parathyroid hormone, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), radiography, and early genetic testing once nutritional deficiency or renal failure are excluded improves diagnostic accuracy. Molecular confirmation enables precise subclassification into hypophosphatemic and calciopenic rickets, supporting genotype-directed therapy, including burosumab for X-linked hypophosphatemia. Early, tailored treatment enhances radiographic healing, growth, and function. Emerging genotype-phenotype correlations further inform genetic counselling and prognosis, strengthening the multidisciplinary management of these complex disorders.

title: A Primer on Radiomics for the Practicing Orthopaedic Surgeon.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is permeating many aspects of daily life. Medicine, and specifically orthopaedic surgery, is being influenced by the rapid growth and success of AI in serving as an adjunct to medical expertise. AI includes many nested subfields and applications such as computer vision, language models, and predictive analytics. Using standard machine learning methods, clinical decision support tools are being developed for clinicians to provide evidence-based, individualized care. Some models predict clinical and functional outcomes after a procedure, whereas others may incorporate administrative metrics to predict factors, such as length of stay, return to the emergency department, and complications. The application of AI to medical imaging focuses on the extraction of a large amount of quantitative data in the form of predefined features from clinical images that humans cannot perceive, a field known as radiomics. There has been recent interest, particularly in oncology, to apply radiomics to aid in diagnosis and prognostication of outcomes. Given the robust growth of radiomics literature, and the anticipated application in orthopaedic surgery, the purpose of this review article is to educate the orthopaedic surgery community on the practical importance and the basics of radiomics.

title: Unintended coverage: how standard breast radiotherapy irradiates the internal mammary nodes.
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common malignancy in women worldwide. Irradiation of regional nodes, including the internal mammary nodes (IMNs), may improve outcomes, but routine IMN irradiation remains controversial because of toxicity. Modern breast radiotherapy may incidentally irradiate the ipsilateral IMNs. We quantified incidental IMN doses and factors affecting coverage in patients without targeted IMN irradiation. In this retrospective dosimetric study, 104 women with clinical stage I-III disease were analysed. The ipsilateral IMNs (levels I-III) were contoured on planning CT scans according to the RTOG guidelines. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) metrics (minimum, mean, and maximum doses; V95%, V90%, and V50%) were recorded. Group comparisons [mastectomy vs. breast-conserving surgery (BCS) and 3DCRT vs. VMAT)] were performed using statistical tests, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. The median age was 52 years; 56.7% of patients were aged > 50 years; left- and right-sided tumours were equally represented. Seventy-five per cent underwent mastectomy and 25% underwent BCS. Eighty-one per cent received 3DCRT; 46% received supraclavicular/axillary irradiation; the median follow-up was 40 months. The mean IMN volume was 7.30 ± 1.76 cm3. The mean IMN dose was 35.53 ± 6.20 Gy, and the minimum dose was 7.73 ± 6.37 Gy. On average, 47.3% of the IMN volume received ≥ 95% of the prescribed dose. Mastectomy plans delivered a higher mean IMN dose than BCS plans (36.55 vs. 32.48 Gy, p = 0.0046). 3DCRT plans provided better IMN coverage than VMAT plans (mean V95%, 51.4% vs. 29.1%; p = 0.0012). Radiotherapy modality and type of surgery were significant in the multivariate analysis. Standard tangential fields provide only partial IMN coverage with wide variability. Most patients did not reach therapeutic IMN doses, highlighting the need for explicit contouring and dedicated planning when IMN irradiation is indicated.

title: Comparison of extended kV-CBCT image quality between conventional and O-ring linear accelerators.
abstract: In cases of non-central or large tumours, the use of an extended field of view is important for patient positioning or adaptive treatment. The aim of our study was to investigate the longitudinal and lateral consistency of extended kilovoltage cone-beam CT (kV-CBCT) image quality over the entire scan length. The study compared extended kV-CBCT image quality between conventional and O-ring linear accelerators (LINACs) using image quality phantoms. The impact of lateral and longitudinal phantom offsets was analysed across the reconstruction algorithms [filtered back projection - Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) and iterative cone-beam computed tomography (iCBCT)] and imaging protocols. The CT calibration curves showed consistent alignment across LINACs, imaging protocols, longitudinal displacements, and reconstruction algorithms. The average mean difference in the CT numbers measured during longitudinal shifts, averaged over the other material inserts, was 37 ± 15 Hounsfield units (HU). In the homogeneity examination, the lateral inserts displayed signal reductions as they moved away from the isocentre. For an imaging protocol on a ring accelerator, the central insert remained near 8 HU, while the signal of lateral inserts located 20 cm from the isocentre decreased from 0 HU to -160 HU. Our results show that the longitudinal extension does not affect image linearity, making extended CBCT protocols suitable for long target volumes. CBCT-based adaptation may be unsuitable for large lateral or peripheral tumours due to poor image quality. Consequently, the generation of synthetic CTs from peripheral regions of CBCT images should be approached with caution.

title: Dense Breast Tissue Segmentation under Limited Annotation: Comparing CNNs, Transformers, Self-Supervision, and Prompting
abstract: Dense breast tissue reduces the sensitivity of mammographic screening and is an important risk factor for breast cancer, making accurate dense-tissue segmentation particularly important when expert pixel-level annotations are limited. We empirically study dense breast tissue segmentation under limited pixel-level supervision using a small expert-annotated dataset (596 images) together with an in-domain unlabeled mammography dataset (20{,}000 images). We compare classical pixel-level segmentation methods, CNN and U-Net encoder--decoder models, transformer-based models, self-supervised pre-training, fine-tuning strategies, loss functions, and prompt-based MedSAM variants under a unified evaluation protocol. CNN-based models achieve the best standalone segmentation performance while providing the most favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost. In contrast, the adaptive fuzzy c-means + SVM baseline and transformer-based models perform worse in this low-label setting. Our analysis of prompt-based MedSAM further shows that SAM-style models are highly sensitive to prompt quality. Box and breast-region prompts lead to poor performance, whereas CNN-generated dense prompts substantially improve MedSAM performance. However, even with mask-decoder fine-tuning, CNN-prompted MedSAM does not outperform the best standalone CNN model, suggesting that current SAM-style models require stronger prompts or adaptation beyond the mask decoder for diffuse breast-density segmentation. Additionally, a density-calibrated hybrid loss primarily improves percent-density calibration by reducing the test MAE from 14.8 to 11.8 percentage points. Our computational cost analysis indicates that many generic self-supervised learning and parameter-efficient adaptation strategies provide limited practical benefit relative to their additional cost. These findings offer practical guidance for developing reproducible dense breast tissue segmentation models in mammography studies with limited labeled data.

title: ConfUSIus: an accessible and scalable toolkit for functional ultrasound imaging analysis
abstract: Functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) maps brainwide hemodynamics at high resolution, yet analysis requires expert knowledge as pipelines remain fragmented across laboratories. We introduce ConfUSIus, an open-source Python package and graphical interface for accessible, scalable, and reproducible fUSI analysis. Its common data model unifies heterogeneous fUSI recordings across beamformed IQ processing, motion correction, registration, denoising, and statistical analysis. ConfUSIus lowers barriers and facilitates method development, comparison, and sharing.
authorString: Le Meur-Diebolt S, Cybis Pereira F.

title: Cerebrovascular Structure–Flow Gradients Revealed by Volumetric Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
abstract: Characterizing the joint organization of microscale cerebrovascular structure and flow in vivo is challenging. Volumetric ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) provides spatially resolved measures of microvascular structure and flow from the same acquisition, but how these features are jointly organized across brain networks remains unclear. Here, we characterized local vascular phenotypes from transcranial volumetric ULM in mice and examined whether they contained reproducible low-dimensional organization. Local measures of vascular structure and flow dynamics were summarized within corresponding brain regions across mice. Subject-specific vascular phenotype similarity matrices were combined into a group-consensus graph and analyzed using diffusion embedding. Two leading gradients, showing distinct spatial distributions across brain networks, were reproducibly recovered across subject and spatial scales. The principal gradient was associated with local vascular density and flow complexity, defining a vascular structure-related axis. The secondary gradient was associated with flow speed and acceleration, defining a flow-dynamics-related axis. These gradients provide a low-dimensional representation of the cerebrovascular structure and flow and provide a reference for studying coordinated vascular changes across disease, aging, and intervention.

title: Real-time Volumetric Imaging for Minimally-Invasive Thoracic Interventions: A Deformable Phantom Study
abstract: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the ability of VoxelMap, a deep learning framework for 3D respiratory motion estimation, to generate volumetric images in real-time from 2D projections acquired for two deformable lung phantoms on a clinical interventional C-arm angiography system. Materials and MethodsVoxelMap was evaluated using the PixelPrint4D and Casper deformable physical thoracic respiratory phantoms. Four-dimensional cone-beam CT (4D CBCT) images acquired on a clinical fixed-room C-arm angiography system were used for network training and volumetric ground truth. Prediction accuracy was evaluated on withheld respiratory phases using structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Model inference time was measured to assess suitability for continuous real-time processing. Deep ensembles were also used to assess model uncertainty. Correlation between ensemble uncertainty and prediction error was evaluated for both phantoms. ResultsVoxelMap achieved high prediction accuracy across withheld respiratory phases in both physical phantoms. SSIM values exceeded 0.92 in all experiments, with a higher performance observed for the Casper phantom (0.969-0.973) than for the PixelPrint4D phantom (0.927-0.943). Model inference times were less than 15 ms for both phantoms which is compatible with real-time processing. Ensemble uncertainty was positively correlated with prediction error in both phantoms, indicating that higher uncertainty was associated with less accurate volumetric predictions. ConclusionsOur study demonstrated that VoxelMap generates accurate volumetric deformations of respiratory anatomy from projections acquired on a clinical interventional C-arm system, with computational inference times compatible with continuous processing. By deriving volumetric information directly from two-dimensional fluoroscopic projections, VoxelMap has the potential to augment continuous fluoroscopic guidance with continuously updated volumetric information. Ensemble uncertainty may provide a potentially useful indicator of prediction reliability. Further studies using clinically representative training data and patient studies is required to establish clinical utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap.

title: Topographic reference modelling of white matter hyperintensities across the adult lifespan
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are among the most common MRI findings in older adults. They are widely regarded as markers of brain aging and cerebral small-vessel disease, and associated with risk for cognitive decline, Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD), and stroke. White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are typically interpreted by total lesion burden, but lesions with similar volumes can occupy different anatomical locations, potentially reflecting distinct pathological processes. Here we present voxelwise topographic reference modelling (vTRM), a framework for characterizing individual WMH masks against age- and sex-stratified frequency maps derived from cognitively unimpaired individuals. Using 42,469 FLAIR-derived lesion masks from twelve adult cohorts, we mapped population-level WMH spatial vulnerability, characterized age-related changes in its distribution across periventricular, lobar and arterial-territory compartments, and constructed paired percentile charts for lesion burden and spatial typicality. A quadrant-based classification defined by these two percentile dimensions revealed graded relationships with ADRD pathophysiology, neurodegeneration, and cognitive impairment, while identifying WMH patterns differentially associated with ageing-related, vascular and neurodegenerative processes among individuals with similar lesion volumes. These reference charts establish a benchmark for normative WMH ageing, enabling quantification of individual deviations from typical age-, sex- and burden-related patterns and identification of WMH phenotypes associated with vascular, neurodegenerative or mixed etiologies. The framework, together with a deployable 3D U-Net model trained on these data for automated WMH segmentation, is available through the Brain Lesion Analytics platform ( https://brainlesionanalytics.org/ ).

title: Ultradeep optical coherence tomography
abstract: Deep optical imaging of intact brain tissue is limited by scattering and absorption, restricting our ability to study subcortical structures. Here, we introduce ultradeep optical coherence tomography (OCT), which combines hardware and computational approaches to enhance the signal from deep tissue regions. Ultradeep OCT utilizes a longer illumination center wavelength of 1575 nm, spectral-domain balanced detection and imaging in the conjugate configuration with the zero optical path difference positioned deep in the tissue. Autocorrelation artifacts are measured and subtracted, and multiple frames are coherently averaged to improve the signal-to-noise ratio further. These techniques, along with computational refocusing and bandwidth control, allowed us to extend structural imaging depth in biological tissues. Ultradeep OCT demonstrated physical imaging depths of 2.3 to 2.8 mm (mean 2.5 mm) in the ex vivo mouse brain and 2.5 to 3.0 mm (mean 2.8 mm) in chicken tissue. The resulting volumes in the ex vivo mouse brain samples depict the dorsal hippocampus and its two major subregions with sufficient contrast to allow segmentation and three-dimensional reconstructions. Features in the thalamus could also be discerned. These findings demonstrate the potential of ultradeep OCT as a label-free approach for visualizing deep-brain structures at a spatial scale complementary to magnetic resonance imaging and microscopy. This approach could enable optical imaging studies of hippocampal structural changes in mouse models of neurodegenerative disease.

title: Assessment of Dissemination in Time in Multiple Sclerosis Using a Single 3D T2-FLAIR magnetic resonance imaging Radiomic Signature
abstract: Background In multiple sclerosis (MS), dissemination in time (DIT) is an important component of demonstrating disease activity and establishing the chronology of lesion development. DIT is routinely assessed from contrast-enhanced or follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Although proved useful, these methods are not without caveats motivating alternative approaches to study lesion chronology. We investigated whether single T2-FLAIR MRI contains sufficient information to distinguish temporally distinct MS lesion categories using radiomic features. Methods In a retrospective longitudinal cohort of 273 participants, 39.0 (10.8) y; 172/273 female (63.0%); 101/273 male (37.0%) with MS (1,311 MRI acquisitions), persistent brain lesions were temporally stratified using serial T2-FLAIR MRI. Long-standing established (LS-E) lesions were defined as observed for six years at least, and recent incident (R-I), as lesions that appeared over the span of two years in a follow-up MRI and were present until the last scan available. Radiomic features were extracted from lesion-level T2-FLAIR MRI. Feature selection was performed in an independent discovery cohort (Group 1, N=55). Selected features were then used to train a support vector machine classifier in a separate development cohort with repeated group-wise cross-validation (Group 2, N=163). Final performance was assessed in an independent test cohort (Group 3, N=55). An exploratory analysis was then performed on baseline MRI from 64 subjects with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), acquired after their first clinical demyelinating event. Results Group 1 comprised 55 participants with 984 classifiable lesions; paired feature selection was restricted to 32 participants who contributed both lesion categories (658 LS-E and 156 R-I lesions), yielding 18 selected radiomic features. Group 2 comprised 163 participants with 3,203 lesions. In the held-out test cohort, 55 participants contributed 814 lesions (622 LS-E and 192 R-I); the classifier achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.74-0.81). Using the fixed decision threshold, 65% of R-I lesions (125/192; 95% CI, 57%-73%) and 73% of LS-E lesions (457/622; 95% CI, 69%-78%) were correctly classified. Conclusions Single T2-FLAIR MRI contains measurable information related to MS lesion chronology. This proof-of-concept framework supports the feasibility of a line of research based on radiomics temporal lesion characterisation without contrast administration or dense longitudinal follow-up MRI, with potential relevance for studying lesion evolution and supporting DIT assessment.

title: NeuroWeave-3D: Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Completion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities
abstract: Multi-parametric MRI segmentation models are accurate when all prescribed sequences are available but can be brittle under missing or corrupted modalities. We propose NeuroWeave-3D, a 3D glioma segmentation framework that treats missing modalities as uncertain evidence rather than deterministic channels to reconstruct. The model combines spatial modality routing, probabilistic latent feature completion, complete-to-missing consistency, and voxel-level uncertainty estimation. A curriculum over all non-empty MRI modality subsets trains one network for arbitrary sequence availability. We define a BraTS-centered evaluation that reports complete-input accuracy, macro and worst-case missing-modality performance, corruption robustness, calibration, and failure detection.

title: In-vivo MRI of noradrenergic and dopaminergic nuclei predicts future cognition and Alzheimers disease progression
abstract: Noradrenergic and dopaminergic nuclei modulate cognition, and post-mortem data indicate they are affected early in the neurodegenerative cascade of Alzheimers disease. We derived in-vivo locus coeruleus (LC) and substantia nigra-ventral tegmental area (SN-VTA) MRI integrity measures from 739 ADNI participants, examined MRI-histology correspondence in individuals with both in-vivo imaging and post-mortem data, and tested whether these measures reflect early MRI-indexed degeneration predicting later cognitive decline. LC and SN-VTA contrast predicted cognitive and behavioral function 10 years later, despite only weak associations with current function. LC- and SN-VTA-associated brain-wide atrophy patterns aligned with PET-derived norepinephrine-transporter and dopamine-receptor maps, respectively. A one-standard-deviation decrease in baseline LC contrast was associated with 84% higher five-year odds of MCI-to-AD progression, and predictive effects of the catecholaminergic nuclei were mediated by their corresponding atrophy patterns. The SN-VTA pattern was associated with less amyloid PET-related memory decline. Together, these findings establish LC and SN-VTA MRI contrast as markers of early neurodegeneration that forecast cognitive decline years before clinical onset.

title: Agreement of abdominal palpation with point-of-care ultrasound for hepatosplenic organomegaly: a cross-sectional, population-based study in schistosomiasis-endemic settings of rural Uganda
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Ultrasound is commonly used to assess hepatosplenic morbidity in schistosomiasis, but access may be limited in resource-constrained settings. Abdominal palpation is simple and inexpensive, yet its clinical value and diagnostic performance for detecting ultrasound-defined organ enlargement remains uncertain. We evaluated standardised abdominal palpation against point-of-care ultrasound in a schistosomiasis-endemic setting in rural Uganda. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study in January-February 2024 of 3177 participants aged 5-92 years from Pakwach, Buliisa and Mayuge districts in the SchistoTrack cohort. Trained nurses who also had midwifery skills performed standardised liver and spleen palpation, assessing palpability, extension, consistency and tenderness. Palpation agreement was assessed against point-of-care B-mode ultrasound performed by sonographers with organ dimensions classified using height-standardised internal reference values. We estimated sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and Cohen’s κ for palpation against ultrasound-defined liver and spleen enlargement and assessed associations between liver consistency and tenderness, and schistosomal periportal fibrosis examined from ultrasound. Results Spleen palpation had high specificity (98.4%), with sensitivity ranging from 10.9% for moderate splenomegaly to 48.6% for severe splenomegaly. There was strong agreement with ultrasound for severe splenomegaly (κ=0.57) though weak agreement for moderate splenomegaly (κ=0.14). Liver palpation had high specificity (97.7%) but very low sensitivity (3.4-7.3%) and minimal agreement with any hepatomegaly found from ultrasound (κ=0.02-0.04). Among participants with a palpable liver, schistosomal periportal fibrosis was more frequent in those with firm/hard than soft liver consistency (53.3%, n=24/45 vs 8.6%, n=3/35; χ²=17.64, p<0.001); while tenderness was not associated with schistosomal periportal fibrosis. Nurses additionally identified clinically relevant findings, including umbilical collaterals, abdominal swelling, and abdominal or hypochondrial pain and tenderness. Conclusions Standardised abdominal palpation cannot replace ultrasound for comprehensive detection or exclusion of hepatosplenomegaly. Nevertheless, severe ultrasound-defined splenomegaly was more readily detected by palpation, while liver consistency and other clinical findings provided information beyond organomegaly. In schistosomiasis-endemic settings with limited access to ultrasound, further research is needed to assess building capacity for abdominal palpation and how it can be combined with clinical information to increase clinical suspicion while possibly informing low-cost strategies for triage and referral.

title: Ophthalmic AI With Just Ten Examples: Comparing Multimodal Large Language Models, Vision Foundation Models, and Vision-Language Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose To compare multimodal large language models (MLLMs), vision foundation models (VFMs), and contrastive vision-language models (VLMs) for ophthalmic image interpretation with no labeled examples (zero-shot) or as few as 10 labeled examples per class (10-shot). Design Retrospective benchmarking study. Subjects 4 public datasets (UCSD, IDRiD, REFUGE, ASOCT-MSDC) and 3 private datasets (OHTS, BPEI-DLS, WashU-OCT) of anterior-and posterior-segment ophthalmic imaging. Methods Nine AI models were evaluated across 3 architectural families: MLLMs (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemma-4-31B-it), VFMs (DINOv3, RETFound, VisionFM), and VLMs (CLIP, EyeCLIP, SigLIP2). Models were assessed on disease classification, disease risk and severity grading, anatomical assessment, and lesion localization in fundus and OCT imaging. MLLMs were also compared with a 3D VFM (OCTCube-M) for whole-volume OCT classification. MLLMs were evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot, without additional training. Vision models (VFMs and VLMs) were adapted by linear probing and fine-tuning on the same 10-shot set and on the full training dataset (FD). Main Outcome Measures Disease classification performance (macro-averaged F1, AUROC, quadratic weighted kappa [QWK]), anatomical localization accuracy, and cross-dataset generalization. Results For retinal OCT disease classification, 10-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.94, versus 0.59 (10-shot) and 0.96 (FD) for vision models. For diabetic retinopathy and macular edema grading, 10-shot MLLMs achieved QWKs of 0.69 and 0.73, versus 0.48 and 0.57 (10-shot) and 0.72 and 0.79 (FD) for vision models. For lesion localization, 10-shot MLLMs achieved an F1 of 0.75, versus 0.70 (10-shot) and 0.86 (FD) for vision models. For vertical cup-to-disc ratio estimation (OHTS), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a mean absolute error of 0.14, versus 0.21 (10-shot) for vision models. For whole-volume OCT classification (WashU-OCT), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.71, versus 0.50 (10-shot) and 0.82 (FD) for vision models. Conclusions Open-weight MLLMs given 10 labeled examples per class outperformed VFMs and VLMs trained on the same examples in most tasks and approached the performance of fully trained VFMs and VLMs in selected disease classification and grading tasks. MLLMs also demonstrated promising zero-shot performance on non-public clinical datasets without task-specific training. By reducing the need for large labeled datasets and task-specific model adaptation, MLLMs could broaden who can develop and validate ophthalmic AI.

title: Lesion-Derived Estimated Functional and Structural Connectomes Predict Post-Stroke Recovery Outcomes
abstract: Accurate prognosis after stroke remains challenging, limiting the ability to predict individual recovery. While advanced connectome MRI can provide further prognostically-useful information regarding affected brain networks, its impractical nature has given rise instead to lesion-based estimates of network disruptions. Here, we present a novel pipeline that leverages our recently developed connectome analysis tools to estimate structural disconnection (eSDC) and functional connectivity (eFC) directly from N=96 patient lesion masks for use in predicting motor, language, attention and memory outcomes at multiple timepoints after stroke. Our approach jointly leverages our Network Modification (NeMo) Tool, a database of white matter tractography results that estimates structural disconnectivity (eSDC), and the Krakencoder, a joint autoencoder that estimates functional connectomes (eFC) from the NeMo Tool's output. Models based on eSDC and eFC predicted almost all outcomes, particularly motor outcomes, significantly better than models that used patients' fMRI-based observed FC (oFC) and models based on only lesion information and covariates. Estimated connectome measures also i) retained meaningful inter-individual variability when compared to observed functional connectomes, ii) reflected population-level, stroke-related changes in functional connectomes, and iii) resulted in outcome prediction models with feature importances that aligned with expected networks of relevance to the given outcome. Feature importance analyses also identified distinct predictive signatures across both modality and outcome domain, indicating that eSDC and eFC capture non-redundant, biologically meaningful information about post-stroke network disruption. Together, these findings establish our lesion-based estimates of post-stroke structural and functional connectomes as a practical, information-rich alternative to advanced imaging in patients. This approach allows for probing an individual's affected neural circuitry underlying stroke impairment and recovery, paving the way toward more efficient, accessible, and personalized approaches to post-stroke prognosis and intervention.

title: How Well Does Structural MRI Classify Autism? A Leakage-Free, Site-Aware and Externally Validated Machine-Learning Evaluation in Two ABIDE Cohorts
abstract: Background Many studies report high accuracy for classifying autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from structural MRI, but small samples, single train–test splits, site effects and information leakage can inflate performance. We evaluated how well brain morphometry distinguishes autistic from typically developing (TD) individuals under rigorous, leakage-free validation. Methods FreeSurfer-derived features (n = 280: regional thickness, area and volume; subcortical volumes; Yeo-network composites; asymmetry indices; global measures) from ABIDE II (804 participants; 341 ASD; 12 sites) were used to train logistic regression, linear support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost and multilayer perceptron classifiers. Confound regression (age, age 2 , sex, brain volume), site-wise centring and standardisation were learned within training folds only. Performance was assessed with nested 10-fold cross-validation, leave-one-site-out validation and external validation in ABIDE I (917 participants; 20 sites), and compared with full-pipeline permutation tests and a confound-only baseline. Results Cross-validated discrimination was modest: the best model (regularised logistic regression on all features) reached an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.60 [0.56, 0.64], significantly above chance (permutation p = .002) but far from clinically useful and below a confound-only baseline using age, sex, brain volume and site (AUC 0.63); non-linear models did not perform better (AUC 0.45–0.60 across models and feature sets). Pooled leave-one-site-out AUCs were 0.54–0.61, with large between-site variation, and AUCs in the external ABIDE I cohort were 0.52–0.58. Age-stratified models did not exceed AUC 0.60. Across 300 random 80/20 splits in young adults, test-set AUCs ranged from 0.21 to 0.90, showing that single-split estimates such as 0.74 can arise by chance. Conclusions Under leakage-free, site-aware and externally validated evaluation, structural MRI morphometry classifies autism only slightly better than chance. Reports of high accuracy should be interpreted with caution, and the heterogeneity of autism argues for stratification and normative approaches rather than binary diagnostic classifiers.

title: Strategies of mechanical adaptations of circulating tumor cells and properties of their cellular microenvironment have predictive and prognostic biomarker value
abstract: Mechanically demanding conditions in the blood circulation damage and kill majority of tumor-shed circulating tumor cells (CTCs). Mechanical fitness: a set of mechanical properties detected with atomic force spectroscopy based force spectrometry supports survival of CTCs. We propose that live CTCs isolated from peripheral blood of prostate cancer patients represent distinct strategies of fitness promoting mechanical adaptations to the fluid shear stress. Some of the cells mimicked properties of erythrocytes (high stiffness) or leukocytes (high deformability). The clustering strategy characterized by exceptionally high adhesion is ingenious to CTCs and not found in blood cells. The abundance of CTCs with elevated adhesion has a predictive value for prostate cancer patients starting 1 st round of androgen deprivation therapy. Moreover, a “high adhesion score” based on individual cells’ or average patient-specific adhesion is instrumental to stratify recurrent patients that underwent diagnostic imaging by PSMA-PET/CT and clarify inconclusive PSMA scan results. Including contribution of erythrocyte-like strategy broadened the predictive power of CTC mechanophenotyping. Improved biomarking opportunities to predict early castration resistances were noted when the composition of CTC microenvironment was included alongside the mechanical properties. We demonstrated previously that the CTC microenvironment is formed by large cells co-purifying by microfiltration of the blood of cancer patients. Analysis of the association of particular components of CTC microenvironment with the clustering strategy led to pointing at highly adhesive CTC-EMT. However, in the advanced patients adhesiveness of CTC-EMT was surpassed by tumor hybrid cells (THCs), a distinctive kind of invasive species formed by incomplete phagocytosis of CTCs by macrophages. THCs changed their mechanical phenotype and strategy preference with disease progression pointing at the dynamic nature of adaptations of tumor-shed cells to circulation conditions.

title: 2D U-NET Deep Learning Architecture for Atherosclerotic Lesion Segmentation and Quantification
abstract: Mice are commonly used for experimental atherosclerosis research, and a common procedure involves morphometric analysis of atherosclerotic lesions on Oil Red O-stained cross-sections of the aortic root. However, manual measurement of atherosclerotic lesion sizes on numerous histological sections is tedious and time-consuming. Here, we developed a deep learning model based on convolutional neural network to quantify atherosclerotic lesions in cross-sectioned aortic roots of mice. Microscopy images were taken from cross-sectioned aortic roots of genetically diverse F2 mice derived from BALB/cJ and LP/J Apoe knockout mice and fed 12 weeks of a Western diet. Aortic cross-sections were stained with Oil Red O and hematoxylin and images captured. Atherosclerotic lesions were manually segmented in 2553 images using Zeiss AxioVision. These images were split into 1,533 for training the U-NET model, 510 for validation, and 510 images for testing. The developed model was evaluated for its performance to measure atherosclerotic lesions by comparing with manual measurement in test images. The model achieved a high degree of accuracy, with an F1 score of 0.82, a Jaccard score of 0.72, a Recall of 0.80, a precision of 0.87, and a correlation coefficient value of 0.98. While manual lesion measurement took approximately 5 minutes per image, the model performed the task in ~3.35 seconds, reducing measurement time by 98.9%. The developed 2D U-NET model provides a new platform for rapid and accurate quantification of atherosclerotic lesion sizes on Oil Red O-stained sections.
