title: MaxCAT-Net: Hybrid transformer-based skin lesion classification and lightweight segmentation with calibration and cross-dataset validation
abstract: Class imbalance, poor calibration of confidence and poor generalisation under different imaging conditions are restrictions of automated analysis of dermoscopic skin lesions. We propose a hybrid classifier MaxCAT-Net (MaxViT + CBAM + Attention Transformer), which consists of a pre-trained MaxViT-Tiny backbone and the combination of CBAM and two-layer lightweight Transformer encoder and evaluate four encoder-decoder networks for lesion segmentation as a separate task on ISIC 2018 Task 1. All the images of exact/near duplicate were removed and the remaining 10,012 images were distributed lesion-wise (72/14/14) without two or more images having the same type of lesion in HAM10000. On the test set ( n = 1,405), MaxCAT-Net outperformed the baselines of ResNet152-CBAM, MobileNetV3-CBAM, GhostNet-hybrid and single MaxViT-Tiny-CBAM with an accuracy of 0.869 (95% CI 0.847–0.890), balanced accuracy of 0.742, macro-F1 of 0.751 and macro-AUC of 0.944, although ablation gains in macro-F1 (0.017–0.022) were not statistically conclusive. By scaling the temperature, the ECE was decreased from 0.099 to 0.038. In the case of the PAD-UFES-20 dataset, however, the accuracy fell to 0.341 and the melanoma recall rate to 0.096 while for the HAM10000 dataset, the melanoma recall rate was only 0.587. A Swin-T-encoder U-Net was able to achieve a Dice score of 0.903 in segmentation (520 test images), whereas a FasterNet-T0 U-Net (1/10th of the number of parameters) had a Dice score of 0.901 (Holm adjusted p < 0.002), and a standard U-Net had a significantly lower Dice score of 0.888. All results are based on one seed and show trends—not definite improvement.

title: Deep learning grading of Schistosoma japonicum -associated liver fibrosis from ultrasound images: a weighted soft-voting ensemble of convolutional and transformer networks
abstract: Background Schistosomiasis morbidity still persists in China despite extensive progress towards elimination of new and active infections. Diagnosis of liver fibrosis related to Schistosoma japonicum remains challenging due to the subjective nature of ultrasound grading and the shortage of experienced sonographers in endemic counties. Methods We developed a deep learning model that grades schistosomal liver fibrosis from a single B-mode ultrasound image without manual delineation of a region of interest. We used 2,921 images from 2,921 adults (aged 18–88 years, median age 54 years; 46.4% female) from a schistosomiasis hospital in Jiangxi Province, China, between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 12.9%, 34.6%, 32.4% and 20.2% had grade 0, 1, 2 and 3 fibrosis, respectively. Fibrosis grades were based on the clinical ultrasound record and re-evaluation by an experienced radiologist according to the Chinese Hand-book of Schistosomiasis Control; discordant cases were reviewed by a second radiologist and resolved by consensus. Predictions from four neural networks with different architectures (ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet-121 and Swin-T) were combined by weighted soft voting, with weights derived from validation performance. Results For the four-grade task this model achieved a macro-F1 of 0.8527 (95% CI 0.8184–0.8856), an accuracy of 0.8500 (0.8136–0.8818) and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9187 (0.8983–0.9373) on a fixed test set of 440 images. For detecting significant fibrosis (grade 2 or 3; test-set prevalence 0.530), sensitivity was 0.9700, specificity was 0.9179, positive predictive value was 0.9300, negative predictive value was 0.9645, and AUROC was 0.9817. The ensemble achieved a higher macro-F1 than each individual backbone. Every ensemble misclassification was to an adjacent grade; no image with severe fibrosis was classified as no or mild fibrosis, or vice versa, whereas each individual backbone made 1–4 errors spanning two or more grades. Conclusions The model may provide an automated aid for Schistosoma japonicum -associated fibrosis grading and could potentially support screening and follow-up in endemic areas after external validation.

title: Screening for rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease using lung ultrasound: a systematic review and meta-analysis of recent studies
abstract: Interstitial lung diseases (ILD) associated with systemic autoimmune disease can have a strong negative impact on patient outcomes. The diagnostic gold standard is high-resolution computer tomography (HRCT). Numerous studies have proven lung ultrasound's (LUS) utility in ILD, as well as other lung pathologies. Recently, there has been more focus on ILD in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a previously overlooked complication, and screening methods. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to summarize the recent knowledge regarding LUS compared to HRCT in screening ILD in RA patients. We reviewed relevant literature from the last 10 years and selected 12 articles. We included seven of those (totaling 756 patients) in a meta-analysis of diagnostic markers. The pooled sensitivity of LUS was 0.88 (95% CI 0.82-0.92) and pooled specificity was 0.86 (95% CI 0.71-0.94). The pooled LR+ and LR- were found to be 6.63 (95% CI 2.84-15.47) and 0.13 (95% CI 0.08-0.22), respectively. Diagnostic odds ratio was 48.54 (95% CI 13.78-170.98). LUS has high sensitivity and specificity for screening ILD in RA patients across different techniques and scoring systems.

title: ACCURACY OF COMPRESSED SENSING ACCELERATED 3D-FLAIR IN THE DIAGNOSTIC WORK-UP OF MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AT 1.5 T
abstract: BACKGROUND3D-FLAIR is central to MR-based diagnosis and monitoring of MS, but long acquisition times remain a limitation. OBJECTIVESThis single-center prospective non-inferiority study evaluated whether compressed sensing (CS) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR at 1.5T provides lesion detection comparable to optimized Generalized Autocalibrating Partially Parallel Acquisition (GRAPPA) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR. Optimized CS- and GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-FLAIR sequences were incorporated into MRI examinations in patients with known or suspected MS. The primary endpoint was manual lesion count by two blinded readers using a 10% non-inferiority margin. Secondary endpoints included image quality, SNR, CNR, and automated lesion count and volumetry. RESULTSSixty-eight patients were included (mean age, 40.1{+/-}13.3 years; 61.8% women). CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR reduced acquisition time by 31.8% compared with GRAPPA (4:00 vs 5:52 minutes). Non-inferiority for manual lesion count was demonstrated for both readers (reader A, p < .0001; reader B, p = .005). Interrater agreement was excellent for CS (ICC = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.837-0.957) and very good for GRAPPA (ICC = 0.851; 95% CI, 0.769-0.906). Subjective image quality was high for both techniques. GRAPPA showed higher objective signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise-ratio (CNR), whereas automated lesion counts and volumes were higher for CS. CONCLUSIONCS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR provided non-inferior lesion detection with substantial scan-time reduction.

title: PROSPECTIVE COMPARISON OF OPTIMIZED COMPRESSED SENSING AND GRAPPA-ACCELERATED 3D-TOF-MRA FOR EVALUATION OF UNTREATED INTRACRANIAL ANEURYSMS AT 1.5 T: A NON-INFERIORITY STUDY
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES3D-TOF-MRA is a standard non-invasive method for detecting and monitoring intracranial aneurysms, but long scan times remain a limitation. Compressed sensing (CS) acceleration for intracranial aneurysm evaluation has mainly been studied at 3T. This prospective single-center non-inferiority study compared CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T with GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-TOF-MRA for evaluating untreated intracranial aneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODSSample size was determined via a preliminary retrospective study. 25 patients with 32 untreated aneurysms underwent both CS- (factor 7, 3:04 min) and GRAPPA-accelerated (factor 2, 5:00 min) 3D-TOF, yielding a 38.7% scan-time reduction. Two blinded neuroradiologists assessed overall image quality (primary endpoint) and artifacts, subjective CNR, aneurysm delineation and diameters (secondary endpoints). Non-inferiority was tested via one-sided t-test (prespecified 10% margin); interrater agreement used ICC. RESULTSCS demonstrated non-inferiority to GRAPPA for overall image quality in both readers (p [≤] .023), though interrater agreement was low (ICC 0.241-0.262), reflecting subjective variability. Secondary exploratory analyses showed heterogeneous preferences. ROI-based CNR was lower for CS (median 169.6; IQR, 91.0-226. vs. 278.2; 181.0-366.2). Aneurysm diameter measurements showed excellent interrater agreement for both techniques (CS ICC, 0.899-0.980; GRAPPA ICC, 0.877-0.973; all p < .001). CONCLUSIONCS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T met non-inferiority criteria vs. GRAPPA-TOF for overall image quality, reducing scan time by 38.7% while preserving aneurysm measurement reliability. However, reduced CNR and reader-preference variability important trade-offs. These findings support the use of CS-accelerated-TOF as a time-efficient alternative to GRAPPA-accelerated-TOF in evaluating intracranial aneurysms, though further research on field-strength effects and small aneurysms is warranted.

title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.

title: Pathology foundation-model embeddings reveal a morphological landscape of breast lesions beyond diagnostic categories
abstract: Background Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories and dissect how these embeddings could reflect a pathobiological continuum or sequence associated with tumor development. Methods To model breast lesion categories in continuous morphology space, we established a leakage-controlled, patient-aware workflow using the frozen foundation model Prov-GigaPath and the BReAst Carcinoma Subtyping (BRACS) dataset, a pathologist-annotated hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) breast lesion dataset spanning normal tissue, benign proliferative lesions, atypical lesions, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive carcinoma (IC). Using the BRACS training split, we defined a train-derived principal component analysis (PCA) morphology space. We then performed two complementary analyses: normal-rooted k-nearest-neighbor (kNN)-Dijkstra graph-distance scoring to derive a trajectory-like morphology score without imposing the full ordinal diagnostic sequence; pairwise Energy distance and squared maximum mean discrepancy with a radial-basis-function kernel (RBF-MMD²) to quantify order-free distributional separation among diagnostic categories. Validation and test data were projected into the train-defined reference space to assess reproducibility. Results Prov-GigaPath embeddings defined a train-derived morphology space with category-associated organization. Without imposing the full diagnostic sequence, normal-rooted kNN-Dijkstra graph distances recovered a trajectory-like morphology arrangement from normal/benign to malignant lesions. Order-free Energy distance and RBF-MMD² further supported graded separation among lesion categories. Validation and test datasets preserved the pathological organization. Furthermore, morphological embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma, without requiring additional molecular information. Conclusions Leveraging morphology-based foundation-model embeddings, we defined a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories, allowing nuanced positioning of breast lesions along a pathobiological continuum associated with tumor development. Our approaches pave the way for extracting biologically and clinically relevant information from routine histopathology to guide molecular testing, individualized risk assessment, and cost-efficient clinicopathological decision-making. Highlights Overlapping morphological features challenge breast diagnostic categorization Foundation-model embeddings defined a morphologic state space Embeddings allow nuanced positioning along morphological continua across categories Embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma Latent morphological signals in H&E slides may refine individualized risk assessment

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Links Group-Specific Plasma Proteomics to Regional Structural Neuroimaging in Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology begins years before clinical symptoms, highlighting the need for scalable biomarkers that capture biological changes across the AD continuum. Broader plasma proteomics may capture systemic processes that vary with disease stage, yet their relationship to AD-related brain neurodegeneration remains unclear. We aimed to identify plasma proteomic signatures across cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD and evaluate their neuroanatomical associations. Methods We analyzed 146 plasma analytes from 565 Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) participants (58 CN, 396 MCI, 111 AD). Group-specific proteomic signatures were identified using pairwise classification models with nested 5×5 cross-validation. SHAP quantified feature importance, with the top 15 proteins per comparison being prioritized for MRI association analysis. We analyzed 103 regional structural MRI volumes harmonized across 57 acquisition sites using ComBat. Separate ordinary least squares regression tested protein-MRI associations, adjusting for age, sex, APOE ε4, diagnosis, and intracranial volume, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Results Classification models using proteomic data achieved AUC of 0.956 ± 0.017 for CN vs MCI, 0.963 ± 0.011 for MCI vs. AD, and 0.836 ± 0.085 for CN vs. AD. SHAP identified group-dependent proteomic signatures. No protein-MRI associations survived FDR correction for CN vs. MCI. In MCI vs. AD, higher cortisol was associated with lower left precuneus and superior parietal volumes, while higher osteopontin was associated with lower left paracentral and accumbens volumes. In CN vs. AD, higher vitronectin was associated with lower posterior corpus callosum volume. Conclusion These findings suggest that plasma proteomics capture group-specific systemic biological signals across the AD continuum. Linking ML-prioritized plasma proteins to regional brain structure provides neuroanatomical context for blood-based biomarker discovery.

title: Bundlemorphometry: Spatially Resolved White Matter Bundle Shape Analysis Using Nonlinear Streamline-Based Registration
abstract: ABSTRACT Diffusion MRI tractometry quantifies microstructural properties along white matter (WM) bundles but does not directly measure their geometry, potentially overlooking localized morphological alterations. Here, we introduce BundleMorphometry, a framework for quantifying local WM bundle shape using the analytical Jacobian of nonlinear streamline-based registration. Individual subject bundles are registered to a reference atlas bundle using BundleWarp, a streamline-based nonlinear registration method. We derive the analytical Jacobian of the resulting deformation field and compute its log-determinant (log det J) to quantify local expansion and compression at each streamline point. To enable spatially resolved group comparisons, these measurements are projected onto the two-dimensional grid, capturing variations along and across each bundle. We evaluated BundleMorphometry using two clinical datasets comprising patients with glioma and Parkinson’s disease (PD). In the glioma dataset, BundleMor-phometry revealed spatially extensive deformation patterns in lesion-affected WM bundles that were not captured by displacement magnitude alone. Additionally, in a group analysis of the PD dataset (32 patients and 32 healthy controls), we identified significant localized morphological differences in the corpus callosum forceps major, mid-body and right spinothalamic tract, with distinct patterns of expansion and compression. These findings demonstrate the potential of BundleMorphometry to advance conventional tractometry by enabling spatially resolved analysis of bundle morphology.

title: Generalizable virtual staining from histopathology to spatial proteomics across biological scales
abstract: Large histology archives capture morphological correlates of molecular tissue states but lack direct spatial protein measurements. In this study, we show that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology can provide a queryable, morphology-based representation of spatial protein expression that remains informative from pixels to patients. To achieve this, we developed QUEST, a model framework that represents protein markers as semantic queries for flexible multiplex immunofluorescence (MIF) prediction. Trained on a heterogeneous atlas of paired H&E and MIF images comprising over 10,000 tissue regions, QUEST captured morphological patterns associated with protein markers and reconstructed their expression intensities across diverse tissue types and cohorts. Its utility extended beyond image reconstruction and preserved biologically meaningful information across multiple scales: virtual staining preserved protein marker expression at the cellular and tissue scales, supported cell phenotyping, cellular neighborhood analysis, and characterization of spatial tissue organization, retained clinically relevant signals for patient stratification, and enabled H&E-based queries to retrieve MIF references with similar molecular profiles. These findings position virtual staining not simply as image generation but as a flexible interface between routine histology and spatial proteomics, expanding the analytical value of existing H&E archives.

title: RyR2-Mediated Ca 2+ Leak Drives Progressive Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Abnormal sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca 2+ release through ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) is a well-established mechanism of ventricular arrhythmias. Whether persistent RyR2 dysfunction can also initiate the structural remodeling characteristic of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) remains unknown. We tested the hypothesis that chronic RyR2-mediated Ca 2+ leak is sufficient to couple electrical instability to progressive cardiomyopathy. Methods We generated a rabbit carrying the severe gain-of-function RyR2-V2475F mutation and characterized disease progression using longitudinal cardiac phenotyping, continuous electrocardiographic monitoring, cellular electrophysiology and Ca 2+ imaging, histopathology, biochemical analyses, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Therapeutic potential was evaluated by continuous treatment with the selective RyR2 inhibitor ent -verticilide for two months. Results RyR2-V2475F rabbits developed spontaneous ventricular tachyarrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, and progressive right ventricular (RV)-dominant fibrofatty cardiomyopathy recapitulating major features of human ACM. Malignant ventricular arrhythmias preceded overt structural remodeling and were associated at the cellular level with early spontaneous Ca 2+ release and early afterdepolarizations. Early disease was characterized by remodeling of excitation-contraction coupling with preserved SR Ca 2+ load and contractile function despite RyR2 dysfunction; upon disease progression, these compensatory changes were accompanied by SR Ca 2+ depletion, impaired RV contractility and reduced left ventricular filling. Single-nucleus transcriptomics identified early fibroblast expansion and predicted cardiomyocyte-centered paracrine signaling before advanced fibrofatty infiltration. Cardiomyocytes also exhibited an altered lipid-metabolic transcriptome and intracellular lipid accumulation, accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake. Selective RyR2 inhibition markedly reduced ventricular tachycardia burden and preserved RV contraction and LV filling during disease progression. Conclusions Severe RyR2 gain-of-function can lead to both malignant ventricular arrhythmias and progressive arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy in a large-animal model, establishing persistent intracellular Ca 2+ dysregulation as a mechanistic link between electrical and structural heart disease. The ability of selective RyR2 inhibition to suppress arrhythmias and preserve cardiac function identifies RyR2 as a potentially actionable therapeutic target in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

title: Peripheral immune biomarkers, brain imaging phenotypes and treatment response in major depressive disorder
abstract: Immune dysregulation is implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD), but its links to clinical features and in vivo brain phenotypes remain uncertain. We examined ten plasma biomarkers in 36 unmedicated MDD patients and 48 control participants using high-sensitivity immune profiling at baseline, alongside PET/MR imaging of brain serotonin transporter (SERT) binding and regional structural measures. Patients underwent three months of antidepressant treatment and were followed up with MR imaging. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) was higher in MDD patients (β = 0.66, 95% CI 0.22 - 1.11), and interleukin-33 (IL-33) correlated with subcortical volumes across all participants (β = 0.22, 95% CI 0.07 - 0.38). No marker correlated with SERT binding or cortical thickness after correction, and neither SERT binding nor brain structural measures differed by diagnosis. In the longitudinal analysis, interleukin-13 (IL-13) was associated with greater antidepressant response during first-line treatment with escitalopram (β = 1.09, 95% CI 0.56 - 1.61). IL-15 and IL-13 showed nominal associations with hippocampal volume increase after treatment. These findings support astroglial involvement in MDD and link peripheral immune variation to subcortical brain structure. IL-13 is a candidate prognostic marker of response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Its tentative association with longitudinal changes in hippocampal volume suggests that immune processes in MDD may be related to both the capacity for clinical improvement and brain structural plasticity during treatment.

title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
abstract: Objective: We aimed to 1) evaluate whether AI algorithms could identify a very low-risk sub-population Lung-RADS 1/2 cases suitable for a safe switch to biennial screening, and 2) externally validate Sybil, an imaging-based deep learning lung cancer risk prediction tool. Materials and methods: We gathered all lung cancer screenings (LCSs) from a tertiary safety-net hospital (n=3120, up to September 2024), manually extracted relevant clinical data, and analyzed Sybil's performance across various subgroups, with a specific focus on Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases. We simulated LCS interval extension using Sybil and the Brock model risk scores calibrated on a subset of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). Confidence intervals were obtained through bootstrapping. Results: The median follow-up was 2.3 years (interquartile range 1.5-3.1), with a total 6-year cancer incidence rate of 2.3% (72/3120). Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases comprised 90.5% of our scans. Sybil's overall area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.819 to 0.912; while its 2-year AUC for Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases was 0.746. In the screening interval extension simulation, calibrating for a 30% shift to biennial screening translated into 33.8% of negative screens in our data being safely extended using Sybil, with no delayed cancers. The Brock model demonstrated an AUC of 0.513 on our data, with a sensitivity of 18.2% using the 1.5% threshold. Conclusion: Sybil has the potential to safely extend LCS intervals for low-risk individuals, reducing radiology workload and opening spots for life-saving new screenings.

title: Olfactory Function in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: A Multi-Cohort Study
abstract: Introduction: Olfactory impairment is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, it is unclear if olfactory performance reflects early pathological changes during preclinical AD and/or predicts subsequent clinical progression among characterized cognitively normal (CN) individuals. We aimed to determine whether odor identification differs by amyloid status, relates to medial temporal lobe (MTL) tau burden and morphometry, and predicts longitudinal conversion to mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Methods: We analyzed data from 257 cognitively normal (CN) older adults enrolled in PREVENT-AD (n = 217) and UCLouvain (n = 40), including 76 amyloid-positive (CN A+) and 181 amyloid-negative participants (CN A−). Participants completed olfactory testing, underwent tau-PET imaging, and structural MRI. Results: CN A+ participants had significantly lower odor identification performance than CN A− participants, with no evidence of cohort heterogeneity. Tau-PET associations with odor identification differed by cohort. After whole-brain FDR correction and exclusion of extreme values, parahippocampal tau burden was negatively associated with odor identification score in UCLouvain ([18F]MK-6240), an association that was not found in PREVENT-AD ([18F]flortaucipir). No morphometric association survived multiple comparison correction. In 250 participants with longitudinal follow-up, each 10-percentage-point higher odor identification score was associated with a 16% lower hazard of incident MCI, independent of baseline global cognition and APOE ϵ4-carrier status. Discussion: Odor identification was lower in preclinical AD and associated with incident MCI independently of baseline global cognition and APOE ϵ4-carrier status. Its association with parahippocampal tau burden differed between cohorts, supporting further investigation using harmonized imaging methods.

title: Rapid Detection and Initial Treatment of Life-Threatening Subdural Hematoma in a Sheep Model
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is the leading cause of death and disability in people under 40 worldwide. There is an unmet need for detection and treatment of life-threatening TBI when computed tomography (CT) scanners and neurosurgeons are unavailable. We developed a new handheld frequency-domain multidetector infrared hemorrhage detection device. Using the new device, military pre-hospital medics required <4 minutes to detect life-threatening subdural hematoma in a sheep model. We developed a second device that allows non-neurosurgeons to safely create a burr hole and partially remove clotted subdural blood. In sheep, the treatment device reduced intracranial pressure within 20 minutes, and improved post-anesthesia blinded neurological outcomes. With human use adaptation, these devices could allow rapid detection and initial treatment of some life-threatening TBIs in challenging situations.

title: Late radiation-induced brain injury is associated with functional cerebrovascular impairment without structural vessel loss in mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) is a major and often irreversible complication of cranial radiotherapy, affecting up to 90% of long-term survivors. Although cerebrovascular damage is a leading mechanistic hypothesis, whether chronic resting hypoperfusion occurs independently of structural vessel loss remains unknown. The aim of this study was to comprehensively characterize cerebrovascular, structural, and behavioral outcomes in a murine model of late RIBI to determine the primary drivers of vascular dysfunction. Methods Adult C57BL/6 mice underwent 12 Gy whole-brain irradiation and were assessed one year later using laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI), 7T MRI, immunohistochemistry, and behavioral testing. Results Irradiated mice exhibited reduced pial flow velocity and flow area by LSCI, indicative of upstream cerebrovascular dysfunction, while bulk cortical tissue perfusion was preserved. This pial hypoperfusion was accompanied by cerebral atrophy, decreased T2* relaxation time and tissue iron deposition consistent with chronic microhemorrhage across multiple brain regions by MRI, blood-brain barrier disruption reflected by reduced ZO-1 and VE-cadherin expression, and increased anxiety-like behavior. Strikingly, capillary density, pericyte coverage, astrocyte endfeet, and NeuN-positive neuronal nuclei were all preserved. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that functional vascular impairment - not structural vessel or neuronal loss - drives hypoperfusion and blood-brain barrier disruption in late RIBI. This dissociation between vascular dysfunction and rarefaction reframes the pathophysiology of RIBI and identifies endothelial dysfunction as a tractable therapeutic target for intervention.

title: Cortical Thinning in Adults with Prader–Willi Syndrome: Distribution Across Functional Networks and Associations with BMI and the GH/IGF-1 Axis
abstract: Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare neurogenetic disorder associated with neuropsychiatric, metabolic, endocrine, and physical abnormalities. Although previous neuroimaging studies have identified regional gray matter alterations, cortical thickness (CT) abnormalities and their distribution across large-scale functional brain networks remain poorly characterized in adults with PWS. We investigated cortical morphology in 23 adults with PWS and 22 age- and sex-matched healthy controls who underwent structural MRI. Cortical reconstruction and surface-based morphometric analyses were performed using FreeSurfer. Between-group differences in CT were assessed using age, sex, and intracranial volume as covariates. Associations between CT and clinical, cognitive, anthropometric, and endocrine measures were examined using Spearman correlations. Significant cortical regions were further mapped onto an a priori functional network atlas. Adults with PWS showed reduced CT in a left-hemispheric cluster involving the inferior precentral gyrus, insula, inferior temporal cortex, and orbitofrontal cortex. This cluster overlapped predominantly with the somatomotor, auditory, cingulo-opercular, language, and frontoparietal networks. Within the PWS group, lower CT was associated with higher body mass index and poorer global functioning. CT was positively associated with IGF-1 levels and was greater in participants with a history of growth hormone therapy during childhood. These findings indicate cortical thinning across regions belonging to multiple functional networks involved in sensorimotor, attentional, language, and executive processes, extending previous volumetric findings. The associations with body mass index, functional measures, and the GH/IGF-1 axis suggest that cortical morphology may reflect an interplay between genetic vulnerability and potentially modifiable metabolic and endocrine factors, raising the possibility of a neuroprotective role for GH/IGF-1 signaling.

title: Statistical design of Path to Prevention platform trial in early neuronal alpha-synuclein disease
abstract: The Path to Prevention (P2P) platform trial is a first-in-class, phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled learning study. Its design expedites the assessment of investigational therapies for the treatment of early-stage Neuronal a-Synuclein Disease (NSD), a biological disease continuum that encompasses and often precedes clinically manifest Parkinson's Disease. P2P is embedded within the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a robust observational longitudinal cohort study on Parkinson's disease progression and a trial-facilitating enrollment framework. A regimen, comprised of an active investigational therapy and a matched placebo control, evaluates a therapeutic candidate within the P2P perpetual platform framework. Multiple regimens can be enrolled, enabling efficient testing of multiple therapeutics. A two-stage randomization scheme determines regimen sample size with 125 participants assigned to a regimen's active therapy and a variable number to placebo control. The treated follow up period is a minimum of 96 weeks and a maximum of 144 weeks, with the last randomized participant followed for 96 weeks. As a pioneering interventional trial in early-stage NSD, P2P endpoint selection was critically informed by modeling and analysis of available PPMI data. In P2P, regimens will be evaluated for efficacy using two primary endpoints: 1) a biomarker outcome of Dopamine Transporter Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (DAT SPECT) imaging measured by the bilateral putamen Specific Binding Ratio (SBR) and 2) a clinical outcome measured by the Movement Disorder Society-Sponsored Revision of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) Part III score. Each endpoint will be assessed separately using a longitudinal Bayesian mixed effects model, which compares the active treatment group to the shared placebo control group. The model uses regimen-specific controls at full weight and dynamically discounts controls from other regimens. Additionally, placebo control estimates are supplemented by non-randomized control data from the PPMI cohort. Clinical trial simulations, informed by longitudinal data from 275 P2P-eligible PPMI study participants (Age 60-81, 35% Female, 65% Male), were conducted to evaluate the design. Each regimen is well-powered to detect a 40% slowing in progression for both the clinical and biomarker primary endpoints when comparing active treatment to randomized control data. Supplementing the control estimation with non-randomized, P2P-eligible registry participant data increases power in the explored scenarios up to 4% for each endpoint. The embedded P2P platform trial is a powerful learning study that leverages statistical efficiencies from the platform trial design and established PPMI infrastructure and is poised to advance treatment development in early-stage NSD.

title: Personalized Prediction of Differences in fMRI Connectivity Estimates Across Preprocessing Pipelines
abstract: Longitudinal functional MRI of the human brain is valuable for tracking changes in functional connectivity (FC) associated with disease progression or treatment response. Even so, measured FC values depend on preprocessing, and nuisance regression and temporal filtering affect individuals differently. We examined whether we could use earlier scans to predict how preprocessing would affect a later scan. In 69 ADNI (Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) participants scanned three times, we measured how nuisance regression and filtering, alone and in sequence, changed the measured FC. A ridge regression model combined these responses with baseline FC from the third scan to predict the effect of reversing the processing order. Just four coefficients were shared across 79,800 connections. In leave-one-participant-out testing, mean squared error was 0.012, compared with 0.017 for predicting the same average response for everyone. It outperformed the best of seven alternative predictions chosen for each participant (0.013; normalized gain 0.069, 95% bootstrap interval 0.006–0.134), with lower error in 44 of 69 participants. About half the benefit of using each person’s earlier responses, rather than the average across participants, came from which connections changed. This advantage persisted after accounting for acquisition variables. The ADNI-trained model reduced mean error in ten Midnight Scan Club participants without refitting. These results support using personal preprocessing history to predict changes in connectivity estimates on newly acquired scans.

title: Cross-cancer knowledge transfer for lymph node metastasis prediction: Applicability of an axillary lymph node-based deep learning model
abstract: Evaluation of lymph node (LN) metastasis is critical for cancer staging and treatment planning. Since radiologic hallmarks of metastatic LNs are shared across primary cancers, a computed tomography (CT)-based deep learning (DL) classifier developed from one anatomy may transfer to others. This study built a DenseNet-121 ensemble model using clinical-implication-applied preprocessing and evaluated its cross-anatomical generalizability to LNs from diverse primary cancers. A DenseNet-121 ensemble model combining fixed-size cropping (FSC) and adjustable square cropping (ASC) was trained from ImageNet initialization on an axillary lymph node (ALN) dataset (n = 1,128 from 523 breast cancer patients). The model utilized clinical-implication-applied perinodal cropping with bicubic filtering and standardized resizing. To test cross-anatomical generalizability, an external dataset of 256 CT images across four anatomical regions was evaluated: cervical, mediastinal, upper-abdominal, and lower-abdominal LNs. Perinodal free margins were systematically varied from 10% to 40% to optimize the balance between context preservation and surround interference. Bicubic filtering and standardized resizing yielded the highest internal performance on the original ALN dataset (FSC-ASC ensemble area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.958, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.920–0.987 at 40% margin). The model demonstrated site-dependent, above-chance generalizability across all external regions. Cervical LNs achieved the highest performance at a 40% margin (AUROC 0.939, 95% CI 0.875–0.989). Mediastinal LNs peaked at a 10% margin (AUROC 0.796, 95% CI 0.672–0.903), with wider margins degrading performance due to adjacent structural interference. Upper-abdominal and lower-abdominal LNs reached optimal performance at a 30% margin (AUROC 0.814 for upper; AUROC 0.917 for lower). A single ALN-trained DL model can accurately predict LN metastasis across cervical, mediastinal, and abdominal stations through site-specific perinodal margin tuning. These findings support the feasibility of cross-cancer knowledge transfer and the clinical utility of generalizable backbones for pan-cancer nodal assessment.

title: Disability-relevant demyelination in multiple sclerosis: five-year evolution following diagnosis
abstract: Improved understanding of how myelin damage contributes to disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) is needed to inform targeted therapeutic strategies and improve clinical trial platforms. Magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) and T1 relaxometry provide in vivo quantitative MRI measures of myelin integrity, and may offer insights into disability-relevant pathology beyond inflammatory relapse. This longitudinal study explores the relationship between early demyelination and disability progression over the first five years following diagnosis. 62 people with relapsing-remitting (pwRR)MS ([≤] 6 months post-diagnosis, 48 female, mean age 38 years) underwent baseline and one-year MRI and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) assessment. At five-year follow-up, 56/62 (90.3%) completed EDSS and 40/62 additionally completed MRI (64.5%). Disability progression was defined as an increase of [≥] 1.5, [≥] 1.0 or [≥] 0.5 points for a previous EDSS score of < 1.0, 1.0 to 5.5, and [≥] 6.0, respectively. Baseline neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and EBNA1 immunoglobulin (IgG) titres were also measured. MTsat was calculated within normal-appearing white matter (NAWM), white matter lesions (WML), cortical and deep grey matter (GM) structures. Associations between change in MTsat and disability progression were assessed with binomial logistic regression. Interactions with interval disease activity (i.e. new/enlarging lesions [NELs]) were investigated, and comparisons were made with healthy control test-retest data (n = 11). Exploratory analyses were performed for: (prolonged) T1; baseline metrics; blood-derived markers; diffusion-weighted imaging; and, disability-associated differences in five-year microstructural MRI trajectories. Greater baseline-to-one-year decreases in NAWM and WML MTsat were associated with baseline-to-one-year disability progression (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 0.255 [0.078 to 0.602] and 0.261 [0.084 to 0.638]; false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected p-value = 0.015 and 0.015). NELs did not influence these associations (interaction p-values > 0.05). One-to-five-year changes in MTsat were not associated with one-to-five-year disability progression (FDR-corrected p-values > 0.05). Neither baseline nor baseline-to-one-year MTsat changes predicted future disability progression. No exploratory analyses reached FDR-corrected statistical significance. We show for the first time that progressive NAWM and WML demyelination measured with MTsat is associated with early disability progression in recently diagnosed RRMS, independent of radiological inflammatory disease activity. Neither MTsat nor T1 are associated with longer-term progression over the subsequent four years. MTsat is sensitive to disability-relevant demyelination not visible on conventional MRI, indicates a potential early window of therapeutic opportunity in the year following diagnosis, and is a promising clinically applicable disease stratifier and surrogate endpoint for therapeutic trials.

title: Agentic AI enables cell segmentation-free cell-type inference and cell-type-guided cell segmentation in spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Cell-type identification in spatial transcriptomics often relies on cell segmentation, which can introduce inaccuracies in cell boundaries and transcript assignment. Segmentation-free or cell-free methods have been developed to completely avoid cell segmentation, but inaccurate cell typing hinder accurate downstream analysis. Here, we introduce SSAF-T, a segmentation-free agentic framework that identifies cell types directly from spatial gene expression without predefined reference datasets. For the reference-free cell typing, SSAF-T incorporates CeLLMan, which employs expert-level agents for each organ to annotate cell types using a literature-grounded knowledge graph. We benchmark SSAF-T on both array-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics datasets in terms of accuracy, reproducibility, and scalability. We further show that SSAF-T provides an accurate cell segmentation based on the segmentation-free mapping, which ensure compatibility to existing downstream analysis ecosystem, and eventually enable quantitative analysis at single-cell level.

title: Computational Modeling of the Acoustic Radiation Force and Viscoelastic Displacement for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation
abstract: Objective: In transcranial ultrasound neuromodulation (TUS), simulations of the harmonic pressure are often used for treatment planning. However, other mechanisms of energy transfer, such as acoustic radiation force (ARF) and the resulting tissue displacement, are reported less frequently. Furthermore, there is limited guidance on how these mechanisms should be simulated. This study evaluates the numerical convergence and accuracy of different ARF formulations and investigates the simulation of ultrasound-induced tissue displacement in the context of TUS. Approach: Two simulations steps are used in k-Wave to first simulate the first order acoustic pressure and velocity fields. Subsequently, these fields are used to calculate the ARF using the momentum-flux density tensor, Reynolds stress force, and attenuation force formulations. The ARF is then applied as input for a second viscoelastic simulation to estimate the tissue displacement induced by the ultrasound field. Numerical accuracy and convergence are quantified as functions of the various numerical choices and hyperparameters in the solvers. Main results: Among the investigated formulations, the attenuation-force approach proved to be the most robust and the least susceptible to numerical errors across variable medium types and transducer geometries. Within the parameter space relevant to TUS, it is a valid approximation of the momentum flux density tensor formulation. Similar tissue displacement distributions are found across the different ARF formulations. However, the accuracy of the displacement simulation decreases with increasing pulse duration. Finally, recommendations are formulated on the ARF calculation method and on the numerical hyperparameters for ARF and displacement simulations. Significance: This study offers guidelines for calculating the ARF and simulating tissue displacement. The proposed framework enables a more comprehensive characterization of ultrasound-mediated energy transfer in TUS.

title: Identification of Kinome Biomarkers and Therapeutic Rescue in cGMP-Linked Retinal Degeneration
abstract: Inherited retinal degenerations, such as Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) and Leber's congenital amaurosis (LCA), are major causes of progressive and irreversible vision loss. The large number of genes associated with these disorders makes their clinical and molecular characterization difficult, while systemic biomarkers for disease progression or treatment response remain limited. These challenges were addressed by targeting cGMP-associated mechanisms shared by RP and LCA and integrating systemic biomarker profiling with retinal outcomes. Kinase activity analysis (kinome analysis) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells distinguished healthy and diseased states and captured therapy-associated signatures in rd10 mice treated with LP-CN03, a liposomal formulation of the cGMP analog CN03. This first systemic analysis in a therapeutically responsive animal model highlights kinome analysis as a potential translational readout. Given shared cGMP signaling in RP and AIPL1 -associated LCA, LP-CN03's therapeutic potential was further evaluated in a new CRISPR-Cas9-generated Aipl1 -/- mouse model. Treatment with LP-CN03 preserved retinal structure and function, as shown by electroretinography, longitudinal optical coherence tomography, fundus imaging, optomotor testing, and photoreceptor-specific gene expression. Together, these findings provide independent in vivo evidence for the neuroprotective effect of LP-CN03 in both cGMP-related RP and LCA, also highlighting the translational value of kinome profiling.

title: [MRI of suspected bone and soft tissue sarcomas - an overview].
abstract: Sarcomas are rare malignant tumors of connective and supportive tissues, associated with relatively poor five-year survival. According to Swedish patient care bundles ("standardiserat vårdförlopp"), MRI should be performed at local radiology departments before a possible referral to a sarcoma center when there is a strong suspicion of a soft tissue sarcoma, highlighting the need for adequate knowledge of appopriate MRI protocols. For soft tissue lesions, MRI is diagnostic only for a few entities, such as simple lipomas. Most muskuloskeletal tumors, however, require biopsy for definitive diagnosis. Consequently, MRI is primarily used to assess tumor extent prior to biopsy and potential surgery. The Swedish Society of Musculoskeletal Radiology (SFMSR) recommends that an MRI protocol for musculoskeletal tumors should always consist of at least the following three sequences: coronal STIR FSE, axial T1-weighted FSE, and axial T2-weighted FSE. Coronal STIR is mainly used for tumor detection and evaluation of lipomatous lesions. Axial T1 is primarily used to assess intraosseous tumor extent and characterize lipomatous lesions. Axial T2 is primarily used to evaluate soft tissue tumor extension and extraosseous components of bone tumors.

title: Presacral Myelolipoma Mimicking Liposarcoma Complicated by Massive Intraoperative Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
abstract: Myelolipoma is a benign tumor composed of mature adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements. Extra-adrenal lesions can occur in the presacral region and may mimic liposarcoma. Resection of a large presacral tumor can also cause life-threatening hemorrhage. We report a presacral myelolipoma that was difficult to diagnose preoperatively and was complicated by massive intraoperative hemorrhage. A 71-year-old woman had an incidentally detected 75 × 75 × 125-mm presacral mass with mixed fatty and solid components on contrast-enhanced CT. MRI showed restricted diffusion, and fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT showed mild uptake (maximum standardized uptake value, 3.93). No growth occurred over approximately 3 months. Because liposarcoma could not be excluded, the patient chose open resection without biopsy for diagnosis and treatment. During cranial dissection along the anterior sacrum, massive bleeding occurred from the right internal iliac venous system, and systolic blood pressure decreased to 50-60 mmHg. Manual compression was insufficient, and massive transfusion was initiated. Intraoperatively, a vein communicating with the right internal iliac vein was found to enter the tumor, and the main trunk of the right internal iliac vein was ligated near its junction with the right common iliac vein. Persistent bleeding required ligation of a tumor-entering branch of the right internal iliac artery; the arterial main trunk was preserved. Hemostasis was prioritized, and the tumor was removed in 2 pieces; the capsule was disrupted without macroscopic tumor spillage. Diffuse presacral venous plexus bleeding was controlled with electrocautery and oxidized cellulose. Operative time was 3 h 21 min, and blood loss was 4850 mL; 10 units of leukocyte-reduced red blood cells and 6 units of fresh frozen plasma were transfused. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of myelolipoma. No vascular complications occurred, and contrast-enhanced CT at approximately 1 year showed no residual or recurrent tumor. Presacral myelolipoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of fat-containing presacral tumors. In large tumors, the relationship with the internal iliac vessels and presacral venous plexus should be carefully assessed, and adequate blood products, early vascular control, and source-specific hemostatic techniques should be prepared before resection.

title: Emergency Resection for Perforated Small Bowel Metastasis from Primary Lung Cancer During Systemic Therapy: A Case Report.
abstract: Small bowel metastases from lung cancer may remain clinically occult until serious complications, including obstruction, bleeding, and perforation, occur. We report a case of perforated jejunal metastasis with a synchronous ileal metastasis at high risk of obstruction, identified during emergency surgery while several previously documented extraintestinal lesions had decreased in size. A 75-year-old woman with metastatic non-small cell lung carcinoma favoring adenocarcinoma had a programmed death-ligand 1 tumor proportion score of 95% and no targetable alteration on the companion-diagnostic panel. Pembrolizumab monotherapy (200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks) was administered for 4 cycles; no antiangiogenic agent had been administered concurrently or previously. Eleven days after the 4th dose, she developed acute abdominal pain. CT showed focal small bowel wall thickening, adjacent extraluminal air, diffuse bowel edema, and ascites. Emergency surgery revealed a perforated jejunal tumor approximately 20 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz. Systematic examination of the entire small bowel identified a 2nd, nearly circumferential ileal tumor approximately 15 cm proximal to the terminal ileum with marked luminal narrowing; both lesions were resected. Histopathological examination showed metastatic poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of pulmonary origin. Neither tumor necrosis nor a histological treatment effect was identified, and the non-neoplastic mucosa showed no findings suggestive of immune checkpoint inhibitor-related enteritis. The patient was discharged on POD 19. Pembrolizumab was not resumed. PET-CT on POD 30 demonstrated widespread disease progression, and the patient transitioned to best supportive care. She died on POD 61 without recurrent gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding. Clinically occult small bowel metastases may present with perforation or impending obstruction during systemic therapy even while previously documented lesions at other sites decrease in size. Because the intestinal lesions were not identifiable before treatment, true discordant progression could not be established. Histopathological findings supported direct tumor-related perforation rather than treatment-induced tumor necrosis or immune-mediated enteritis. Emergency source control and systematic examination of the entire small bowel may identify additional lesions that alter operative management.

title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Interpretation in Diagnostic Radiology: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy and Operational Efficiency.
abstract: Rising imaging workload and a shortage of radiology specialists have driven interest in artificial intelligence (AI) to improve diagnostic speed and accuracy. This systematic review, without meta-analysis, describes how AI affects diagnostic accuracy and operational efficiency compared with human interpretation in diagnostic radiology. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) and Cochrane guidance, PubMed, ClinicalKey, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched on 11 April 2026 for studies published from January 2019 onwards. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and a Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2)-based risk-of-bias assessment. Twenty-one studies were included: 11 compared standalone AI with human readers, six compared AI-assisted with unassisted readers, and four reported both; 18 evaluated task-specific image-analysis AI and three evaluated generative AI models. Because no subgroup was homogeneous enough to pool, we synthesised results narratively and stratified them by comparison type, AI category, imaging modality, and study quality. Standalone image-analysis AI achieved high sensitivity for fractures and selected chest findings but performed less well on subtle findings and lower-quality images, and in one computed tomography-referenced comparison a radiologist outperformed AI. AI assistance improved reader performance more consistently, particularly among less experienced readers. Generative models did not reach specialist performance on complex tasks. Efficiency gains were concentrated in normal studies, and the only randomised trial found lower mammography screen-reading workload with similar early screening performance. No study assessed patient outcomes, and 18 of 21 studies were retrospective. This evidence supports AI only as a supervised, complementary tool; improvements in diagnostic accuracy should not be equated with clinical benefit.

title: From Spiradenocarcinoma to Spiradenoma: A Case of Histopathological Diagnostic Reclassification.
abstract: Spiradenocarcinoma is a rare malignant cutaneous adnexal neoplasm that may arise from a preexisting spiradenoma. Distinguishing benign from malignant lesions can be challenging, and diagnostic classification has important implications for treatment and follow-up. A 37-year-old woman presented with an approximately 3-cm erythematous-violaceous nodule on the right ankle that had been present for five years and had recently grown rapidly. The initial histopathological assessment described a malignant epithelial neoplasm compatible with spiradenocarcinoma associated with a benign spiradenoma component. The patient underwent wider surgical re-excision with clinical margins exceeding 1 cm, and computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no metastatic disease. No residual neoplasm was identified in the re-excision specimen. Subsequent review of the original histological slides at a second laboratory identified a well-circumscribed, lobulated, solid-cystic dermal lesion with two distinct epithelial cell populations and an interspersed lymphocytic infiltrate, without infiltrative growth, nuclear atypia, mitotic activity, or necrosis in the reviewed material. The diagnosis was revised to benign spiradenoma. Immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of an eccrine neoplasm. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing spiradenoma from spiradenocarcinoma and the clinical implications of discrepant histopathological assessments. Morphological evaluation remains central to classification, while immunohistochemistry provides complementary information.

title: Beyond Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Narrative Review of the Radiological and Endoscopic Features of Solid Pancreatic Neoplasms.
abstract: Solid pancreatic neoplasms comprise a heterogeneous group of tumors with distinct histopathological characteristics, biological behaviors, and therapeutic implications. Although pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the predominant malignancy, non-ductal neoplasms, including pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (PACC), pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs), solid pseudopapillary neoplasms (SPNs), and pancreatoblastoma, represent important diagnostic alternatives. This narrative review aims to summarize and compare the radiological and endoscopic features of solid pancreatic neoplasms, emphasizing their differential diagnosis and the contribution of endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided tissue acquisition to diagnostic characterization. A narrative review of the literature was conducted, focusing on studies addressing CT, MRI, conventional and contrast-enhanced EUS, elastography, and EUS-guided tissue acquisition in the characterization and differential diagnosis of solid pancreatic tumors. PDAC typically demonstrates infiltrative growth and reduced enhancement, whereas non-ductal neoplasms may exhibit well-defined margins and variable vascular patterns. PACC may present as a well-circumscribed mass with heterogeneous enhancement and areas of cystic degeneration, while PanNETs frequently demonstrate hypervascularity, and SPNs often exhibit mixed solid and cystic components. However, substantial imaging overlap limits reliable histological differentiation. Beyond the morphological and vascular characterization provided by EUS, EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB), combined with histological and immunohistochemical analysis, plays a crucial role in establishing a definitive diagnosis, particularly for uncommon neoplasms. Emerging technologies, including radiomics and artificial intelligence (AI), offer promising opportunities for improving diagnostic characterization. Accurate differentiation of solid pancreatic neoplasms requires an integrated approach combining cross-sectional imaging, EUS, and histopathological assessment. Recognizing characteristic imaging patterns and understanding their limitations may improve diagnostic accuracy and guide appropriate tissue acquisition and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Laterality Disorder Associated With NME7 Variants.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital laterality disorder characterized by a mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Although isolated SIT is generally associated with a favorable prognosis, prenatal diagnosis requires careful evaluation to exclude associated structural malformations and syndromic presentations, as well as genetic investigation to identify a possible underlying etiology and improve prognostic assessment. The genetic basis of SIT is complex and remains incompletely understood. To date, genotype-phenotype correlations for SIT-associated genetic variants remain poorly established. We report the prenatal and postnatal clinical course of a fetus with isolated SIT carrying a homozygous intragenic deletion of the NME7 gene, identified by whole-exome sequencing. A primigravida woman was referred at 22 + 2 weeks of gestation after dextrocardia was identified during the second-trimester morphology scan. Detailed ultrasound and fetal echocardiography were performed to assess organ laterality and exclude associated structural abnormalities. An invasive diagnostic procedure (amniocentesis) was performed, including chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) and trio whole-exome sequencing. Ultrasound confirmed isolated SIT, characterized by dextrocardia, a right-sided stomach, and a left-sided liver and gallbladder. Echocardiography revealed normal cardiac anatomy and function. CMA identified a maternally inherited Xp22.33 deletion encompassing the entire SHOX gene, which was detected in the mother but not in the father and was considered an incidental finding. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous, likely pathogenic intragenic deletion involving exons 2-7 of the NME7 gene. Targeted parental DNA analysis confirmed that both parents were heterozygous carriers of the deletion. The pregnancy was continued based on the present molecular findings, since the implication of NME7 variants seemed to be responsible for a non-syndromic form of SIT. A healthy female infant was delivered at term. Postnatal evaluation confirmed SIT with a small atrial septal defect with no hemodynamic impact and no other associated anomalies. This case highlights the additional diagnostic value of whole-exome sequencing in fetuses with apparently isolated laterality abnormalities. It adds to the currently limited evidence linking NME7 variants to isolated SIT. This case also emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary assessment and genetic counseling to optimize diagnosis, prognostic evaluation, parental counseling, and postnatal management.

title: [Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoid with Multiple Distant Metastases Treated with Primary Tumor Resection].
abstract: A 73-year-old man presented with cough and was found to have a tumor in the right lower lobe associated with obstructive pneumonia. Chest computed tomography (CT) and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography revealed multiple distant metastases involving the liver, lymph nodes, and bone. Bronchoscopic biopsy suggested typical pulmonary carcinoid. Although curative resection was not feasible, primary tumor resection was performed to achieve local control and prevent recurrent obstructive pneumonia. Histopathological examination demonstrated atypical pulmonary carcinoid. The patient subsequently received carboplatin plus etoposide, followed by everolimus and a somatostatin analogue after disease progression. Local control was achieved, and the patient's general condition has been maintained despite slow progression of liver metastases. This case suggests that primary tumor resection may be a useful treatment option in selected patients with metastatic atypical pulmonary carcinoid.

title: [Mediastinal Hodgkin Lymphoma with Technical Difficulty in Thoracoscopic Biopsy:Report of a Case].
abstract: A woman in her twenties was referred for evaluation of an abnormal chest radiograph. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a solid mass anterior to the trachea, and positron emission tomography (PET) demonstrated heterogeneous uptake, raising suspicion of malignant lymphoma. Thoracoscopic biopsy was performed, but the mass was rubbery-hard due to fibrosis and resistant to dissection, making tissue sampling difficult. Three intraoperative frozen sections showed predominantly fibrous tissue, and no definitive diagnosis was reached. Histopathological examination of formalin-fixed specimens revealed cellular components in only one section, leading to a final diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Biopsy in Hodgkin lymphoma can be challenging due to extensive fibrosis, occasionally resulting in non-diagnostic samples. A thorough evaluation of preoperative tissue sampling methods is required.
